surveyed the entire ocean-like assembly and then spoke these verses:
In the vast lands adorned by the Buddha, as numerous as all the atoms of the universe,
pure sons of the Buddha completely fill them; they rain down inconceivable and most wondrous Dharma,
just as one sees the Buddha seated in this assembly, so it is in every atom.
The Buddha’s body neither goes nor comes, yet all lands are clearly manifested therein;
It displays the practices cultivated by Bodhisattvas, the infinite stages, paths, and skillful means,
As well as the inconceivable, true principle, causing all sons of the Buddhas to enter the Dharma-realm.
He manifests transformation-buddhas as numerous as motes of dust, universally responding to the desires of the hearts of all sentient beings.
He enters the gates of skillful means within the profound Dharma-realm, extensively expounding them in their vastness and boundlessness.
The names of the Tathāgatas are equal to the world, pervading all lands throughout the ten directions.
Every skillful means is never in vain; Taming sentient beings, all are freed from defilement.
Within every single atom, the Buddha Manifests boundless great supernormal powers;
Seated at every site of enlightenment, he can expound The Buddha’s own past practices for awakening.
Throughout all vast eons of the three periods of time, the Buddha manifests within every single thought-moment all the events of their formation and destruction;
with inconceivable wisdom, there is nothing he does not know.
The assembly of his sons is vast and limitless; those who wish to fathom the stages of the Buddhas [will find it impossible].
The Dharma-gates of all Buddhas are boundless; To fully comprehend them is exceedingly difficult.
The Buddha is like space, free from discrimination; Equal to the true Dharma-realm, he has no dependence.
His emanations travel everywhere without exception, All sitting at the site of enlightenment to achieve perfect awakening.
The Buddha, with his wondrous voice, extensively proclaims and elucidates it, so that all stages (*bhūmi*) are clearly understood.
He manifests universally before each and every being, bestowing upon them all the Dharma equal to that of the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Pure Virtue Wondrous Light attained the power to travel everywhere to the assemblies of bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions.

The liberation door of adorning the site of enlightenment; the liberation door of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Attainment of the Light of the Most Victorious Lamp, who manifests the gate of attaining perfect awakening in a single thought-moment to teach and mature inconceivable realms of sentient beings;
and the liberation door of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Radiance Lion Banner, who has attained the cultivation of the bodhisattva’s merit.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Adornment Born from All Buddha-Lands attained the liberation door of manifesting all Buddha-lands.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Jewel Flame Subtle Light attained the liberation door of observing the realm of the Buddhas' supernormal powers without confusion.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Sound Merit-Ocean Banner attained the [liberation door] of manifesting all Buddhas within a single assembly at a site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Earth Adornment attained the liberation door of the adornment of the earth.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Wisdom Light-Illumination Tathāgata-Sphere attained the liberation door of following and observing the profound and vast treasury of the dharma-realm of the Tathāgatas.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Awakening Pleasing Sound attained the liberation door of the treasury of offerings for attending upon and serving all Buddhas.
In the past, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Pure and Boundless Merit and Majestic Radiance attained the liberation door of the vast empowerment that gives birth to all spiritual transformations.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Jewel Topknot Flower Banner attained the liberation door of universally entering the practices of all worlds to give birth to the boundless practices of a bodhisattva. The Bodhisattva Universal Mark Most Supreme...
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Prabhā obtained the liberation door of being able to manifest all Buddha-realms within the signless dharma-realm.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Viśuddhaguṇasuprabhā, receiving the Buddha’s awesome power, [spoke].
Having universally observed the ocean of liberation gates of all bodhisattvas, he then spoke these verses:
All lands throughout the ten directions, Are entirely purified in a single instant;
Turning the wheel of Dharma with wondrous sounds, They pervade the world, peerless and unequaled.
The realm of the Tathāgata is boundless; in a single thought-moment, it completely fills the entire dharma-realm.
Within every single atom, he establishes sites of enlightenment and fully realizes bodhi, manifesting miraculous transformations.
World-Honored One, in the past you cultivated all practices throughout hundreds of thousands of immeasurable kalpas.
All Buddha-fields are adorned, appearing unimpeded like space;
The Buddha’s power of spiritual penetrations is immeasurable, Filling all infinite eons.
Even if one were to pass through immeasurable eons, Examining them moment by moment without weariness, [one would never reach their end].
You should contemplate the realm of the Buddha’s supernormal powers:
The lands of the ten directions are all adorned and purified, All of which appear here before you, In infinite varieties, differing from moment to moment.
Even after contemplating the Buddha for hundreds of thousands of immeasurable eons, One cannot grasp even the limit of a single pore.
The Tathāgata’s gate of unimpeded skillful means— this light shines universally upon inconceivable lands.
Having served oceans of boundless Buddhas throughout past kalpas while dwelling in the world,
all now rush together like rivers toward the sea, coming to make offerings to the World-Honored One.
The Tathāgata appears throughout the ten directions;
within each and every atom are infinite lands, and the realms therein are all immeasurable, abiding through boundless and inexhaustible eons.
In past ages, for the sake of sentient beings, the Buddha cultivated an ocean of boundless great compassion.
Following all sentient beings into the cycle of birth and death, you universally transform the assemblies to bring them to purity.
The Buddha abides in the treasury of the *tathatā* dharma-realm;
signless and formless, free from all defilements, sentient beings perceive his various bodies, and all their sufferings and hardships are utterly extinguished.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaraprabhāmahāvyūha attained the liberation door of skillful means for giving birth to the various stages and perfections of a bodhisattva,
for teaching and transforming sentient beings, and for adorning and purifying all buddha-lands.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Cloud-Sound Ocean-Light Free-from-Dust-Treasury attained the liberation door of universally entering the various differentiated locations within the Dharma-realm in every moment of thought.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Wisdom-Born Jewel-Crest attained the liberation door of manifesting pure great merit before all sentient beings throughout inconceivable eons. [Merit]...

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sovereign King Pure Light attained the liberation door of universally beholding the various adornments when all Bodhisattvas first arrive at the site of enlightenment in the ten directions.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Good Valor Lotus Topknot attained the liberation door of universally manifesting all Buddha-dharmas in accordance with the ocean of faculties and understandings of all sentient beings.
The gate: The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Wisdom Cloud Sun Banner attained the liberation door of accomplishing the Tathāgata’s wisdom and abiding forever for immeasurable eons.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Great Vigor Vajra Navel attained the liberation door of the power of the seal of universal entry into all boundless dharmas.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Fragrant Flame Light Banner attained the [liberation door] of manifesting...

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Manifesting All Buddhas from Their Initial Cultivation of the Bodhisattva Path until the Attainment of the Accumulation of Wisdom attained the liberation door of the profound and beautiful voice of great brilliance.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Great Merit Light Wisdom-Born attained the liberation door of abiding securely in the ocean of all the great vows of Vairocana.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Displaying... [attained... the liberation door of manifesting... [the ocean of all the great vows of Vairocana].
The Gate of Liberation of the Tathāgata’s Profound Realm Pervading the Dharma-Realm. At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ocean-Light Moon Great Radiance,
empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, surveyed the entire ocean of adornments of the assembly of bodhisattvas and spoke these verses:
All the pāramitās and the stages, vast and inconceivable, are all perfectly fulfilled;
immeasurable sentient beings are entirely tamed, and all buddha-fields are adorned and purified.
Just as the Buddha transforms the realms of sentient beings, he fills the lands of the ten directions.
Within a single thought-moment, he turns the wheel of Dharma; Universally responding to the myriad dispositions of beings, there is nowhere it does not reach.
Throughout immeasurable and vast eons, the Buddha universally appears before all sentient beings;
Just as he extensively cultivated and purified his practices in the past, he now reveals to them those same pure realms of conduct.
I behold all ten directions without exception, seeing all Buddhas manifesting supernatural powers,
seated at their sites of enlightenment and attaining perfect awakening; surrounded by assemblies who hear the Dharma together,
they are the vast radiance of the Buddha’s Dharma-body, able to appear in the world through skillful means.
Universally following the inclinations of the minds of sentient beings, He rains down the Dharma according to their faculties;
The True Suchness, the body of equality and formlessness, The stainless radiant and pure Dharma-body,
The immeasurable body of tranquil wisdom— Universally responding throughout the ten directions, he expounds the Dharma.
The powers of the Dharma King are all pure; his wisdom is like space, without limit.
He reveals everything without omission or concealment, causing all sentient beings to awaken and enter therein together.
Just as the Buddha practiced and cultivated in the past, until he attained all-encompassing wisdom.
Now he emits rays of light that pervade the entire Dharma-realm, within which all things appear with perfect clarity.
Through his original vows, the Buddha manifests spiritual powers, so that there is nowhere throughout the ten directions that is not illuminated.
Just as the Buddha cultivated his practices in the past, he proclaims them all within this web of light.
The realms of the ten directions are inexhaustible; Peerless, boundless, and each distinct, The Buddhas, with unimpeded power, emit great light, Making all lands clearly manifest.
From the self downward, the assembly born together praises his virtues. First, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva offers praise. First, he offers general praise for entering the inconceivable.
This discourse deliberates upon the ocean of skillful means for the gates of liberation. It is said that inconceivable liberation is the ocean of the fruit of Vairocana;
yet, this ocean of the fruit transcends all speech. To now proclaim it is itself a skillful means. The reason for speaking it is to enable entry into the ocean of the Tathāgata’s merits.
This, then, generally clarifies the cause and conditions for the preaching of the Dharma in this assembly. Next, ten [points] are listed:
These gates of liberation all manifest the skillful means for entering the ocean of fruition. They consist of both prose and verse.
Subsequently, various bodhisattvas each attain one kind of gate of liberation; however, the sutra lists only four.
The commentary explains that each of these many gates of liberation has its own specific meaning, continuing until the Bodhisattva Great Radiance of Ocean Moonlight.

At that time, from every one of the ornaments—the lion throne, the exquisite jewel lotuses, the wheel-shaped pedestals, the steps, and all the windows and lattices—there emerged Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field. Their names were:
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramatī-vaiśravaṇa-abhijñārāja (King of Oceanic Wisdom and Sovereign Supernatural Powers), and Ghanasvara-samanta... (Cloud Sound Universal... [and so forth].
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajra; the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Crest of Radiant Light from All Jewels;
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Courageous Wisdom of the Great Wisdom Sun; and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Seal of the Inconceivable Jewel-Wisdom of Merit.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Śatākṣa-padma-śikha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Suvarṇajvālā-paripūrṇaprabha,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Dharmadhātu-samantaghoṣa, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Meghasvara-vimalacandra,
and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Suvikrānta-prabhāketu— these and others were the leaders. There were many such Buddhas.
Appearing simultaneously in numbers as vast as the atoms within a buddha-field, these bodhisattvas each raised various clouds of offerings, namely:
clouds of all kinds of mani-jewel flowers; clouds of the exquisite fragrance of all lotuses; clouds of the perfect radiance of all jewels;
clouds of fragrant flames from boundless realms; clouds of light from sun-treasury mani-wheels; and all manner of delightful...
Clouds of the sound of mental inclinations; clouds of the radiant flames of all jewel lamps with boundless forms and colors;
clouds of flowers and fruits from the branches of various jewel trees; clouds of inexhaustible jewel maṇi-kings of pure radiance;
clouds of maṇi-kings of all kinds of ornaments—such clouds of offerings, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-world, those bodhisattvas [produced].
Each one produced such clouds of offerings, raining down upon the oceans of assemblies at all places of enlightenment in an uninterrupted succession.
Having manifested these clouds, they circumambulated the World-Honored One to the right for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of times.
Then, in their respective directions and not far from the Buddha, they magically created immeasurable varieties of precious lotus lion-thrones, each upon which—
They sat cross-legged. The conduct of these bodhisattvas was pure and vast as the ocean; they attained the light of wisdom that illuminates the Dharma of universal gates;
they followed the unimpeded conduct of all Buddhas and were able to enter the ocean of all eloquence and dharmas.
They have attained the dharma-gate of inconceivable liberation and abide on the stage of the Tathāgata’s universal gate.
Having attained all dhāraṇī-gates, they are fully able to contain and receive the ocean of all dharmas. They dwell skillfully on the ground of the equalizing wisdom of the three periods of time.
Having attained profound faith and vast joy, their boundless accumulation of merit is utterly purified;
they observe the entire dharma-realm of space without exception, and they diligently make offerings to all Buddhas appearing in every land throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-vaśavarti-abhijñārāja, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power,
surveyed the entire ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment and spoke these verses:
All that the Buddhas have realized, you have fully known; like space, unimpeded, you illuminate all clearly.
Your light pervades immeasurable lands throughout the ten directions; dwelling amidst the assemblies, you are universally pure and adorned.
The merits of the Tathāgata are immeasurable, filling the dharma-realm of the ten directions.
Universally seated beneath all the kings of trees, The great lords have gathered together like clouds.
The Buddha possesses such supernormal powers That in a single thought-moment he manifests inexhaustible signs.
The realm of the Tathāgata is boundless; Each, according to their liberation, is able to perceive it.
In the past, throughout oceans of kalpas, the Tathāgata diligently practiced various skillful means within all realms of existence to transform sentient beings,
causing them to accept and practice the teachings of all Buddhas;
Vairocana, endowed with perfect majesty, now sits upon the Lotus Treasury Lion Throne.
The entire assembly is pure and dwells in tranquility, gazing together in reverence.
The treasury of mani jewels emits radiant light, universally producing boundless clouds of fragrant flames.
Infinite flower garlands hang down in common array; upon such a seat, the Tathāgata sits.
The auspicious gates are adorned with various ornaments; they constantly emit clouds of lamp-light and jewel-flames, vast and blazing, illuminating everything without exception.
Upon the Buddha’s seat, the excellence of the adornments increases;
there are windows made of various exquisite maṇi jewels, draped with decorations of wondrous precious lotuses.
Constantly emitting wondrous sounds that delight all who hear them, The Buddha sits upon it, exceptionally radiant;
a jeweled wheel supports his seat, crescent-shaped.
With a vajra as its base, brilliant with the glow of golden light, Bodhisattvas with topknots constantly surround him; the Buddha shines most brilliantly within their midst.
Various transformations fill the ten directions, Proclaiming the vast vows of the Tathāgata;
All reflected images appear therein, And thus the Buddha sits serenely upon this throne.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Thunderous Sound Shaking Everywhere, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, universally surveyed all paths.
In that assembly, amidst the ocean-like gathering, he spoke these verses:
"The World-Honored One formerly accumulated the practices for enlightenment, Making offerings to the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions.
Sustained by the majestic power of the Sugatas, Within the seat of the Tathāgata, there is nothing not seen."
The wish-fulfilling king of fragrant-flame mani-jewels adorns the lion throne with exquisite flowers;

all manner of ornaments appear as reflections therein. All members of the assembly clearly behold them, and the Buddha’s seat universally manifests these signs of adornment, with each form and category distinct in every thought-moment.
According to the differing understandings of all sentient beings, each sees the Buddha seated upon it;
Precious branches hang down and spread, with nets of lotus flowers;
The flowers open to reveal Bodhisattvas emerging from within, Each producing subtle and pleasing sounds, praising the Tathāgata as he sits upon his seat.
The measure of the Buddha’s merit is like space; All adornments arise from this.
The various ornaments within each stage Cannot be comprehended by any sentient being.
The ground is of vajra, indestructible, Vast, pure, and utterly level.
A net of mani-jewels hangs suspended in the air, spreading everywhere beneath the Bodhi tree;
the ground is of boundless colors and wondrous forms,
strewn with powdered pure gold and scattered with famous flowers and various jewels, all of which brilliantly illuminate the Tathāgata’s seat.
The earth deities rejoice and leap for joy, manifesting in an instant without end;
they universally raise clouds of all manner of adornments and constantly remain before the Buddha, gazing up at him.
Precious lamps are vast and intensely blazing; their fragrant flames and flowing light never cease.
Manifesting various distinctions according to the occasion, the earth deities offer this as an act of worship.
Within all the lands of the ten directions, every kind of adornment found upon those grounds now appears here in this place of enlightenment;
such is possible through the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Jewel Radiance Topknot, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty,
surveyed the entire ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment and spoke these verses:
When the World-Honored One practiced in the past, he beheld all Buddha-lands as perfectly complete;
such an inexhaustible vision of the ground is now fully manifested within this site of enlightenment.
Through the World-Honored One’s vast and great supernormal powers, light is extended everywhere, raining down mani-jewels.
Thus these treasuries of jewels are scattered across the site of enlightenment; the ground all around is entirely adorned with exquisite beauty.

Through the power of the Tathāgata’s merit and spiritual penetrations, wondrous mani-jewels universally adorn the ground as well as the Bodhi tree, which alternately emit light and sound to proclaim the Dharma.
Immeasurable jewel lamps rain down from the sky, Adorned with an intermingling of various jewel-kings;
From them all issue forth subtle and wondrous sounds of Dharma— Such are the manifestations of the earth goddesses.
Throughout the jewel ground, clouds of exquisite light appear everywhere, And jewel torches blaze with brilliance like flashing lightning.
A vast net of jewels is spread out to cover it above, And various jeweled branches are distributed as a magnificent adornment.
You all should universally observe this ground, Adorned with all manner of wondrous jewels;
It reveals the ocean of the various karmas of sentient beings, Causing them to realize the true nature of phenomena.
Throughout the ten directions, all the Buddhas, And every tree of perfect enlightenment,
appear within the site of awakening; They proclaim the Tathāgata’s pure Dharma according to the inclinations of sentient beings’ minds, And from that ground, wondrous sounds emerge everywhere.
Just as that which should be expounded upon the Buddha’s seat, Each and every dharma-gate is fully proclaimed therein;
From that ground, sublime fragrances and light constantly emerge, And within the light, pure sounds are universally intoned.
If there are sentient beings capable of receiving the Dharma, They shall all hear it and their afflictions will be extinguished.
Each and every adornment is perfectly complete; even in billions of eons, none could describe it.
The Tathāgata’s spiritual power is nowhere lacking; therefore, this ground is entirely adorned and pure.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Great Wisdom Sun-Vigorous Intelligence, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, universally observed the one...
To the entire ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment, he spoke these verses:
The World-Honored One sits with serene composure in the Dharma Hall, Radiantly illuminating the midst of the palace.
In accordance with the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, His body appears universally throughout the lands of the ten directions.
The Tathāgata’s palace is inconceivable, adorned with a treasury of mani jewels;
all its ornaments radiate light, and the Buddha seated within is exceptionally brilliant.
The pillars are made of mani jewels of various colors, and bells of pure gold are spread like clouds.
Jeweled stairways are arranged in rows on all four sides; The gates and portals are wide open according to their respective directions.
Exquisite flowers, silks, and brocades form ornate canopies, While branches of jeweled trees provide mutual adornment.
Maṇi necklaces hang down on all four sides, As the Ocean of Wisdom sits serenely within.
A net of mani-jewels and banners of exquisite fragrance, with clouds of blazing lamps spread as a canopy,
and covered with various ornaments— there sits the Transcendent One of Right Knowledge,
manifesting clouds of transformations throughout the ten directions, which together with those clouds proclaim the Dharma everywhere in the world.
All sentient beings are fully tamed; thus, from the Buddha’s palace, there appear mani-jewel trees that blossom with wondrous flowers.
Whatever adornments exist throughout the lands of the ten directions across the three periods of time—there is none whose reflection does not manifest therein.
In every place there are clusters of mani-jewels, Their flames blazing in infinite varieties;
Windows and doors open in alternating directions according to the quarters, The architecture is adorned with supreme beauty.
The palace of the Tathāgata is inconceivable, Possessing pure radiance and myriad characteristics.
All palaces appear within it, and in each one sits a Tathāgata;
the palaces of the Tathāgatas are boundless, and the Self-Awakened One dwells therein.
All the assemblies from the ten directions gather here, coming toward the Buddha without exception.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Inconceivable Jewel-Seal of Wisdom and Merit, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power,
surveyed the entire ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment and spoke these verses:
In the past, the Buddha cultivated an ocean of manifold merits;
Born from the power of his vows and spiritual penetrations, as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-lands, The site of enlightenment was adorned and pure, free from all defilements;
A king of wish-fulfilling jewels served as the roots of the trees, And diamond-maṇi gems formed their trunks.
A jeweled net is spread far and wide, covering it from above; Exquisite fragrances swirl together in a circling embrace.
The tree branches are adorned with every kind of treasure; With mani-jewels for its trunk, they vie with one another in their upward growth.
Branches and twigs are densely arrayed like layered clouds; Beneath it, the Buddha sits at the site of enlightenment.
The site of enlightenment is vast and inconceivable; its trees completely cover it on all sides.
Dense leaves and profuse blossoms shelter one another in mutual reflection, and within every flower, mani-fruit is formed.
From between all the branches, wondrous light radiates forth, its brilliance illuminating the entire site of enlightenment.
Pure, blazing, and inexhaustible, manifested thus through the power of the Buddha’s vows;
with a treasury of maṇi jewels serving as flowers, casting shadows and radiating brilliance like variegated clouds,
they hang their fragrance from the trees, pervading everywhere to universally adorn the site of enlightenment.
Behold, within the Bodhimaṇḍa of the Sugata, lotuses and jeweled nets together produce pure,
radiant wheels of light that manifest from here; the sounds of bells and chimes resound amidst the clouds,
and throughout all the lands of the ten directions, there appear trees adorned with exquisite colors.
Within the Bodhi tree, there is nothing that does not appear; beneath it, the Buddha has abandoned all defilements.
This site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) is vast, accomplished through merit. From its branches, a rain of jewels falls eternally without end;
from within these jewels emerge bodhisattvas, all of whom go to the ten directions to serve and honor the Buddhas.
The realm of all Buddhas is inconceivable; It causes all those trees to universally produce the sounds of music.
Just as the path to Bodhi was previously accumulated, The entire assembly, hearing these sounds, all come to see it.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Hundred-Eyed Lotus-Crest, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed everything universally.
The assembly at the site of enlightenment then spoke these verses:
All the mani-jewels emit wondrous sounds, Proclaiming the names of the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
The immeasurable deeds of supernatural power of those Buddhas Are all clearly seen within this site of enlightenment.
Multitudes of flowers bloom in competition like spread-out tassels; clouds of light and streams of Dharma pervade the ten directions.
The Bodhi-tree deity holds these toward the Buddha, gazing with single-minded devotion as an offering.
The flaming radiance of mani-jewels forms banners; from within these banners, a brilliant and wondrous fragrance is emitted.
Its fragrance universally perfumes all multitudes; therefore, that place is entirely adorned and pure.

Lotus flowers hang down, radiating golden light; that light unfolds clouds of the Buddha’s wondrous voice, universally shading all lands throughout the ten directions, forever extinguishing the fever of afflictions for sentient beings.
By the sovereign power of the King of Bodhi Trees, A light is constantly emitted, most pure and radiant;
Throughout the boundless assemblies of the ten directions, There is none in whom it does not manifest within the site of enlightenment.
The jeweled branches and their blazing flames are like bright lamps; From that light, sounds are produced, proclaiming great vows.
The Buddha has fully explained all that he practiced throughout his former existences;
the tree-spirits, as numerous as the atoms of all lands, all together rely upon this site of enlightenment,
and before the Bodhi trees of each Tathāgata, they proclaim the gates of liberation in every thought-moment.
The various practices cultivated by the World-Honored One in the past, And the offerings made to all the Tathāgatas—
Whatever was originally practiced and whatever renown was gained, All appear within the mani-jewels of the site of enlightenment.
From them all issue sublime sounds, Whose resonance is vast and pervades the ten directions.
If there are sentient beings capable of receiving the Dharma, none fail to be tamed and made pure;
In the past, the Tathāgata universally cultivated and refined All manner of infinite adornments throughout the ten directions.
At every single Bodhi tree in the ten directions, There are infinite varieties of adornment.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Golden Flame Perfect Radiance, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty,
surveyed the ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment and spoke these verses:

In the past, when the Buddha cultivated the practices for enlightenment, he attained clear understanding regarding all objects of experience, and was pure and free from doubt concerning what is possible and what is impossible; this is the Tathāgata’s first power of knowledge.
Just as in the past he equally contemplated the nature of all phenomena, so too does he now clearly penetrate the entire ocean of karma.
Thus, now within this net of light, you universally expound throughout the ten directions the great skillful means cultivated over past kalpas;
you transform and guide according to the faculties of sentient beings, causing the minds of the entire assembly to be purified.
Therefore, the Buddha is able to achieve the power of knowledge regarding the faculties.
Just as sentient beings differ in their understandings, And their desires, inclinations, and practices each vary,
The Buddha teaches the Dharma to them according to what is appropriate. By the power of his wisdom,
he is thus able to pervade All the oceans of lands throughout the ten directions, And all realms of sentient beings therein.
The Buddha’s wisdom is equal to space, Capable of manifesting entirely within a single pore;
He fully knows the conduct of Buddhas in all places, And in a single thought-moment, the three periods of time without exception.
Regarding the lands, eons, sentient beings, and times of the ten directions— He is able to reveal them all so that they are clearly understood.
The power of meditative concentration and liberation is boundless, and the skillful means of samādhi are likewise so;
the Buddha manifests these to bring joy, universally cleansing away the darkness of afflictions.
Buddha-wisdom is unimpeded, encompassing the three periods of time, manifesting all within a single pore in a single instant.
The Buddha-lands and their sentient beings— All that appears arises through the power of recollection.
The Buddha-eye is as vast as space, Universally perceiving the entire dharma-realm without exception.
Within the stage of non-obstruction, its peerless function is such That the Buddhas can expound its immeasurable qualities.
All sentient beings are possessed of various fetters, Along with all their latent tendencies and habitual propensities;
The Tathāgata appears throughout the world And causes them all to be extinguished through skillful means.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Sound of the Dharma Realm, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, universally surveyed all paths.
Having gathered the ocean-like assembly, he then spoke these verses:
"The Buddha’s majestic spiritual power pervades the ten directions; He manifests vast displays without discrimination.
The perfections of the conduct toward Great Bodhi, Which were fulfilled in the past, he causes all to see."
In the past, you gave rise to great compassion for sentient beings;
By practicing the perfection of generosity, this body of yours has become most sublime, Able to bring joy to all who behold it.
In the past, throughout an ocean of boundless great kalpas, You cultivated and maintained the perfection of pure ethical discipline.
Thus you have attained a pure body that pervades the ten directions, universally extinguishing all the heavy sufferings of the world.
Because your past cultivation of patience was pure, and because you believed in and understood reality without discrimination,
your physical marks are all perfectly complete, universally emitting light that illuminates the ten directions.
In the past, you diligently cultivated for an ocean of many eons;

Because you can turn back the deep and heavy obstacles of sentient beings, You are able to manifest emanation bodies throughout the ten directions, Appearing beneath the King of Bodhi Trees everywhere.
The Buddha has long practiced cultivation for immeasurable eons; The great ocean of his meditative concentration is universally pure.
Thus, those who behold him find their hearts filled with joy, And the defilements of the afflictive obscurations are entirely extinguished.
The Tathāgata, having cultivated an ocean of various practices in the past, Is fully endowed with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, he radiates light that illuminates everywhere, Completely destroying all the darkness of ignorance.
Through various skillful means, he transforms sentient beings, Causing all that they cultivate and refine to be fully accomplished.
He travels everywhere throughout the ten directions, Without resting for even a single boundless eon.
In the past, during oceans of great eons, the Buddha Purely cultivated his vows and the perfections.
Therefore, he appears throughout all worlds, Saving sentient beings until the end of the future;
Having extensively cultivated and refined all powers and dharmas over immeasurable eons,
He is able to accomplish the power of spontaneity, Universally manifesting in all lands of the ten directions.
In the past, the Buddha cultivated the wisdom of the universal gate; The nature of all-knowledge is like empty space.
Therefore, he attained unimpeded power, Extending light that universally illumines the lands of the ten directions.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Cloud-Sound Pure Moon, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, universally surveyed all paths.
Having gathered this ocean-like assembly, he then spoke these verses:
"The realm of his supernormal powers is equal to space; No sentient being in the ten directions fails to see it.
The ground accomplished through his past cultivation— All is fully explained within the fruit of the mani-jewel."
Having purified their diligent practice through immeasurable eons, they enter the First Ground, the Utterly Joyful,
giving birth to the vast wisdom of the Dharma-realm. Universally beholding the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions,
they abide in the Stainless Ground within all phenomena, maintaining pure precepts equal in number to all sentient beings.
Having extensively practiced for many eons, making offerings to oceans of boundless Buddhas,
one accumulates merit on the Ground of Radiance (*Arciṣmatī*);
having fully heard the vast Dharma-clouds of the treasury of *śamatha* and the firm patience (*kṣānti*), it is thus described within the fruit of the *maṇi*.
The Ground of Immeasurable Wisdom-Light of the Flame-Ocean, Thoroughly understanding all realms, it gives rise to compassion;
The body of equality throughout all lands, It expounds everywhere according to the Buddha’s governance.
The Ground of Difficult to Conquer, the Gate of the Universal Treasury, Where movement and stillness accord without contradiction.
The realm of the Buddha-dharma is entirely equal; as the Buddha has purified it, so can they all expound it.
This ground of the ocean of wisdom through vast cultivation thoroughly understands all dharma-gates and universally manifests lands like space, proclaiming this Dharma-sound from within the trees.
The body of empty space pervades the entire Dharma-realm; A lamp of wisdom that universally illumines all sentient beings.
All skillful means are utterly pure; That which was traversed in the distant past is now fully expounded.
Adorned by all vows and practices, The immeasurable oceans of lands are all purified.
All conceptual constructions are unable to move it; this groundless stage is proclaimed by all as having immeasurable spheres of supernatural power (*abhijñā*).
It is the power of light that skillfully enters the teachings—this is the Pure Stage of Excellent Intelligence (*sādhumatī*), wherein the practices of oceans of eons are fully elucidated.
The tenth stage, Vast Cloud of Dharma, contains all things and pervades space;
it is proclaimed within the sounds of the realm of all Buddhas. These sounds are the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Banner of Light of Good Valor, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions.
Then he spoke in verse:
"Countless sentient beings within this assembly, With various inclinations and pure minds,
Are all able to awaken to and enter the wisdom of the Tathāgata, Thoroughly comprehending all realms of adornment."
Each has given rise to pure vows and cultivated all practices; All have made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas.
Some are able to see the Tathāgata’s true body, As well as all his various spiritual transformations.
Others are able to see the Buddha’s Dharma-body, Incomparable, unimpeded, and universally pervasive.
All the infinite natures of phenomena enter his body without exception;
some behold the Buddha’s wondrous form-body, its boundless colors and marks blazing with light.
According to the differing understandings of sentient beings, he manifests various transformations throughout the ten directions.
Some see the body of unimpeded wisdom, equal throughout the three times like space,
universally turning according to the inclinations and joys of sentient beings, so that all may behold its various distinctions;
some are able to comprehend the Buddha’s voice, which pervades all lands throughout the ten directions.
In accordance with what sentient beings should understand, he utters sounds and speech without obstruction;
Or one may see the various lights of the Tathāgata, Various illuminations pervading the world.
Or, within the Buddha’s radiance, One may further see all Buddhas manifesting their supernormal powers.
Some behold the Buddha’s ocean-like clouds of light, Emitting from his pores a blazing radiance that manifests the path of his past cultivation,
Causing them to give rise to deep faith and enter the Buddha’s wisdom;
Or they behold the marks of the Buddha adorned with merit, And see the source from which this merit arises.
The oceans of perfections practiced in the past, All are clearly seen within the marks of the Buddha;
The Tathāgata’s merit is immeasurable, Pervading the dharma-realm without limit.
As well as the realms of his supernormal powers— By the power of the Buddha, these can be proclaimed.
From within this lower lion throne, a multitude of beings emerged, headed by ten bodhisattvas, foremost among whom was Sāgaramati-vikrīḍita-abhijñārāja.
Their number was as vast as the atoms within many buddha-fields. Each raised clouds of various offerings;
having presented these offerings, they each manifested at their respective locations precious lotus lion thrones.
Each sat down cross-legged and praised his virtue, being able to pervade the ten directions and diligently make offerings to the Buddha.
Each spoke verses in praise of one specific quality of the Buddha: first, praising the Buddha’s body and seat; second, praising the seat and the ground;
third, praising the site of the field; fourth, praising the palace; fifth, praising the mastery over the trees throughout; sixth, praising the field and the trees; and seventh, praising the Buddha.

10. The Ten Powers (daśabala). 8. Praising the Buddha’s ten perfections (pāramitā). 9. Praising the Buddha’s ten stages (bhūmi). 10. Praising the Buddha’s essence and function. Each of these commentaries has its own specific meaning.
At that time, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, the entire ground of the Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean underwent six kinds of ten-fold [earthquakes].
The earth shook in eight ways: namely, it moved, moved everywhere, and moved universally; it rose, rose everywhere, and rose universally; it leaped, leaped everywhere, and leaped universally;
it quaked, quaked everywhere, and quaked universally; it roared, roared everywhere, and roared universally; it crashed, crashed everywhere, and crashed universally.
Each of these lords of worlds manifested inconceivable clouds of offerings and rained them down upon the Tathāgata.
They came to the ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment, bringing what were known as clouds of all manner of fragrant flowers and ornaments;
clouds of all kinds of exquisite mani-jewel decorations; clouds of nets of jewel-flames and flowers; clouds of infinite varieties of round halos of mani-jewels;
clouds of treasuries of pearls of every color; clouds of all kinds of precious sandalwood incense; and clouds of all kinds of precious canopies. Pure...
Clouds of mani-kings of pure and wondrous sound; clouds of sun-light mani necklaces and wheels; clouds of treasuries of light from all jewels;
clouds of all various distinct ornaments—such clouds of offerings as these were immeasurable and inconceivable in number.
Each of these lords of worlds manifested such clouds of offerings, raining them down.
The ocean-like assemblies at the Tathāgata’s place of enlightenment were nowhere not fully pervaded.

Just as every world-ruler in this world-system gave rise to joy and made such offerings, so too did all the world-rulers in every world within the Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean likewise make offerings. Within all those worlds, there were likewise...
As the Tathāgata sat upon the site of enlightenment, each world-ruler attained individual faith and understanding;
each had their own object of focus, each their own gateway of samādhi skillful means, each practiced the dharmas that assist the path, each achieved realization, and each rejoiced.
Each entered individually; each awakened to and understood the various dharma-gates; each entered the realm of the Tathāgata’s spiritual powers;
each entered the realm of the Tathāgata’s powers; each entered the gate of the Tathāgata’s liberation.
Just as it was in this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, so it was likewise throughout all world-oceans in the ten directions, to the very limits of the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space.
Thus it is.
Below this, the auspicious omens of heaven and earth are clarified; that is to say, the shaking of the earth and the arising of offerings serve as manifest proof.

Above, the Buddha attained perfect enlightenment, and the ocean-like assembly gathered like clouds, each expressing congratulations and praise. Having thus manifested the Buddha’s loftiness and profundity, he now accords with the capacities of sentient beings.
As for the meaning: it accords with the Buddha’s vows above; thus the Lord of the World provides offerings on his behalf, and Heaven and Earth manifest auspicious omens for him.

Regarding the text, first the earth shakes, then the offerings arise. Starting from the narrow and extending to the vast, it is called the Flower Treasury (Avataṃsaka); this is established based on the lower section to universally encompass all.

In reality, it pervades the entire Dharma-realm. Furthermore, the assembly gathered at the site of the teaching, down to those who manifest auspicious signs and present offerings, all collectively constitute a wondrous adornment.
The preceding section concludes the explanation of the causes and conditions for the arising of the teaching; the following section distinguishes the ritual procedures for expounding the Dharma.
Outline of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, Fascicle Five;
Outline of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, Fascicle Six.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan.
Commentary on the Meaning by the Śramaṇa Chengguan of Qingliangshan Dahuayan Monastery;
Extracted and Annotated by the Śramaṇa Deqing of Huanshan Fayun Monastery.
Chapter Two: The Manifestation of the Tathāgata’s Physical Form.

From this chapter onward is the main body of the treatise (*śāstra*). It consists of six chapters of scripture, categorized as the section that "exhibits the fruit to encourage joy and engender faith.
The first chapter, "The Causes and Conditions for the Arising of the Teaching," is now concluded. Next, there are two chapters concerning the ritual procedures for preaching the Dharma;

this present chapter is one of them. This constitutes the skillful means (*upāya*) specific to this section. First, the manifestation of signs serves as the remote skillful means; subsequently follows the "Samādhi" chapter.

This serves as the proximate preparation. Now, the first chapter consists of six sections: (1) the universal assembly’s joint invitation; (2) the summoning of those with karmic affinity by means of light;
(3) the gathering of the summoned like clouds; (4) the manifestation of auspicious signs to indicate the teaching; (5) the extolling of the Buddha’s virtues;

and (6) the conclusion that reveals the inexhaustibility [of the teaching]. Regarding the title of this chapter, "Manifestation of Signs," there are five types of signs manifested: the first is the manifestation from the face.
First, the light-sign summons the assemblies from the ten directions; second, the light-sign between the eyebrows manifests to show the master of the Dharma discourse;
third, the network of lands trembles to awaken the various capacities of sentient beings; fourth, a flower appears before the Buddha to indicate that the teaching concerns the fruits of reliance;
fifth, the white tuft of hair emits a multitude [of rays] to signify that the teaching flows from the Buddha. Because there are these five signs, it is given this name.
At that time, the various bodhisattvas and all the lords of the world reflected thus:

"The assembly of the oceanic multitudes has already gathered below, and since they all long for the realm of the Buddha, they collectively offer this request through mindfulness. There are two parts to this request:
first, the request made through the prose reflection of the oceanic multitudes; second, the request made through the verses of the offering-sound. Together, these comprise forty lines.
Question: What is the ground of all Buddhas? What is the realm of all Buddhas? What is the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all Buddhas?
What is the conduct of all Buddhas? What is the power of all Buddhas? What is the non-attachment of all Buddhas?
[He] was afraid. [He asked: "What are the samādhis of the Buddhas? What are the supernormal powers (abhijñā) of the Buddhas?
What is the mastery (vaśitā) of the Buddhas? What is the inability of others to grasp the Buddhas?"
These ten questions concern the Buddha’s qualities and functions being perfectly complete.
What is the eye of the Buddhas? What is the ear of the Buddhas? What is the nose of the Buddhas? What is the tongue of the Buddhas?
What is the body of the Buddhas? What is the mind of the Buddhas? What is... [the rest of the text]... of the Buddhas?
The radiance of the Buddha’s body: What is the light of the Buddhas? What is the voice of the Buddhas? What is the wisdom of the Buddhas?
We pray only that the World-Honored One, out of compassion for us, will reveal and expound upon these.
These ten phrases inquire about the Buddha’s manifest body and characteristics. The preceding twenty phrases inquire about the fruit.

Furthermore, all Buddhas throughout the oceans of worlds in the ten directions expound for the sake of all bodhisattvas the ocean of worlds, the ocean of sentient beings, the ocean of the establishment of the dharma-realm, the ocean of Buddhas, the ocean of the Buddha’s pāramitās, the ocean of the Buddha’s liberation, and the ocean of the Buddha’s transformations.
The ocean of transformations; the ocean of the Buddha’s teachings; the ocean of the Buddhas’ names and titles; the ocean of the Buddhas’ lifespans.
These examples cite the Buddhas of the ten directions expounding the ten oceans for the sake of bodhisattvas, thereby manifesting that their transformative activity is universally pervasive.
And the ocean of all bodhisattvas’ vows; the ocean of all bodhisattvas’ setting forth; the ocean of all bodhisattvas’ aids to the path;
the ocean of all bodhisattvas’ vehicles; the ocean of all bodhisattvas’ practices; the ocean of all bodhisattvas’ renunciations;
the ocean of all bodhisattvas’ supernormal powers; the ocean of all bodhisattvas’ perfections; all bodhisattvas...
The earth and oceans; the ocean of wisdom of all bodhisattvas. We pray that the Buddha, the World-Honored One, will likewise speak for us in this manner.
The following ten phrases inquire into the profound and vast nature of the causal virtues. These ten oceans span from the stage of the Ten Faiths up to the position of Equal Enlightenment.
Because the inquiries are so profound, these forty questions take the ten oceans within the state of fruition as their general framework. Nine.
The *Huìtóng* (Compendium) answers the ten "seas" (*sāgara*) as follows: 1. The "Chapter on the Accomplishment of Worlds" answers the Sea of the Establishment of Worlds;
2. The "Chapter on the Treasury of Flowers" answers the Sea of Worlds; 3. The "Chapter on Names and Titles" answers the Sea of the Tathāgatas’ Names and Titles;

4. The "Chapter on the Four Noble Truths" answers the Sea of Exposition; 5. From the "Chapter on Radiance and Enlightenment" through the "Chapter on the Ten Patiences," these answer the ten phrases individually.

The response to the question concerning the ocean of sentient beings is provided by the "Chapter on the Six Asaṃkhyeyas," for those who cultivate the causes are precisely the beings to be transformed.
The prose section cites the numbers, while the verses extensively clarify the successive layers of transformations, which are subtle and difficult to describe.
The seventh [section] answers the ocean of lifespan by means of the lifespan and dwelling places; the eighth consists of five [sections] beginning with the "Inconceivable."

The twenty questions regarding the fruits are answered individually to provide a general elucidation of the ocean of Buddhas, as the Buddha is revealed through the profound depth and vastness of his virtues.
Ninth, the eighth assembly answers the question regarding the ocean of *pāramitās*, because all stages are subsumed therein and all practices are brought to fulfillment.

Tenth, the ninth assembly answers the question regarding the ocean of liberation, because one realizes and enters the *dharmadhātu* to give rise to great salvific activity. The above is explained according to the general [classification].
If one speaks according to the specific [classification], the answers should be fully gathered. This has two meanings.
First, the answer by manifestation of signs, which is detailed in the following text. Second, the answer by verbal explanation, which itself has two meanings.

First, because the sūtra has not yet reached its conclusion—since there is no final summary after the Vairocana Chapter—the intention is that the answer shall be provided within future sūtras. Second, it is an answer that encompasses both.
"Others. This means that by correctly answering the questions regarding the establishment of the world and the world itself, one simultaneously answers the remaining thirty-eight questions.
The supplementary commentary states: "The first twenty phrases inquire about the fruit; these cite the fruit realized by Vairocana. The subsequent ten..."
The first phrase asks about the cause; it specifically asks about the cause for grasping the fruit. The intermediate ten phrases cite examples to ask about the ten oceans within the fruit.
Since these are all sought after by Bodhisattvas, they are practiced universally across all stages, from the Ten Faiths up to Equal Enlightenment.

Because each stage universally encompasses [all others], it constitutes universal practice (*samantacaryā*). The final three [stages] involve thorough investigation throughout; all of these are this very practice. Therefore, the Commentary states:
"The nine assemblies answer together.
At that time, by the majestic spiritual power (*anubhāva*) of the bodhisattvas, from within the clouds of all offering implements, there naturally emerge..."
Then, with a voice, he spoke these verses:
"Having fulfilled his practice through immeasurable eons, He attained perfect enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree.
To deliver sentient beings, he manifests his body everywhere, Like clouds pervading all the way to the end of the future."
May all doubts of sentient beings be severed, And may vast faith and understanding be fully inspired in them.
May boundless suffering be universally eliminated, And may the peace and bliss of all Buddhas be realized by all.
Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms of countless lands Have all come together to this assembly to gaze upon [the Buddha].
May you preach the sublime Dharma according to their inclinations and remove their doubts:
How is the ground of all Buddhas to be understood? How is the realm of the Tathāgata to be observed?
The empowerment of the Buddhas is boundless; I pray that you reveal this teaching so that it may be purified.
What is the sphere of action of the Buddhas, Which through wisdom can be clearly entered as the pure, vast, and boundless powers of a Buddha? For the sake of all bodhisattvas, you should reveal:
What are the vast samādhis, And how are the dharmas of fearlessness purified?
The power and function of your supernormal knowledges are immeasurable; we pray that you will speak of the various Buddha-dharmas according to the inclinations of sentient beings.
Like a sovereign lord of the world, your conduct is autonomous and cannot be restrained, as are all other vast dharmas;
for the sake of benefiting others, please expound them.
How is it that the Buddha-eye is immeasurable? The same is true for the ears, nose, tongue, and body.
Furthermore, how is it that the mind is immeasurable? I pray you will show the skillful means by which this is known.
As with the oceans of all lands and the oceans of sentient beings, So too are the oceans of all establishments within the Dharma-realm.

And the oceans of all Buddhas are likewise boundless; I pray that for the sake of the sons of the Buddha, you will fully expound them all, So that they may forever emerge from the ocean of inconceivable means of deliverance, And universally enter the ocean of expedient means of liberation.
I pray that within this site of enlightenment, you will proclaim The entire ocean of all dharma-gates.

The following is an invocation through verses accompanied by sound. Whereas the previous invocation was made through mindfulness, this one is made through explicit speech so that the assembly may all understand together.
As for the musical instruments producing sound, since they previously made offerings for the sake of the Dharma, they now proclaim the mind through those offerings;

because they do not depend on being struck or played, they are called "spontaneous" (*svayambhū*), thereby manifesting that the offering implements are themselves the essence of the *dharmadhātu*. Regarding what is invoked within these verses:
This refers to restating the intent of the forty questions previously requested by the Bodhisattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of the Bodhisattvas, [emitted light] from between his teeth at the gate of his mouth.
He emitted as many rays of light as there are atoms in a buddha-field, namely: the light called "Universal Illumination of Multitude of Jewel Flowers";

the light called "Adorning the Dharma Realm with Various Sounds"; the light called "Hanging Down Subtle Clouds"; the light called "The Buddhas of the Ten Directions Sitting at the Site of Enlightenment and Manifesting Spiritual Transformations";
the light called "Cloud Canopies of All Jewel Flames"; and the unobstructed light that fills the entire dharma realm.
The light that universally adorns all Buddha-fields; the light that stands loftily erect as pure vajra-jewel banners;
the light that universally adorns the sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) where assemblies of bodhisattvas gather;

the light that extols the names of all Buddhas with wondrous sounds—and so forth, each of these being as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, and each of those, in turn, possessing as many [lights] as there are atoms within a Buddha-field.

Radiant light serves as its retinue; that light is entirely endowed with the colors of various wondrous jewels and universally illumines world-oceans, numbering as many as the atoms within one hundred million Buddha-lands in each of the ten directions.
Within those world-oceans, the assemblies of bodhisattvas each perceive this Flower Bank Arrayed World-Ocean within the radiance. By the Buddha’s spiritual power, that light, in those [worlds]...
Before the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas, he spoke these verses:
Through oceans of practice over immeasurable eons, Making offerings to oceans of Buddhas throughout the ten directions,
And transforming and delivering oceans of all sentient beings, He has brought them to the state of the Wondrously Awakened, the Pervasive Illuminator.
From within his pores emerge clouds of emanations, Their radiance universally illuminating the ten directions.
All those who are ready for transformation are awakened, Causing them to hasten toward Bodhi with pure non-obstruction.
In the past, the Buddha traveled through the various realms of existence, Teaching and maturing all living beings.
With sovereign supernormal powers of boundless measure, In a single thought, he causes all to attain liberation.
The Bodhi tree is a wondrous mani-jewel, Adorned with every kind of exquisite ornament.
Beneath it, the Buddha attained perfect enlightenment, Emitting great radiance that shines everywhere.
A great sound thunders and roars, pervading the ten directions, universally proclaiming the Dharma of quiescence;
according to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, he employs various skillful means to bring them to understanding.
Having practiced the perfections in the past until they were all perfected, their number is equal to the atoms within a thousand lands.
All powers are now fully perfected; you all should go together to pay homage.
Sons of the Buddhas of the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms of all lands, have all gathered here with joyful hearts.
Having already rained down clouds of offerings, they now stand before the Buddha, gazing up at him with single-minded devotion.
The Tathāgata’s single voice is immeasurable; It can expound the profound and vast ocean of the sūtras.
Universally raining down the sublime Dharma to accord with the minds of all beings, That Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings should be visited and seen.
All the vows of the Buddhas of the three periods of time Were proclaimed beneath the Bodhi tree.
In a single instant, all things appear before you; you should quickly go to the presence of the Tathāgata, Vairocana, the great ocean of wisdom.
From his face, light radiates such that there is nowhere it does not reach;
now, awaiting the assembly, he is about to proclaim his voice. You should go and behold him, and hear what he says.

The following section concerns the summoning of those with karmic affinity. Since the Bodhisattvas previously invoked through recollection are all manifestations of the dharmadhātu’s dependent origination, they belong to those with affinity.

As he is about to answer the questions posed, and since that which is questioned is the ocean of the dharmadhātu—not merely what is present before one—he employs light to illuminate the ocean of the dharmadhātu, thereby convening the assembly of those with affinity from throughout the ocean-like realm.
Light was emitted from the gaps between his teeth; because he possessed forty teeth, this served as a symbolic response to the forty questions.
Since this very light constitutes the essence of the teaching, he next spoke these verses through the Buddha’s spiritual power, using the gāthās within that light.

It is said that when the Buddha’s ten titles were fully realized and his perfect enlightenment was first achieved, he summoned those from the ten directions to go together to behold him and listen to the Dharma;
therefore, it concludes by saying, "You may go to behold him and hear what he teaches."

At that time, all the assemblies throughout the oceans of worlds in the ten directions, having been awakened by the Buddha’s radiance, each came together to approach and make offerings to the Tathāgata Vairocana.
That is to say, to the east of this Flower Bank Array Ocean of Worlds, there is another ocean of worlds named Pure Light Lotus Array. In that world...
Within the realm-seeds, there is a land named Maṇi-kaṇṭhaka-vajra-garbha. The Buddha there is named Dharma-jala-buddha-ananta-ākāśa-rāja.

Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Vipaśyana-vara-dharma-padma-dhvaja, who, together with as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, has come to visit the Buddha.
In each location, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of bodhisattva physical forms, filling the void without dispersing or ceasing.
Furthermore, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of light from all-jeweled lotus flowers raining down, and ten kinds of clouds of Sumeru jewel peaks.
Furthermore, ten kinds of clouds of solar radiance appeared; ten kinds of clouds of precious flower garlands appeared;
ten kinds of clouds of all manner of music appeared; ten kinds of clouds of powdered incense trees appeared;
ten kinds of clouds of various forms of unguents and burning incenses appeared; and ten kinds of clouds of all manner of fragrant trees appeared. Such were the worlds that manifested.
Clouds of offerings as numerous as the atoms in the ocean, completely pervading all of space without dispersing or ceasing, appeared.
Having manifested these clouds, they paid homage to the Buddha as an act of worship. Then, in the eastern direction, each manifested a lion throne of various flower-luminous treasuries;
upon these thrones, they sat cross-legged. To the south of this Flower Treasury World, [they likewise appeared].
Next, there is an ocean of worlds named Treasury of Adornments of the Radiance of All Jewel Moons.
Within that world-system, there is a land named Adornment of Perfect Boundless Light. The Buddha there is named Sumeru King of Universal Wisdom Radiance Virtue.
Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Universally Illuminating the Ocean of Dharma.
The Bodhisattva Prajñā, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came to where the Buddha was.
Each manifested ten kinds of clouds of *maṇi* kings of the treasury of light of all adornments, which filled the void without dispersing or ceasing.
They further manifested ten kinds of clouds of *maṇi* kings that rain down all precious ornaments and universally illuminate, and again manifested ten...
There appeared clouds of mani-kings of blazing jewel-flames proclaiming the names of Buddhas; further, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of mani-kings expounding all Buddha-dharmas;
further, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of mani-kings with various wondrous trees adorning the site of enlightenment;
further, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of mani-kings whose precious light shines everywhere, manifesting multitudes of transformation Buddhas; further, there appeared...
Ten kinds of clouds of *maṇi*-kings manifesting the adornments of all sites of enlightenment;

furthermore, ten kinds of clouds of *maṇi*-kings manifesting the lamps of secret flames that proclaim the realms of all Buddhas; furthermore, ten kinds of clouds of *maṇi*-kings manifesting the images of the palaces of inconceivable Buddha-fields;
furthermore, ten kinds of clouds of *maṇi*-kings manifesting the images of the bodies of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Clouds of mani-kings, as numerous as the atoms within such oceans of worlds, completely filled the void without dispersing or vanishing.
Having manifested these clouds, they paid homage to the Buddha as an offering.
Then, in the southern direction, each manifested a lion throne consisting of a treasury of Jambūnada gold lotuses made of indranīla gems; upon those thrones—
He sat in the full lotus posture. To the west of this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, there is another world-ocean named Lovely Jewel Radiance.
Within that world-system, there is a land named Producing Supreme and Wondrous Requisites for Sustenance.
The Buddha there is named Fragrant Flame Merit Jewel Adornment. Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there was a bodhisattva-mahāsattva...
The Bodhisattva named Moonlight Fragrance Flame Universal Adornment, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came to where the Buddha was.
Each manifested ten kinds of clouds of pavilions made of all manner of precious incense and exquisite flowers, which filled the void without dispersing or fading.
They further manifested ten kinds of pavilions of sovereign jewels with infinite colors and forms.
Clouds of ten kinds of precious lamp-flame incense pavilions appeared; clouds of ten kinds of pavilions made of all manner of pearls appeared;
clouds of ten kinds of pavilions made of all manner of precious flowers appeared; clouds of ten kinds of pavilions adorned with precious necklaces appeared;
and clouds of ten kinds of light universally manifesting all adornments throughout the ten directions appeared.
Clouds of jeweled pavilions; furthermore, clouds of pavilions adorned with ten kinds of various precious powders interspersed;
furthermore, clouds of pavilions adorned throughout the ten directions by ten kinds of various jewels;
furthermore, clouds of pavilions with ten kinds of flower-gateways and networks of bells—such clouds of pavilions, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely pervaded [the space].
Without dispersing or extinguishing from the void, these clouds appeared and paid homage to the Buddha as an offering.
Then, in the western direction, each manifested a lion throne made of great treasuries of true golden leaves.
Upon these thrones, they sat cross-legged. To the north of this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, there is another world-ocean named Vaidūrya Lotus.
Within the world-system called *Puṣpaprabhāsa-paripūrṇagarbha*, there is a land named *Utpalavicitravyūha*.

There, the Buddha is named *Samantajñānadhvaja-rāja*. From within that Tathāgata’s ocean-like assembly, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva named *Siṃhavikrīḍitaprabha*, who comes together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds.
They approached the place where the Buddha was. Each manifested ten kinds of clouds of all-fragrant mani-jewel trees of exquisite beauty, which filled the void without dispersing or ceasing.
They further manifested ten kinds of clouds of trees adorned with dense leaves and sublime fragrances.
They further manifested ten kinds of clouds of trees adorned with manifestations of all boundless forms and colors. They further manifested ten kinds of all flowers.
He manifested clouds of trees arrayed with universal adornments. He further manifested ten kinds of clouds of trees adorned with the perfect radiance of flames of all jewels.
He further manifested ten kinds of clouds of trees adorned with the bodies of Bodhisattvas manifesting all types of sandalwood fragrance.
He further manifested ten kinds of clouds of trees displaying the inconceivable adornments of former sites of enlightenment. He further manifested ten kinds of multitudes...
There appeared clouds of jewel-robe treasuries like the radiance of sun-light trees; furthermore, ten kinds of clouds of trees that universally emit all pleasing sounds appeared.
Such clouds of trees, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely filled the void without dispersing or vanishing.
Having manifested these clouds, they prostrated toward the Buddha as an offering, and then, from the northern direction, each—
He manifested a lion throne made of mani-lamp lotus-treasures and sat upon it in the full lotus posture.
To the northeast of this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, there is another world-ocean named Jambūnada-gold and crystal-colored banner.
Within that world-system, there is a land named Adorned with Various Jewels, and the Buddha there is named Sarva-... [omitted].
The Lamp of Fearlessness in the Dharma. Within that ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Most Victorious Light-Lamp Inexhaustible Treasury of Merit.

Accompanied by as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, he came to the presence of the Buddha, each manifesting clouds of lion-thrones within jewel-lotus treasuries of ten kinds of boundless colors and forms.
They pervaded all of space without dispersing or ceasing. Furthermore, they manifested ten kinds of clouds of lion thrones from the light-treasury of mani-kings;
ten kinds of clouds of lion thrones adorned with various ornaments of every kind of embellishment;
ten kinds of clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of flames of lamps made of garlands of many jewels; and ten kinds of clouds that universally rained down jewels.
Clouds of lion thrones adorned with necklaces appeared; furthermore, ten kinds of clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of all fragrant flowers and precious necklaces appeared;
furthermore, ten kinds of clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of mani-kings that manifest the adornments of all Buddha-seats appeared;
furthermore, ten kinds of lion thrones adorned with windows, doorways, staircases, and various necklaces appeared.
There appeared clouds of lion thrones made of the essence of all kinds of mani-tree branches and stalks;
there also appeared clouds of lion thrones from the sun-light-essence treasury, adorned with ten kinds of precious incense.
Such clouds of lion thrones, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely filled the void without dispersing or vanishing. Having manifested these clouds, they remained.
They prostrated before the Buddha as an act of worship.
Then, in the northeast, each manifested a lion throne of precious lotus flowers and mani-light banners; upon these thrones, they sat cross-legged.
To the southeast of this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, there is another world-ocean named Golden Adornment Lapis Lazuli Light Universally Shining. In that world...
Within the realm-seeds, there is a land named Pure Fragrant Radiance. The Buddha there is named King of Universal Joy and Profound Faith.

Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Wisdom Lamp Universal Illumination, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, has come to the presence of the Buddha, each manifesting ten kinds of all... [as previously described].
Clouds of wish-fulfilling jewel canopies of the mind-kings filled the void without dispersing or ceasing.
Furthermore, ten kinds of canopies of all-flower adornments made of indranīla jewels appeared; ten kinds of canopies of all-fragrant maṇi jewels appeared;
ten kinds of canopies of jewel-flame lamps appeared; and ten kinds of canopies manifesting the Buddha’s supernormal powers and preaching the Dharma appeared.
There appeared clouds of the King of Nīlas’ canopies; furthermore, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of mani-canopies manifesting the colors and forms of all clothing and ornaments;
furthermore, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of canopies of radiant clusters of all-jeweled flowers;

furthermore, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of canopies with the sound of jewel-nets and bells; furthermore, there appeared [ten kinds of] clouds of canopies with mani-terraces and lotus-flower nets.
They manifested ten kinds of clouds of canopies in the form of images of all inconceivable ornaments.
Such clouds of various precious canopies, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely filled the void without dispersing or ceasing.
Having manifested these clouds, they prostrated toward the Buddha as an offering, and then, in the southeastern direction, each magically created a precious lotus flower.
He sat upon a lion throne, assuming the full lotus posture.
To the southwest of this Flower Treasury Ocean of Worlds, there is another ocean of worlds named Sunlight Pervading Illumination.
Within that world-system, there is a land named Lion Sun Radiance, where the Buddha is named Sound of Universal Wisdom Light. There, amidst the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata—
Within it, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Samantakusumaprabhājvālācūḍa, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came to where the Buddha was.
Each manifested ten kinds of clouds of various exquisite, adorned jewel-canopies, which filled all of space without dispersing or vanishing.
They further manifested ten kinds of clouds of flower-canopies adorned with light, and further manifested...
There appeared clouds of ten kinds of canopies of pearl-treasury covers of infinite colors.

There further appeared clouds of ten kinds of mani-king canopies that emit the sounds of the compassion of all bodhisattvas. There further appeared clouds of ten kinds of canopies of garlands of flames of various exquisite jewels.
There further appeared clouds of ten kinds of canopies with hanging nets and bells adorned with exquisite jewels. There further appeared clouds of ten kinds of mani-tree branches...
Clouds of majestic canopies; furthermore, clouds of ten kinds of mani-king canopies that universally illuminate with the light of the sun;
furthermore, clouds of ten kinds of canopies made of all types of ointment and incense; furthermore, clouds of ten kinds of canopies from the treasury of sandalwood;
furthermore, clouds of ten kinds of vast canopies adorned with universal radiance within the sphere of the Buddhas. Such as these, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds...
Clouds of jewel canopies, as numerous as atoms of dust, completely filled the void without dispersing or vanishing. Having manifested these clouds, they prostrated toward the Buddha as an offering.
Then, in the southwest, each of them magically created a lion throne adorned with a treasury of light-flames of sapphire-blue jewels.
Upon those thrones, they sat cross-legged. This was in the Flower Treasury World-Ocean.
To the northwest, there is an ocean of worlds named Jewel Radiance. Within that world-system, there is a land named Adorned with Various Fragrances.
The Buddha there is named Light of the Ocean of Infinite Skillful Virtues.
Within the great ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva named King of Inexhaustible Light Maṇi, who, together with an ocean of worlds...
Bodhisattvas as numerous as atoms arrived together at the place where the Buddha was.

Each manifested ten kinds of clouds of light, perfectly complete with all jewels, which filled the entirety of space without dispersing or fading. They further manifested ten kinds of clouds of light, perfectly complete with the flames of all jewels;
they further manifested ten kinds of clouds of light, perfectly complete with all exquisite flowers; they further manifested ten kinds of all...
There appeared clouds of perfect light from the emanation-buddhas; further, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of perfect light from the buddha-lands of the ten directions;
further, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of perfect light from jewel trees with the thunderous sound of the buddhas' realms;

further, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of perfect light from all kinds of lapis lazuli and mani-jewel kings; further, there appeared ten kinds of clouds manifesting infinite multitudes within a single thought-moment.
There appeared clouds of perfect light manifesting the signs of birth; further, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of perfect light manifesting the sounds of the great vows of all Tathāgatas;
and further, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of perfect light manifesting the sounds of mani-kings that transform all sentient beings.
Such clouds of perfect light, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely pervaded the void without dispersing or vanishing.
Having manifested these clouds, they prostrated toward the Buddha as an offering.
Then, in the northwest, each of them magically created a lion throne of inexhaustible radiance and majestic power; upon those thrones, they sat cross-legged.
Below this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, there is another world-ocean named Lotus Fragrance Wondrous Virtue Treasury.
Within that world-system, there is a land named Jewel Lion Radiant Illumination. The Buddha there is named Dharma-Realm Radiance.
Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Dharma-Realm Light.
Jvālāmati, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came to where the Buddha was.
Each manifested ten kinds of clouds of light from all the treasuries of mani-jewels, which filled the void without dispersing or fading.
They further manifested ten kinds of clouds of light from all fragrances, and further manifested ten kinds of clouds of light from all jewel-flames. Furthermore, they manifested...
Ten kinds of light-rainclouds emerged, proclaiming the sounds of the Dharma taught by all Buddhas;
further, ten kinds of light-rainclouds appeared, manifesting the adornments of all Buddha-lands; further, ten kinds of light-rainclouds appeared, consisting of pavilions of exquisite flowers;
further, ten kinds of light-rainclouds appeared, manifesting the deeds of all Buddhas in teaching and transforming sentient beings throughout all kalpas; further, they appeared...
There appeared ten kinds of clouds of light from the filaments of all inexhaustible jewel flowers, and further, ten kinds of clouds of light from all manner of adorned seats.
