Such clouds of light, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely pervaded the void without dispersing or fading.
Having manifested these clouds, they paid homage to the Buddha as an offering, and then, from below—
Each manifested a lion throne of precious flaming lamp lotus-treasury and sat upon those thrones in the full lotus posture.
Above this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, there is a world-ocean named Adorned with the Radiance of Mani Jewels.
Within that world-system, there is a land named Subtle Light Without Characteristics, where the Buddha is named Unobstructed.
Within that ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata King of Merit and Radiance, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Unobstructed Power, Diligence, and Wisdom.
Accompanied by as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, he approached the presence of the Buddha.
Each manifested ten kinds of clouds of jewel-light flames with infinite colors and forms, which filled all of space without dispersing.
They vanished. Then there appeared ten kinds of clouds of radiant flames from mani-jewel nets.
Then there appeared ten kinds of clouds of radiant flames adorning all vast buddha-fields. Then there appeared ten kinds of clouds of radiant flames of all exquisite fragrances.
Then there appeared ten kinds of clouds of radiant flames of all adornments. Then there appeared ten kinds of clouds of radiant flames from the emanations of all buddhas.
Furthermore, they manifested ten kinds of clouds of radiant flames from the flowers of various wondrous trees; furthermore, they manifested ten kinds of clouds of radiant flames of all vajras;
furthermore, they manifested ten kinds of clouds of mani-jewel radiant flames proclaiming the boundless practices of bodhisattvas;
furthermore, they manifested ten kinds of clouds of radiant flames of all pearl-lights. Such clouds of radiant flames were as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
The clouds pervaded the entirety of space without dispersing or vanishing. Having manifested these clouds, they paid homage to the Buddha as an act of offering.
Then, in the space above, each transformed themselves into lion thrones made of lotus-treasures that radiated light and proclaimed the sounds of the Buddhas' voices.
Upon those thrones, they sat cross-legged. There were as many such beings as there are atoms in ten billion buddha-fields.
Within the ocean of realms, there were bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten billion buddha-fields.
Each was surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, who had gathered for this assembly.
Each of these bodhisattvas manifested clouds of various offerings, adorned with diverse ornaments as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.

They pervaded all of space without dispersing or extinguishing. Having manifested these clouds, they paid homage to the Buddha as an offering, and then, in the direction from which each had come, they each magically created various lion thrones adorned with jewels.
Upon those thrones, they sat cross-legged.
What follows below concerns the gathering of clouds [of assemblies], which consists of three sections: first, the assembly at the site of enlightenment; second, the manifestation of sovereign power;
and third, the self-description through sound and light. As for those who have gathered, they come from the eight directions, above, and below—thus comprising the ten directions.
Proceeding from the east of this Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean, they circumambulate it to the right in succession, namely, by means of this Vairocana.
The dwelling place of the Tathāgata is the Flower Treasury (Kusumatalagarbha) world-system as its primary realm.
Those gathered there are outside this primary realm, in the ten world-systems of the ten directions; these are also merely cited by their primary realms as forming a single layer of enclosure.
If one considers them to be inexhaustible, then each of those directions likewise has ten such realms, thus layering upon layer like the apertures of Indra’s net.
Therefore, the Sūtra states that there are "oceans of worlds," which is precisely what this scripture explains. Here, we merely cite one instance of these layers to illustrate their inexhaustibility.
Within the clarifications provided in the Sūtra, each direction contains ten matters: first, the determination of the direction; second, the elucidation of the ocean of lands;
third, the differentiation of the names of the worlds; fourth, the presiding Buddha; fifth, the presiding Bodhisattva; sixth, the retinue; seventh...
They arrive at the Buddha’s abode. Eighth, they perform offerings; ninth, they present offerings; tenth, they transform their seats according to their respective directions.
Thus, in each of the ten directions, there are these ten [acts]. Therefore, the concluding summary states:
"In this way, within world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in ten billion buddha-fields, there are bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten billion buddha-fields, each one..."
In each [of these], there were bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds surrounding them in front and behind, who had gathered for this assembly.
Judging by the number established here, the previously mentioned oceans of worlds in the ten directions are actually the worlds situated in immediate succession around the central principal land;
they were merely designated by the name of a single layer. Now, the establishment states "ten billion buddha-fields."
Within oceans of worlds as numerous as atoms of dust, there are thus ten billion world-oceans, each presided over by a Buddha, in every direction.
In this way, their inexhaustibility is made manifest.

Once they were thus seated, from every single pore of the bodies of those bodhisattvas, there manifested ten world-ocean-microdust quantities of all kinds of multicolored light rays made of various jewels.
Within each and every ray of light, there appeared ten world-ocean-microdust quantities of bodhisattvas, all seated upon lion thrones within lotus treasuries. These bodhisattvas—
They are able to enter everywhere into the oceans of all established realms within the entire dharma-realm, down to every single atom.
Within each and every atom, there are vast lands as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-worlds.

Within each of these lands, there are the World-Honored Buddhas of the three periods of time. These Bodhisattvas are able to go everywhere to them, drawing near to serve and make offerings, remaining ever mindful.
In every thought-moment, by means of the dharma-gate that manifests mastery over dreams, he awakens sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
In every thought-moment, by means of the dharma-gate that manifests the death and rebirth of all devas, he awakens sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
In every thought-moment, by means of the dharma-gate that expounds all bodhisattva practices, he awakens sentient beings...

With every thought-moment, he awakens as many sentient beings as there are atoms in an ocean by means of the Dharma-door of the spiritual transformations of praising the Buddha’s merits that universally shake all lands; with every thought-moment,
he awakens as many sentient beings as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds by means of the Dharma-door of manifesting the ocean of all great vows that purifies and adorns all Buddha-lands.

With the dharma-gate of the Buddha’s voice and speech that universally gathers all sentient beings, they awaken as many sentient beings as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds in every thought-moment.

With the dharma-gate of the rain-clouds of all Buddha-dharmas, they awaken as many sentient beings as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds in every thought-moment. With light in every thought-moment...

The Dharma-door of Manifesting Spiritual Transformations that Universally Illuminates the Lands of the Ten Directions and Pervades the Entire Dharmadhātu, awakening world-ocean-microdust numbers of sentient beings in every thought-moment;

and the Dharma-door of the Power of Liberation of All Tathāgatas, Universally Manifesting Buddha-bodies to Pervade the Entire Dharmadhātu, awakening world-ocean-microdust numbers of sentient beings in every thought-moment. In every thought-moment...
By means of the Dharma-door of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva establishing the ocean-like assemblies of all congregations, he awakens sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
In this manner, he pervades the entire dharma-realm, awakening all according to the inclinations of sentient beings' minds.
Within every single thought-moment and in each individual land, he causes sentient beings as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru to attain awakening.
May those who have fallen into the evil realms be forever freed from their suffering.
May each of the sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, who abide in false determination, enter the assembly of right determination.

May each of the sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, be born in the heavens according to their inclinations. May each of the sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, be established in the [Buddha-]voice.
Upon hearing of the stage of the Pratyekabuddha, they caused as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru to serve spiritual friends and fulfill various meritorious practices;
they caused as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru to resolve upon the mind of unsurpassed Bodhi;
and they caused as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru to advance toward the Bodhisattva’s stage of non-retrogression.
They transformed the earth, causing as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru to each attain the pure eye of wisdom and perceive all the equal dharmas seen by the Tathāgata;
they caused as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru to each [attain this].
Abiding in the ocean of all powers and vows, they employ inexhaustible wisdom as their skillful means to purify all Buddha-lands,
causing sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru to each dwell securely in the vast ocean of Vairocana’s vows and be born into the family of the Tathāgata.
The following section reveals the Bodhisattvas who have gathered, each manifesting their sovereign power. Each has eight matters:
first, light is manifested from a single pore; second, within that light, further Bodhisattvas are manifested;
third, the Bodhisattvas within the light each enter into the atoms within the ocean of established dharma-realms; fourth, each of those individual atoms contains vast lands; fifth...
1. Within every single *kṣetra*, there is a Tathāgata. 2. The manifested Bodhisattvas each proceed to the presence of the Tathāgatas to offer worship.
3. They assist the Buddha in proclaiming his transformational teachings. 4. Each one brings about great benefit.

In every moment of thought, they cause sentient beings as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru to be born into the family of the Tathāgata. This commentary fully explains the benefits gained from this emission of light.
Manifesting the inexhaustible, at that time, from within the radiance of all the bodhisattvas, they simultaneously uttered these verses:
"From within all the radiances, wondrous sounds emerge, Pervading all lands throughout the ten directions."
He proclaims the various merits of the Buddha-sons, Who are able to enter the wondrous path to enlightenment;
Practicing through oceans of eons without weariness, He causes suffering sentient beings to attain liberation.
With a mind free from inferiority or fatigue, The Buddha-son skillfully enters these expedient means.
Throughout oceans of kalpas, they cultivate skillful means; There is nothing among all the infinite and boundless dharma-gates that they do not enter.
They constantly proclaim that the nature of all Buddhas of the three periods of time is quiescent;
They cultivate and perfect every single one of their vows until all are exhausted.
Precisely for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, they perform pure deeds as their own practice;
within the assemblies of all Buddhas throughout the ten directions, there is nowhere they do not go,
entering the Tathāgata’s dharma of quiescent extinction by means of the ocean of profound wisdom.
Each and every ray of light is boundless, Entering all inconceivable lands;
The pure eye of wisdom perceives them all— This is the sphere of activity of these Bodhisattvas.
A Bodhisattva can abide upon a single hair-tip, And cause all lands throughout the ten directions to tremble.
They cause sentient beings to have no thoughts of fear; this is the stage of pure skillful means.
Within every single atom, they manifest immeasurable bodies, further appearing in various adorned lands;
in a single thought-moment, they pass away and are born everywhere so that all may see them—those who have attained the adornment of unimpeded wisdom.
All kalpas throughout the three periods of time can be manifested within a single instant;
Knowing that the body is like an illusion, devoid of essence or form, And having realized the unimpeded nature of phenomena (dharmatā),
One is able to enter all the supreme practices of Samantabhadra, Which all sentient beings joyfully desire to behold.
"The Buddha-sons who can abide in this Dharma-gate let out a great roar amidst all the lights.
(This and below describe the sound of the light itself. Since previously the sound of the light issued an invitation, now the sound of the light describes itself.

Because the Bodhisattva’s rank is ultimate and its application is exhaustive in depth and breadth, if it were not described by itself, the assembly at that time would find it difficult to know. There are ten lines of text.)
[Verse: From "Arriving at the midst of all radiances" up to "the great roar of sound.

At that time, the World-Honored One, desiring to cause the entire assembly of bodhisattvas to attain the supernatural power of the Tathāgata’s boundless realm, emitted a light from between his eyebrows.
This light is named "The Radiance of the Wisdom of All Bodhisattvas," and it shines everywhere.

It illuminates the treasuries of the ten directions; its form is like clouds of jewel-colored lamps, universally shining upon all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions, causing the lands therein and all sentient beings to appear clearly.
Furthermore, it causes the entire network of worlds to tremble everywhere.

Within each and every atom, countless Buddhas appear. According to the differing dispositions and desires of sentient beings, they universally rain down clouds of the sublime Dharma wheels of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, revealing the ocean of the Tathāgatas' pāramitās.
Furthermore, they rain down immeasurable clouds of renunciation, causing all sentient beings to forever cross over birth and death. They also rain down clouds of the great vows of all Buddhas.
He manifested the assemblies at the bodhimandas of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Having performed these deeds, he circumambulated the Buddha to the right and entered through the soles of his feet. At that time, a great lotus flower suddenly appeared before the Buddha.
That flower possesses ten kinds of adornments, which no other lotus can equal. That is to say: its stalk is interspersed with various jewels;
its calyx is composed of the sovereign maṇi-jewel kings; all the jewels of the dharma-realm form its petals;
fragrant maṇis constitute its filaments; Jāmbūnada gold adorns its pericarp; and it is graced by exquisite nets.

Covering it above, its radiance and color were pure and clear. Within a single thought-moment, it manifested the infinite spiritual transformations of all Buddhas and was able to universally produce all sounds.
The King of Maṇi Jewels reflected the bodies of the Buddhas, and within those sounds, it was able to universally expound all the practices and vows cultivated by Bodhisattvas.
Once this flower had arisen, in the space of a single thought-moment, at such a [place]...

From within the mark of the white tuft between his brows, there emerged a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Sarvadharmavijayasvara, accompanied by a multitude of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds;
they circumambulated the Tathāgata to the right for immeasurable times.

Having prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, the Bodhisattva Supreme Sound sat upon a lotus pedestal, while the assembly of bodhisattvas sat upon the lotus filaments, each taking their place in succession.
That Bodhisattva Supreme Sound of All Dharmas, having realized the profound realm of reality (*dharmadhātu*), gave rise to great joy;
he entered the wisdom of the Buddha’s sphere of activity, free from doubt or obstruction, and entered the unfathomable Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*) of the Buddha.
O Ocean! You go to the abodes of all Tathāgatas in all lands, manifesting spiritual powers from every pore of your body. In every thought-moment, you universally contemplate the entire dharma-realm.
All Buddhas of the ten directions bestow their power upon you, enabling you to dwell securely in all samādhis until the end of future kalpas.
You constantly behold the bodies of all Buddhas—the ocean of merit within the boundless dharma-realm—and even unto a single...
Regarding all samādhis, liberations, supernormal powers, and transformations, he then, within the assembly, relying on the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power,
surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"The Buddha-body fills the entire Dharma-realm, Universally appearing before all sentient beings."
Responding to conditions and meeting sentient beings, there is nowhere he does not reach; yet he eternally remains upon this seat of Bodhi.
Within each and every pore of the Tathāgata, Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of all lands sit amidst assemblies of Bodhisattvas surrounding him, proclaiming the supreme practices of Samantabhadra.
The Tathāgata sits upon the seat of enlightenment; From a single pore, he manifests oceans of many lands, And from every single pore, it is likewise so;
Thus pervading the entire Dharma-realm, He sits serenely within each and every land, Universally encompassing all buddha-fields.
Bodhisattvas from the ten directions gather like clouds; there are none who do not come to this site of enlightenment.
As numerous as the atoms within all buddha-lands, these oceans of bodhisattvas of merit and radiance are present within the assembly of the Tathāgata, pervading the entire realm of phenomena.
Within every atom of the Dharma-realm and all its lands, he appears before all assemblies;
such is the realm of his wisdom of emanations.
Within the congregations of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas of supreme wisdom sit together in harmony, established through the practices of Samantabhadra.
Each listening to the Dharma, they give rise to joy; Practicing everywhere for immeasurable eons, they have already entered the vast vows of Samantabhadra.
Each giving birth to all Buddha-dharmas within the ocean of Vairocana’s teachings, Through practice, they shall realize the stage of the Tathāgata.
Awakened by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, praised and rejoiced in by all Tathāgatas,
you have attained the great supernormal powers of all Buddhas; you circulate throughout the entire Dharma-realm without exception,
and within every atom of all buddha-fields, clouds of manifested bodies constantly appear, filling them all.
Universally for the sake of all sentient beings, he emits great light, raining down the rain of Dharma upon each according to their inclinations.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named King of the Lotus Light Wisdom Who Observes All Supreme Dharmas.
Empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, he surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
The Tathāgata’s profound wisdom universally enters the Dharma-realm; Able to turn in accordance with the three periods of time, he serves as the guiding light for the world.

All Buddhas share the same Dharma-body; Without dependence and without distinction, they accord with the inclinations of all sentient beings, Causing them to perceive the physical form of the Buddha, Endowed with all-encompassing wisdom.
Thoroughly knowing all phenomena within all lands, there is nothing in which the Buddha’s body and radiance do not appear;

his physical marks are inconceivable, and he causes all sentient beings who have faith and joy to see them according to their needs. From the body of a single Buddha, he manifests as immeasurable Buddhas.
The thunderous voice pervades all lands, expounding the Dharma as deep as the ocean.
From within every single pore, nets of light pervade the ten directions, proclaiming the Buddha’s wondrous sounds to tame those who are difficult to tame.
Within the Tathāgata’s radiance, profound and sublime sounds constantly emerge, praising the ocean of the Buddha’s merits.
As well as the practices of the Bodhisattvas, the Buddha turns the wheel of the True Dharma;
the teachings he proclaims are immeasurable, boundless, and peerless, such that those of shallow wisdom cannot fathom them.
Throughout all worlds, he manifests his body and attains perfect enlightenment, performing miraculous transformations in each, filling the entire realm of phenomena.
The Tathāgata, in each and every body, manifests Buddhas equal in number to all sentient beings; throughout all lands as numerous as atoms, he universally displays his supernormal powers.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Dharmaprītiprajñāprabha, who, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power...
The deity surveyed the ten directions and spoke these verses:
The Buddha’s body is ever manifest, Pervading the entirety of the Dharma-realm.
He constantly emits a vast sound That universally shakes the lands of the ten directions. The Tathāgata manifests his body everywhere, Entering throughout all worlds.
In accordance with the inclinations and desires of sentient beings, he manifests his supernormal powers.
The Buddha appears before all beings according to their minds; whatever they behold is entirely the Buddha’s spiritual power, boundless in its radiance.
His preaching of the Dharma is likewise immeasurable, as the sons of the Buddha perceive it according to their own wisdom.
Able to enter and able to observe that the Buddha-body is without birth, yet is able to manifest birth;
the nature of phenomena is like empty space, wherein all Buddhas dwell—dwelling nowhere and going nowhere, yet seen everywhere.
Their radiance is all-pervading, and their fame is heard afar.
Without essence and without abiding place, Nor is there any birth to be found; Formless and shapeless, all that appears is like a shadow.
The Buddha, in accordance with the minds of sentient beings, Raises great clouds of Dharma through various gates of skillful means, Manifesting realization to discipline them throughout all worlds.
I see the Buddha seated at the site of enlightenment, surrounded by a great assembly;

his body illuminates the lands of the ten directions, and all the bodies of the Buddhas possess inexhaustible marks. Though he manifests immeasurable forms and features, they are ultimately never exhausted.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another bodhisattva-mahāsattva named Fragrant Flame Light Universal Radiance Wisdom.
Empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, he surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
The bodhisattvas in this assembly have entered the inconceivable stages of the Buddha; each and every one is able to perceive the spiritual powers of all Buddhas.
With their bodies of wisdom, they are able to enter everywhere; within the atoms of all lands, they see their own bodies therein.
They behold all Buddhas universally, appearing in all lands like reflections.
Within all the abodes of all Tathāgatas, and within all those [realms], he manifests all miraculous deeds;
having purified the various practices and vows of Samantabhadra until they are clear and pure, he is able to universally behold the spiritual transformations of the Buddhas in all lands;
his body dwells in all places, and all are entirely equal.
With wisdom acting thus, they enter the realm of the Buddha; having realized the Tathāgata’s wisdom, they illuminate the entire dharma-realm equally.
They universally enter the pores of the Buddha and, throughout all oceans of lands and all buddha-fields, manifest supernormal powers and display various forms.
And various names and titles— within a single moment, they can universally manifest all spiritual transformations,
attain perfect enlightenment at the site of awakening, and turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma.
Within the samādhis of the bodhisattvas, they can manifest in a single thought-moment all the vast lands throughout inconceivable billions of eons.
In all Buddha-lands, every single bodhisattva universally enters the body of the Buddha,
which is boundless and inexhaustible.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another bodhisattva mahāsattva named Siṃhavikrāntamati-prabhāsa (Lion-Leap Wisdom Radiance), who, having received...
The Buddha, by his majestic spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
The Buddha Vairocana is able to turn the wheel of the true Dharma;
Throughout all lands of the Dharma-realm, he is as pervasive as clouds. Within the ten directions, there exist All the great oceans of worlds.
Through the Buddha’s supernormal powers and the force of his vows, he turns the wheel of Dharma everywhere.
Within the vast assemblies in all buddha-fields, his names differ according to each realm; he expounds the wondrous Dharma in accordance with the needs of beings.
This great majestic power of the Tathāgata is accomplished through the vows of Samantabhadra throughout all lands.
The wondrous voice reaches everywhere; the Buddha’s body is equal to the atoms of all lands.
Universally raining down the rain of Dharma, it is unborn and without distinction, appearing throughout all worlds.
Within all the atoms of lands across countless billions of eons, the deeds performed in the past are fully proclaimed by that wondrous voice.
Throughout the lands as numerous as atoms in the ten directions, A net of light pervades them all.
Within that light, every Buddha appears, Universally transforming all living beings. The bodies of these Buddhas are without distinction, Filling the entire Dharma-realm.
They cause sentient beings to behold their form-bodies, Skillfully subduing them according to their capacities, Throughout all lands of the three periods of time.
All the various teachers, distinguished by their diverse names, have all been made to see— through this teaching—
the past, future, and present; they shall all hear the sublime wheel of Dharma turned by all the Tathāgatas within this assembly.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another bodhisattva mahāsattva named Dharmasāgaraprajñāguṇagarbha.
Empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, he surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
All these sons of the Buddhas in this assembly have skillfully cultivated manifold wisdoms; these people are already able to enter such gates of expedient means.

Within each and every land, they universally proclaim the vast sound that expounds the spheres of the Buddha’s conduct, heard throughout the lands of the ten directions within each and every thought-moment.
Universally observing all phenomena, Abiding securely in the stage of True Suchness (tathatā),
Thoroughly comprehending the ocean of all dharmas within each and every Buddha-body— For inconceivable billions of eons,
They have cultivated the perfections (pāramitās) and purified the buddha-fields; Within each and every atom, They are able to realize all dharmas.
Thus, being without obstruction, they travel throughout the lands of the ten directions;
They visit every single Buddha-field without exception, Beholding the supernatural powers of the Buddhas and entering the sphere of their practice.
The vast voices of all Buddhas throughout the Dharma-realm—there is none they do not hear— And Bodhisattvas are able to fully comprehend them.
Skillfully entering the ocean of sounds, they proclaim wondrous voices throughout oceans of eons. Their voices are equal and without distinction;

their wisdom pervades the three periods of time. Entering that stage of vocal resonance, they attain the wisdom of sound regarding all voices of sentient beings as well as the sovereign voices of Buddhas, understanding them all completely.
Attaining stage after stage, dwelling within the stages of power, such is the Dharma obtained through diligent cultivation over billions of eons.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another bodhisattva mahāsattva named Universal Radiance of the Lamp of Wisdom. Empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, he [spoke].
Surveying the ten directions, he spoke in verse:
All Tathāgatas are far removed from all marks; If one can know this Dharma, one sees the Teacher of the World.
Within the samādhi of the Bodhisattva, The light of wisdom is universally clear and bright.
Able to know the sovereign nature of all Buddhas, One who sees the true body of the Buddha awakens to the profound Dharma;
Universally observing the dharma-realm, They assume bodies according to their vows,
born from an ocean of merit, Abiding securely on the ground of wisdom, And examining all phenomena.
Practicing the most supreme path within all Buddha-fields, In the manner of all Tathāgatas,
thus pervading the Dharma-realm, One perceives the true essence everywhere; Having diligently practiced for billions of eons throughout the vast lands of the ten directions,
One is able to traverse the ocean of all phenomena And sport within the state of the Perfectly Enlightened One.
The sole firm and solid body is seen within all atoms; Unborn and without marks, it appears universally in all lands.

According to the minds of sentient beings, it appears before them all, Manifesting various means of subduing them, Swiftly causing them to turn toward the Buddha-way, By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power.
The appearance of all bodhisattvas is sustained by the power of the Buddhas; they behold all Tathāgatas,
the teachers of all multitudes, who possess immeasurable majestic spiritual power and awaken all bodhisattvas throughout the entire dharma-realm.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another bodhisattva mahāsattva named Universal Wisdom of the Flower Flame Topknot.
Sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, he surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
Throughout all lands, he universally proclaims subtle and wondrous sounds;
He extols the Buddha’s merits, filling the entire dharma-realm. The Buddha takes the Dharma as his body; Pure as empty space, yet manifesting various forms and colors.
He causes beings to enter this Dharma; If there are those with deep faith and joy, [they shall attain it].
And those who are sustained by the Buddha—know that such persons are able to give rise to the wisdom of a Buddha.
Those with little wisdom cannot understand this Dharma; only those with the pure eye of wisdom can see it.
Through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, they observe all phenomena.
When entering and when departing, all that is seen is clearly understood. Among all dharmas, there are no limits to the Dharma-gates;
one accomplishes all-knowledge. Entering the deep ocean of Dharma, one dwells securely in the Buddha-lands;
giving rise to all-knowledge, there is neither going nor coming.
Such is the nature of all Buddhas: The ocean of all sentient beings, The Buddha-body appears like a reflection, Differing according to their respective understandings; Thus do they see the Guide.
From every single pore, He manifests various supernormal powers; Those who have purified themselves through the practice Of Samantabhadra’s vows are able to see him.
With each and every body, the Buddha turns the wheel of Dharma everywhere; it pervades the entire dharma-realm, beyond the reach of thought.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another bodhisattva-mahāsattva named Inexhaustible Light of Majestic Virtue and Wisdom, who, having received the Buddha’s...
With majestic spiritual power, he surveyed the ten directions and spoke these verses:
Within each and every buddha-field, He sits at the site of enlightenment everywhere, Surrounded by assemblies of followers, Having utterly subdued the armies of Māra.
The Buddha’s body emits radiant light, Pervading and filling the ten directions.
Manifesting in accordance with what is appropriate, The forms and appearances are not of a single kind;

Within each and every atom, Radiant light completely fills them all. Universally beholding the lands of the ten directions, With their various distinct differences— The oceans of lands throughout the ten directions, Consisting of all manner of infinite realms, Are entirely level and pure.
Composed of sapphire, they may be positioned above or alongside; some resemble closed lotuses, while others are circular or square.
With all manner of diverse forms and characteristics, they traverse the lands of the entire dharma-realm without obstruction.
Within every assembly, they constantly turn the sublime wheel of Dharma.
The Buddha’s body is inconceivable; all lands are contained within it.

In every such place, he guides the world by proclaiming the true Dharma. The wondrous wheel of Dharma that he turns is based on the single principle of reality, wherein the nature of phenomena is without distinction;
with his perfect voice, he expounds the characteristics of all dharmas.
Elucidating the principle of ultimate reality according to the distinctions of their understanding,
he manifests inexhaustible Dharma-gates throughout all buddha-fields; therein one sees the Buddha seated at the site of enlightenment, his body appearing like a reflection,
wherein neither arising nor ceasing can be apprehended.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another bodhisattva mahāsattva named Dharmadhātu-samantāloka-mati.
Empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, he surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
The subtle and wondrous body of the Tathāgata, Its form and characteristics are inconceivable; Those who see it give rise to joy, reverence, faith, and delight in the Dharma.
Every single mark upon the Buddha’s body Manifests infinite Buddhas, Universally entering the worlds of the ten directions;
Within each and every atom, Are oceans of lands throughout the ten directions.
The immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, in every single thought-moment, each manifest their spiritual powers;
the Bodhisattvas of great wisdom have deeply entered the ocean of Dharma. Sustained by the power of the Buddhas, they are able to know these skillful means.
If there are those who already dwell securely in all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, [they shall likewise attain this].
Beholding all those buddha-fields through the spiritual power of all Buddhas— if a person possesses faith and understanding,
as well as great vows, is endowed with profound wisdom, and has mastered all phenomena,
they will be able to examine each and every body of the Buddhas, without any obstruction regarding form or sound.
Thoroughly comprehending all objects, they are able to abide within the bodies of all Buddhas;
swiftly entering the stage of the Tathāgata through the range of their wisdom, they universally encompass the entire Dharma-realm.
Within a single thought-instant, they are able to manifest all such lands—as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field—within each and every atom.
All lands and all matters of supernatural power are entirely manifested within a single field;
such is the power of the Bodhisattva.
At that time, among the assembly, there was another Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Vīryabalāpratihatamati, who, having received the Buddha’s...
With majestic spiritual power, he surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
The Buddha utters a single wondrous sound, Which is heard throughout the lands of the ten directions; All voices are fully contained within it, And the rain of Dharma fills everywhere.
It is an ocean of all speech and expression, A voice that accords with every kind of being.
Throughout all Buddha-fields, they turn the pure wheel of Dharma;
In all lands, they behold the Buddha’s miraculous transformations And hear the sound of the Buddha preaching the Dharma. Having heard it, they proceed toward Bodhi;
throughout the various lands of the Dharma-realm, Within each and every atom, lies the power of the Tathāgata’s liberation.
Manifesting bodies everywhere therein, the Dharma-body is identical to space;
Unimpeded and without distinction, its forms and colors appear like reflections, Displaying a manifold variety of marks.
These reflections have no location, being like space and devoid of intrinsic nature; The person of vast wisdom Thoroughly realizes their equality.
The Buddha-body is ungraspable; It is without birth and without arising or action.

Appearing universally before all things according to their needs, it is as equal as space. All Buddhas throughout the ten directions Entirely enter into a single pore, Each manifesting their own supernatural powers;
Only those with the eye of wisdom can perceive this— Such is the Buddha Vairocana.
The power of their vows pervades the entire Dharma-realm; throughout all lands, they constantly turn the unsurpassed wheel.
Within a single hair-pore they manifest spiritual transformations, which all Buddhas proclaim together;
even after passing through immeasurable eons, one cannot reach their limit.
Thus, within the site of enlightenment in this four-continent world-system, by the spiritual power of the Buddha,
there assembled from each of the ten directions bodhisattva hosts as numerous as the atoms in ten million world-oceans.
It should be known that it is exactly the same in every site of enlightenment within every four-continent world-system throughout all world-oceans.
The fourth major section below concerns the manifestation of auspicious omens to symbolize the Dharma. The signs manifested above merely summoned those with a karmic connection;
now that the assembly has gathered and the ocean of Dharma is about to be expounded, these omens are manifested once more. There are three parts to the description of these omens:

first, light reveals the Master of the Dharma, desiring to cause the great assembly to attain the supernatural powers of the Tathāgata; next, flowers appear to symbolize the meaning, which is universal...
Because it manifests the Buddha’s *Avataṃsaka* as that which is expressed; third, it manifests the teaching through the assembly, for the Dharma relies upon people for its propagation.

Regarding the light shining throughout the ten directions and entering from beneath the feet: the feet symbolize that which the Buddha treads upon, signifying that the fruit-wisdom of the Middle Way serves as the essence of the *dharmadhātu*, which is what the Bodhisattvas tread upon by means of realization and entry. Thereupon, a great lotus flower suddenly appeared...
It appears. However, the lotus flower also specifically symbolizes the Flower Treasury World (*Puṣpakaraṇḍa*), which has been purified by the Buddha.

Its sudden appearance signifies that phenomena arise based on principle, and thus it is difficult to fathom. The adornment of the lotus fully represents the essence of the fruition-body (*phala-kāya*) as perfected through adornment;
therefore, after the flowers have emerged, the fact that a bodhisattva emerges from within the white tuft of hair between the eyebrows signifies that the wisdom of fruition serves as the cause.
Regarding the phrase "named Supreme Sound" (*Suśvara*): it is called "Supreme Sound" because the teachings it expounds are perfect and complete.

The phrase "together with his retinue" indicates that this Perfect Teaching (*paripūrṇa-deśanā*) subsumes all other scriptures as its retinue. Subsequently, the one named Supreme Sound spoke verses in praise of the Buddha;
in order to extol the Buddha’s virtues, he expressed himself to the full extent of his capacity, manifesting his own boundless devotion.
To manifest the boundless virtues of the Buddha, he observes the ten directions and speaks these verses.

Within these verses, the Buddha is praised in general terms, while also implicitly containing various questions; the commentary (*śāstra*) assigns each section to its respective subject. First, regarding the bodhisattvas emerging from between the eyebrows:
they praise the bodhisattvas of the ten directions, with each one individually reciting a verse of praise. This constitutes ten sections, each differing in its specific praise.

He constantly extols the merits of the Buddha. The conclusion states that throughout every ocean of worlds, in each and every site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) within the four continents, it is exactly the same, thereby manifesting the single essence of the *dharmadhātu*.

Above this, the conclusion further states that from each of the ten directions, there have come and gathered like clouds assemblies of bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in a billion oceans of worlds.
He then universally employed the previously manifested light to summon assemblies from each of the ten directions, numbering as many as the atoms within a billion-world-ocean of worlds.

His intention was that while this single four-continent world-system possesses such a site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), every world within each of those oceans of worlds likewise contains four continents;
that each such assembly is precisely intended to manifest the layered relationship between the principal and the retinue.

[This section is] weighty, for it is a chorus sung in unison throughout the ten directions. However, by deeply contemplating the concluding text, one will naturally perceive its inexhaustible meaning.
The "Distant Expedients" chapter ends; the "Tathāgata Manifests His Signs" chapter ends.
Essential Summary of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Fascicle Six;
Essential Summary of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Fascicle Seven.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a śramaṇa from the Kingdom of Khotan.
Commentary by the Śramaṇa Chengguan of Qingliangshan Dàhuáyan Monastery;

Chapter Three: The Samādhi of Samantabhadra.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra sat upon a lion throne within the Lotus Treasury before the Tathāgata.
Empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, he entered a samādhi called "The Body-Treasury of Vairocana, the Tathāgata of All Buddhas.
This samādhi universally enters into the equality of all Buddhas and is able to manifest manifold reflections throughout the Dharma-realm.
These images are vast and unimpeded, equal to empty space. They enter into every turning of the ocean of the dharma-realm without exception.

They give birth to all dharmas of samādhi and are universally able to encompass the dharma-realm of the ten directions. The ocean of the light of wisdom of all Buddhas of the three periods of time arises from them.
All oceans of established realms throughout the ten directions can be manifested within them. They contain and preserve all things.
The power of all Buddhas liberates the wisdom of all Bodhisattvas, enabling them to universally contain within the motes of dust of all lands the boundless Dharma-realm;
to accomplish the ocean of all Buddha-merits; to manifest the ocean of all Tathāgatas’ great vows;
and to ensure that all wheels of Dharma turned by all Buddhas are circulated and upheld without interruption. Thus, in this world...
Within this realm, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva entered this samādhi before the World-Honored One.

Thus, throughout the entire Dharma-realm and the space-realm—in the ten directions and the three periods of time—within all subtle, unobstructed, and vast luminous lands seen by the Buddha-eye, reached by the Buddha’s power, and manifested by the Buddha’s body, as well as every single atom within these lands: each and every one...
Within the dust motes, there are Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds. In each of these fields, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.

Before each Buddha, there are Samantabhadra Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, all of whom have likewise entered this Samādhi of the Treasury Body of Vairocana Tathāgata of All Buddhas. At that time, one...
Before each of these Samantabhadra Bodhisattvas, all the Buddhas of the ten directions appeared.
Those Tathāgatas spoke with one voice, praising them: "Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You are able to enter this Samādhi of the Bodhisattva Vairocana-Tathāgata-Garbha-Kāya of all Buddhas. O Son of the Buddha, this is [the power] of all the Buddhas of the ten directions..."
All Buddhas bestow their collective empowerment upon you, by virtue of the power of the original vows of Tathāgata Vairocana,
and also by the power of your own cultivation of the practices and vows of all Buddhas. That is to say, you are able to turn the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas,
to reveal and manifest the ocean of wisdom of all Tathāgatas, and to universally illumine, without exception, all the oceans of established worlds throughout the ten directions.
Therefore, it causes all sentient beings to purify their defilements and attain purity; it universally encompasses all great lands without attachment;
it enters deeply into the spheres of all Buddhas without obstruction; it universally manifests the merits of all Buddhas;
and it is able to enter the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena, increasing wisdom. Thus it observes...
Because he has mastered all dharma-gates; because he thoroughly understands the faculties of all sentient beings;

and because he is able to uphold the ocean of the scriptural teachings of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas—at that time, all the Buddhas of the ten directions immediately bestowed upon the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra the wisdom-power of entering the nature of omniscience, the wisdom of entering the boundless measure of the Dharma-realm, and [the wisdom of]...
They attain the wisdom that accomplishes the realm of all Buddhas; they are granted the wisdom that knows the formation and destruction of all oceans of worlds;

they are granted the wisdom that knows the vastness of all realms of sentient beings; they are granted the wisdom of the various samādhis that abide in the non-differentiated, profound liberation of all Buddhas;
they are granted the wisdom that enters the ocean of the faculties of all Bodhisattvas; and they are granted the wisdom that knows the speech of all sentient beings.
The wisdom of eloquence for turning the wheel of Dharma like the ocean; the wisdom of the body that universally enters all oceans of worlds within the Dharma-realm;

and the wisdom of attaining the voices of all Buddhas—just as the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra received such wisdom before the Tathāgatas in this world-system, so too did he receive it in all oceans of worlds and in each individual world-ocean therein.
All that exists within a single atom of Samantabhadra is likewise so. Why is this? Because the nature of phenomena is such when one realizes that samādhi.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions each extended their right hands and stroked the crown of the head of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

Those hands were all adorned with the marks and signs of excellence; they emitted wonderful nets of light, flowed with fragrances, and radiated flames. Furthermore, from them issued forth the various [teachings] of the Buddhas.
The wondrous voice and the matters of sovereign spiritual powers; the ocean of Samantabhadra vows of all bodhisattvas of the past, present, and future;
the pure wheels of Dharma of all Tathāgatas; and all the images of the Buddhas of the three periods of time—all these appeared therein.
Just as in this world, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra is touched on the crown of his head by the Buddhas of the ten directions, so too...

In all these oceans of worlds, and within every single atom of those oceans of worlds, all Samantabhadras likewise have their heads stroked by the Buddhas of the ten directions. At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra arose from this samādhi.
Upon arising from this samādhi, he immediately [manifested] from as many atoms as there are in all the oceans of worlds.

They arise from the ocean-gates of samādhi; that is to say, they arise from the samādhi-gate of skillful wisdom that knows the moments of thought throughout the three periods of time are without distinction;
they arise from the samādhi-gate that knows all atoms within the entire dharma-realm of the three periods of time;
they arise from the samādhi-gate that manifests all buddha-lands of the three periods of time; they arise from the samādhi-gate that manifests the dwellings of all sentient beings.
It arises from the gate of samādhi that knows the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings;

it arises from the gate of samādhi that knows the individual names of all sentient beings; it arises from the gate of samādhi that knows the distinct locations and positions throughout the dharma-realm of the ten directions;
it arises from the gate of samādhi that knows that within every single atom there are clouds of infinite, vast Buddha-bodies.
They arise from the gateways of samādhi. They arise from the gateway of the samādhi that expounds the ocean of principles of all dharmas.

When Samantabhadra Bodhisattva arises from such gateways of samādhi, each of those bodhisattvas individually attains oceans of clouds of samādhis as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, oceans of clouds of dhāraṇīs as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, and [oceans of clouds of... world...
Clouds of oceans of skillful means for all phenomena, as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of realms; clouds of oceans of gateways of eloquence, as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds;
clouds of oceans of spiritual practices, as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds;

clouds of oceans of the light of wisdom from the treasuries of merit of all Tathāgatas who universally illumine the dharma-realm, as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds. [As numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds...]
The ocean-clouds of the skillful means of all Tathāgatas’ powers and wisdom, which are without distinction;
within each and every pore of all Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, there appear clouds of many oceans of lands.

Within each and every one of these oceans of lands, as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, each Bodhisattva manifests the descent from the Tuṣita heaven, the birth in this world, the attainment of Buddhahood, and the turning of the wheel of the True Dharma.
Through the ocean-clouds of the turning of the Wheel of Dharma, the parinirvāṇa, and so forth,
the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra arose from samādhi within this world-system, and the assembly of bodhisattvas obtained such benefits. In the same manner,
it was likewise throughout all oceans of world-systems and within every single atom of those oceans of world-systems.

The purpose of this chapter’s introduction is as follows: since the previous assembly has already gathered and light has manifested the Dharma Lord, and he is now about to preach the Dharma, the Dharma Lord enters meditative absorption (*samādhi*) to receive empowerment as a proximate means (*upāya*).
Because he preaches immediately upon emerging from absorption, the *samādhi* is considered the proximate cause.
As for the title of the chapter, "Puxian" (Samantabhadra), it clarifies that the Dharma Lord preaches the Universal Dharma (*samanta-dharma*), and thus [the chapter is named after] the *samādhi*.
This is the function of karma; it is not proclaimed unless there is realization. This, then, is the simultaneous presentation of person and dharma.
Regarding the statement that the name of the samādhi is the "Vairocana Tathāgata-garbha-body": *vairo* means vast and great; *loca* means birth.
That is volition (*cetanā*). Because compassion is boundless, it is called "vast" (*vipula*); because wisdom is unsurpassed, it is termed "great" (*mahat*).
Because the perception of birth has been exhausted, it is said that "birth has ceased. Because one has departed from existence and dwells eternally in *nirvāṇa*, one is called a Tathāgata.
To contain and encompass ten thousand virtues is called the "Treasury Body" (*garbhakośa-kāya*); this is precisely the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*) that has emerged from its entanglements.
Because this Dharma-body is the very substance of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), it is termed the "Treasury Body. This means that the Dharma-bodies of all Buddhas pervade the entire Dharma-realm;
within each atom, they further contain all lands, layer upon layer without end. This clarifies that the body which pervades all lands encompasses all that is pervaded.

The oceans of lands are all, without exception, contained within the body of the Tathāgata; therefore, it is called the "Treasury Body" (*garbha-kāya*). There are four propositions regarding this pervasive integration:
first, the body pervades the oceans of lands; second, the lands are within the body; third, the body pervades the lands within the body; fourth, the lands enter and pervade the bodies of the lands.
Thus, interior and exterior are identical, and the primary and secondary realms are blended in harmony, free from obstruction or hindrance. This is the third [point].
It is named for its subtle functioning; thus, intending to expound this Dharma, he enters this samādhi. The Buddha’s nature of equality is the Tathāgatagarbha;
therefore, by entering solely into the body of the Tathāgatagarbha, one has already entered the equality of the Buddhas.
Therefore, the subsequent text states: "In this world-system, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva enters samādhi before the World-Honored One.

Likewise, throughout the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space—in all ten directions and the three periods of time—there are all lands seen by the Buddha-eye, reached by the Buddha’s power, and manifested by the Buddha-body, which are subtle, unimpeded, vast, and luminous. And...
Within every single atom of this land, there are Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.
Within each of these fields, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.
Before each of these Buddhas, there is a Samantabhadra Bodhisattva as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds; all of them likewise enter into this Vairocana of all Buddhas.

In the Samādhi of Concealing the Body, before each and every Samantabhadra, all the Buddhas of the ten directions appear before them and praise the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra for being able to enter this samādhi.
This very samādhi already manifests the infinite, multilayered nature of the Dharma-realm.
These praises by the Buddhas serve to manifest the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of the Buddhas; this is "vocal empowerment" (*vāg-adhiṣṭhāna*). This will be explained in the following text.
At that time, all Buddhas of the ten directions immediately bestowed upon Samantabhadra Bodhisattva the great wisdom capable of entering all-knowledge;
this is the empowerment of mind (*cittādhiṣṭhāna*). Next, each of the Buddhas of the ten directions extended their right hand and stroked the crown of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s head;
this is the empowerment of body (*kāyādhiṣṭhāna*). Then, the general conclusion states: "In this world, the Buddhas of the ten directions stroked [the crown of] Samantabhadra..."
Worthy One, within every single atom of all world-oceans, there are Samantabhadras who are all touched on the crown of their heads by the Buddhas of the ten directions.
This passage generally clarifies the "Section on Empowerment.
Below this, at the time when the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra arises from samādhi—specifically, at the moment of arising from this samādhi—he emerges from the atoms of all world-oceans.
The gates of the ocean of samādhis arise in numberless ways, causing all bodhisattvas to each obtain the benefit of the Dharma.
To conclude this universal application, it says: "In this world, and even throughout all those oceans of worlds, within every single atom, it is exactly like this."
At that time, by the majestic spiritual power of all Buddhas and the power of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s samādhi, all the oceans of worlds in the ten directions trembled slightly.
Each world was adorned with various jewels and emitted sublime sounds proclaiming all dharmas.
Furthermore, within the ocean-like assemblies of all Tathāgatas’ places of enlightenment, ten kinds [of rain] fell everywhere.
The clouds of the great maṇi-kings. What are the ten? They are: the cloud of the maṇi-king *Sūkṣma-tārā-vicitra-dhvaja*; the cloud of the maṇi-king whose radiance shines brilliantly;
the cloud of the maṇi-king from which jewel wheels hang down; the cloud of the maṇi-king manifesting the images of bodhisattvas from within treasuries of various jewels;
the cloud of the maṇi-king that proclaims the names of the Buddhas; and the cloud [of the maṇi-king] whose light is blazing and illuminates everywhere.
Clouds of mani-kings at the sites of enlightenment in all buddha-fields; clouds of mani-kings with various transformations whose light illuminates the ten directions;
clouds of mani-kings praising the merits of all bodhisattvas; clouds of mani-kings like the blazing intensity of the sun’s rays;
clouds of mani-kings whose delightful music is heard throughout the ten directions—raining down these ten [types of clouds] everywhere.
Having thus produced clouds of great maṇi-kings, all the Tathāgatas emitted rays of light from every pore of their bodies.
Within those rays of light, they spoke these verses:
Samantabhadra dwells universally in all lands, Seated upon jeweled lotuses, beheld by all;
All supernatural powers he manifests, And enters into infinite samādhis.
With various bodies, Samantabhadra Constantly flows throughout the entire Dharma-realm, filling it completely.
Through the power of samādhi, supernormal knowledges, and skillful means, you proclaim the universal sound with total unimpededness.
In the presence of all Buddhas throughout every land, you manifest various samādhis and supernormal powers;
each and every such power pervades everywhere throughout the lands of the ten directions, leaving none untouched.
Just as in all lands where Tathāgatas dwell, so it is within every mote of dust in those lands;
the manifestations of samādhi and supernormal powers are all through the power of Vairocana’s vows.
The body of Samantabhadra is like space; abiding in reality, it is not a land.
According to the desires of the minds of all sentient beings, he manifests bodies equal in number to all things;
Samantabhadra abides in all great vows and has attained this immeasurable power of spiritual transformations.
Within every buddha-field belonging to all buddhas, he manifests his form and proceeds to each one.
The oceans of all assemblies are boundless, And the emanated bodies dwelling therein are likewise immeasurable.
The lands manifested are all adorned and pure; Within a single kṣaṇa, many eons are seen.
Samantabhadra dwells peacefully in all lands, Manifesting spiritual powers beyond compare.
Shaking the ten directions so that there is nowhere it does not reach, Causing all who behold it to perceive the power of the merit of all Buddhas' wisdom;
With various great dharmas all brought to fulfillment through the skillful means of diverse samādhis, He reveals his own past practices for enlightenment.
Thus, this sovereign and inconceivable [power] manifests throughout all lands of the ten directions to reveal the universal entry into all samādhis;
within clouds of Buddha-light, his merits are praised.
At that time, the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas turned toward Samantabhadra, joined their palms, and gazed up at him; empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, they were all of one mind.
He praised him with these words:
"Born from the teachings of all Buddhas, Arisen through the power of the Tathāgata’s vows,
The treasury of space, equal to True Suchness— You have already purified this Dharma-body."
Within the assemblies of all Buddha-fields, Samantabhadra dwells everywhere;
he who is the radiance of the ocean of merit and wisdom shines equally throughout the ten directions so that there is nowhere he is not seen.
Samantabhadra’s vast ocean of great merit pervades the ten directions, traveling everywhere to draw near to the Buddhas.
All the lands existing within every atom, you are able to go to them all and manifest clearly;
O Son of the Buddha, we have always seen you,
having personally attended upon all the Tathāgatas and dwelling within the true realm of samādhi for as many eons as there are atoms in all lands.
The Sons of the Buddha, with their universally pervasive bodies, Go to all lands throughout the ten directions to deliver the ocean of sentient beings;
There is not a single atom of the Dharma-realm that they do not enter, Entering into every atom within the Dharma-realm; Their bodies are inexhaustible and without distinction.
Just as empty space is all-pervasive, so too does he proclaim the vast Dharma of the Tathāgata;
He who is the light of all merits proceeds like a great cloud to the oceans of sentient beings— vast, powerful,
and most excellent— to preach the peerless Dharma practiced by the Buddha.
To deliver sentient beings throughout oceans of kalpas, you have cultivated all the supreme practices of Samantabhadra;
you manifest all dharmas like a great cloud, and your vast voice is heard everywhere.
How are these lands established? And how do the Buddhas appear?
And for the sake of the ocean of all sentient beings, I pray that you will explain this according to its true meaning.
Here, this immeasurable ocean of the great assembly all stands before the Honored One in reverent attendance.
To turn the pure and wondrous wheel of Dharma, may all Buddhas rejoice in this.

The following section is the "Manifestation of Signs as Proof. Because the Bodhisattvas of the ten directions attained benefit and their minds were filled with joy, the earth shook and various auspicious omens appeared.
Since the members of this assembly attained realization upon hearing [the teaching] at its conclusion, the manifestation of omens as proof is placed later.

Although the members of this assembly have not yet heard [the teaching], they have already attained benefit; therefore, the omens appear first. This is because this assembly distinguishes the fruit and manifests its excellence.

Therefore, the supplementary commentary states: because at the beginning of this dharma of the fruit, the assembly in the ocean did not speak but made their request, and although the Tathāgata commanded Samantabhadra to preach by merely bestowing light upon him, there was as yet no verbal command; thus, Samantabhadra now enters this Tathāgata...
The Samādhi of the Body of the Tathāgatagarbha: this very samādhi already manifests the entire substance of the inexhaustible Dharma-realm.
Therefore, although nothing is explicitly stated, the answer is already fully revealed. Thus, the ocean-like assembly of beings from the ten directions does not need to wait for words;
they first silently realize the ineffable essence. This is the conclusion of Samantabhadra’s exposition, whereby the ocean-like assembly attains [realization].
The earth quakes and auspicious omens appear to testify to this benefit. Therefore, next, light is emitted from every pore of all the Tathāgatas;
within that light, verses are spoken to praise their virtues, thereby extolling Samantabhadra, who is the master of the teaching on the profound penetration of the Dharma-realm.
Thus, next, all the Bodhisattvas, having heard the verses within the light...
They praise the virtues of Samantabhadra. Although they had previously obtained benefits, they did not know the source from which those benefits arose;

now, however, they realize they were obtained from Samantabhadra. Therefore, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, they all turn toward Samantabhadra and, with one voice, speak verses in praise and entreaty.
The ten stanzas are divided into three parts: the first part provides a general summary of the preceding meditative concentration; the next eight [stanzas] provide specific [details].

This reveals the pervasive characteristic. The final section concludes with praise for the reasons [for this teaching]: because one is inwardly capable of receiving the Dharma and outwardly has the Buddhas rejoicing in it, one ought to preach it.
Thus ends the "Chapter on Samantabhadra’s Samādhi."
The Fourth Chapter: The Accomplishment of the World (*Lokadhātu-saṃpad*).
Regarding the purpose of this chapter’s introduction: since the conditions previously explained have been fulfilled, what follows herein correctly sets forth that which was to be taught.

It provides a general clarification of the characteristics of the fruit and specifically answers the questions concerning the ocean-like establishment of the *dharmadhātu*; thus, this chapter is introduced. The subsequent "Chapter on the Treasury of Flowers" (*Kusuma-kośa*) serves as its specific [subsequent] section.

This elucidates the adornment and purity of the Original Teacher. This chapter serves as a general exposition of the characteristics of the fruit of all Buddhas. Regarding the explanation of the term "world" (*loka*):

"world" (*loka*) refers to the three periods of time, for it falls within the past, future, and present. "Sphere" (*dhātu*) refers to spatial divisions, for there is a distinction between this and that.
Furthermore, "world" (*loka*) means concealment or obscuration; "sphere" (*dhātu*) also means a boundary or limit. That which is conditioned and subject to destruction is the world. That is to say—
The unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) and indestructible dharmas are concealed; arising from true nature (*tathatā*), they are identical to unconditioned dharmas.
Thus, the conditioned (*saṃskṛta*) and destructible world is concealed, which is termed "non-intermixture. This constitutes their respective limits.

Therefore, those who perceive the Flower Treasury World (*Puṣpasaṃbhava-kṣetra*) do so in contrast to the Sahā world, while those who perceive the Sahā world do so in contrast to the Flower Treasury World.

The "accomplisher" refers to the conditions by which accomplishment is achieved. There are ten such conditions and so forth; because the subject and object are viewed as a unified whole, it is called the "accomplishment of the world.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, universally observed all worlds.
The ocean; the ocean of all sentient beings; the ocean of all Buddhas; the ocean of the entire dharma-realm; the ocean of the karma of all sentient beings;
the ocean of the faculties and desires of all sentient beings; the ocean of the wheels of Dharma of all Buddhas; the ocean of all three periods of time;
the ocean of the power of the vows of all Tathāgatas; the ocean of the miraculous transformations of all Tathāgatas. Having observed them in this way:
He addressed the ocean-like assembly of bodhisattvas at the site of enlightenment, saying: "O Sons of the Buddha!

The wisdom of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, which knows the inconceivable purity of the formation and destruction of all oceans of worlds, is inconceivable. The wisdom that knows the inconceivable ocean of the karma of all sentient beings is inconceivable.
The wisdom that knows the inconceivable ocean of the establishment of all dharma-realms is inconceivable. Thus he spoke.
The wisdom that knows the ocean of all infinite Buddhas is inconceivable. The wisdom that enters the ocean of all inclinations, understandings, and faculties is inconceivable.
The wisdom that universally knows all three periods of time in a single thought-moment is inconceivable.
The wisdom that displays the ocean of the infinite vows of all Tathāgatas is inconceivable. The wisdom that manifests the ocean of the spiritual transformations of all Buddhas is inconceivable.
Inconceivable is the wisdom that turns the wheel of Dharma; inconceivable is the ocean of establishing and expounding [the teachings];
inconceivable is the pure body of the Buddha; inconceivable is the universal illumination of the ocean of boundless forms and marks.
The primary marks and secondary characteristics are all pure and inconceivable. The ocean-like wheel of light of infinite forms and colors is fully pure and inconceivable.
The ocean-like clouds of light of various forms and colors are inconceivable.
The ocean of supreme jewel-flames is inconceivable. The ocean of accomplished speech and sound is inconceivable. Manifesting the three...
The inconceivable mastery over the ocean of lineages for taming and ripening all sentient beings;
the inconceivable courageous taming of the ocean of sentient beings such that none pass by in vain; and the inconceivable abiding in the stage of Buddhahood.
Entering the realm of the Tathāgata is inconceivable. The majestic power of his protection and sustenance is inconceivable.
Observing all that is practiced by the wisdom of the Buddhas is inconceivable. The perfection of his powers such that none can subdue him is inconceivable.
The merit of his fearlessness such that none can surpass it is inconceivable. Abiding in the samādhi of non-differentiation...
Inconceivable is the power of supernormal transformations; inconceivable is the wisdom of pure sovereignty;
inconceivable is the fact that all Buddha-dharmas cannot be destroyed.
All such dharmas as these, I shall fully proclaim by relying upon the spiritual power of the Buddha and the majestic spiritual power of all Tathāgatas, in order to cause sentient beings—
Because they are born into the ocean of the Buddha’s wisdom; in order to cause all bodhisattvas to attain stable dwelling within the ocean of the Buddha’s merits;
in order to cause all oceans of worlds to be adorned by the sovereign power of all Buddhas;
in order to cause the lineage of the Tathāgatas to never be interrupted throughout all oceans of eons; and in order to [cause them to dwell] in all worlds...

Because it reveals the true nature of all phenomena within the ocean of realms; because it causes the teaching to be proclaimed in accordance with the infinite oceans of the various understandings of all sentient beings;
because it employs skillful means in accordance with the oceans of the faculties of all sentient beings to cause the qualities of the Buddha-dharma to arise;
and because it destroys all obstacles in accordance with the oceans of the inclinations and desires of all sentient beings.
Because it is a mountain; because it causes the ocean of mental activities of all sentient beings to follow [the path] and purify and cultivate the way of transcendence;
because it causes all bodhisattvas to dwell securely within the ocean of Samantabhadra’s vows;

and at that time, because the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra further desired to generate joy in the ocean-like assemblies at the countless sites of enlightenment, and to cause them to increase in all dharmas.
Because of their joyful devotion, they cause the arising of a vast ocean of true faith and understanding; they cause the purification of the body that is the treasury of the universal Dharma-realm;
they cause the establishment of the ocean of Samantabhadra’s vows; they cause the purification of the eye of wisdom that enters into the equality of the three periods of time;
they cause the growth of the great ocean of wisdom that universally illumines the treasury of all worlds; and they cause the arising of dharanis...
Because she upholds all wheels of Dharma by means of her power; because she causes the entire realm of the Buddhas to be fully revealed within all sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*);

because she causes all Dharma-gates of the Tathāgatas to be opened and expounded; and because she causes the vast and profound nature of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) throughout the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) to increase. Then, she spoke these verses:
The ocean of merit of profound wisdom universally manifests throughout the infinite lands of the ten directions;
according to what each sentient being should perceive, its radiance shines everywhere as it turns the wheel of Dharma.
The oceans of lands in the ten directions are inconceivable, for the Buddha has purified them all throughout immeasurable eons.
To bring sentient beings to maturity through transformation, he appears in all lands;

the Buddha-realm is profoundly deep and difficult to conceive. He universally shows the way for sentient beings to enter it, yet those whose minds delight in the small and who are attached to existence cannot penetrate what the Buddha has realized.
If one possesses pure faith and a firm mind, One will always be able to draw near to spiritual friends.
All Buddhas will grant them their power; Thus one can enter the wisdom of the Tathāgata.
Free from all flattery and deceit, with a pure mind, One constantly delights in the nature of compassion and joy.
Those whose aspirations are vast and who possess deep faith, upon hearing this Dharma, give rise to joy;

abiding in the ground of Samantabhadra’s vows, they practice the pure path of the bodhisattvas and contemplate the dharma-realm as being like space— it is these who can know the sphere of the Buddha’s activity.
These bodhisattvas have attained a sublime benefit;
They behold all the Buddha’s supernormal powers, Which those who practice other paths cannot know; Only the practitioners of Samantabhadra can realize them.
Sentient beings are vast and boundless, And the Tathāgata protects and mindful of them all.
The turning of the wheel of the True Dharma reaches everywhere;
By the power of Vairocana’s realm, all lands enter my body, and the Buddhas who dwell therein do likewise.
You should observe all my pores; I now reveal to you the realm of the Buddha.
The practices and vows of Samantabhadra are boundless; I have cultivated them until they are fully perfected.
This vast body of the realm of the Universal Eye is that which the Buddhas have practiced—listen attentively to this.
Below, the Dharma-ocean is correctly presented in three chapters; among these, the first two chapters clarify the fruition, while the final chapter [clarifies the cause].
The "Discernment of Causes" answers the previous thirty questions regarding effects by clarifying those effects; the "Discernment of Causes" answers the first ten questions regarding causes.

Now, the present chapter generally discerns the oceans of lands belonging to all Buddhas and sentient beings, while the subsequent chapter specifically elucidates the adornments and purifications of our own Teacher’s land.
This chapter answers the question concerning their establishment, encompassing both causes and effects, whereas the subsequent chapter concerns effects alone.

Regarding "observing universally" and so forth: previously, one entered samādhi to internally accord with its source; now, it is said that one observes universally to externally examine its characteristics.
"In this way" and below is the formal exposition. Next, from "The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, know all world-oceans" onwards, there are ten inconceivable points.
These restate the ten phrases concerning the world-oceans and so forth as questions. Next is "the pure Buddha-body."
"Regarding the ten inconceivable [aspects] following 'conceivable': this restates the ten questions concerning the six sense faculties and the three karmas mentioned above.
Next, regarding the ten inconceivable [aspects] following 'abiding in the stages':

this restates the ten questions concerning the initial perfection of qualities and functions mentioned above. Next, from 'all such dharmas' up to 'fully proclaiming': this grants permission to speak."

Regarding the limits [of the text], the Commentary asks: "If it is said that [the sūtra] explains everything in full, why does the subsequent section speak only of the establishment [of the world] and the world-system itself?
The answer is: "Because the sūtra has not been transmitted in its entirety; furthermore, at the end of the Vairocana Chapter, there is no concluding summary."

If the sūtra were complete, one should further answer the remaining thirty-eight questions. Moreover, although two world-oceans have been described, they already comprehensively encompass the thirty phrases of inquiry.
Next, the ten subsequent phrases—beginning with "In order to cause sentient beings to enter the ocean of the Buddha’s wisdom"—explain the benefits that are accomplished.
Next, at that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva further desired to cause [them] to...
Because the ocean-like assembly gives rise to joy, the following praises the excellence [of the teaching] and exhorts them to listen.
Next, in order to cause their love and delight for all dharmas to increase, the following ten phrases specifically clarify the meaning of joy. Next, ten verses in verse form are spoken.

Of these, the first two verses clarify the appearance of the Buddha. Next, the suitability of the vessel (the listener) is determined; the first of these verses excludes those who are not suitable vessels, and the next four...

The verse clarifies that [the audience] is indeed a vessel for the Dharma. The subsequent verse concludes by attributing [this capacity] to the power of the Buddha. The following two verses exhort them to listen.
The subsequent text properly sets forth what is to be taught.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra addressed the great assembly, saying:
This single phrase constitutes the introduction to the assembly.
O Sons of the Buddha, there are ten matters regarding the oceans of worlds that have been spoken, are being spoken, and will be spoken by all Buddhas of the past,
present, and future.

Below this, Samantabhadra provides the explicit exposition. Regarding the thirty questions on the fruits mentioned previously, he answers the single question concerning the "ocean of world-systems' establishment" (*lokadhātu-vyavasthāna-samudra*), while the remainder are all subsumed therein.

The vastness and depth of the world-systems are metaphorically termed an "ocean. This means that by accumulating lands (*kṣetra*) they form "species" (*gotra*), and by accumulating species they form an "ocean.
The ocean has no separate substance; it is the collective name for the world-systems. However, the categories of phenomena are extensive.
They are numerous; I shall briefly cite ten of them.
What are these ten? They are: the causes and conditions for the arising of world-oceans; the basis upon which world-oceans rest;
the shapes of world-oceans; the essential nature of world-oceans; the adornments of world-oceans; the purification of world-oceans; and so forth.
The emergence of Buddhas in oceans of realms; the kalpa-durations of oceans of worlds; the distinctions in the transformations of kalpas in oceans of worlds;
