and the gates of non-distinction in oceans of worlds.
This enumeration sets forth ten kinds of differences within oceans of worlds.

O Sons of the Buddha, briefly stated, there are these ten matters regarding the oceans of worlds. Were they to be explained in detail, they would be equal in number to the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
They have been taught by all Buddhas of the past, present, and future; they are being taught now; and they shall be taught in the future.
This summary briefly reveals what is vast. As for the phrase "dust motes of world-oceans," even wisdom finds it difficult to fathom;

how could one possibly describe it? Were one not a realized Dharma-cloud [Bodhisattva], how could one receive this teaching? Nevertheless, regarding the ten matters mentioned above, the number of each within every single *kṣetra* (buddha-field) is indeterminate.
Regarding the category of "conditions," there may be one, two, three, or many; regarding the category of "purity," there may be one...
They may be many or they may be none, because there are lands that are purely defiled.

That they are without distinction yet all possess [all qualities] is because, in terms of their essential nature, they are equal and integrated by the Buddha’s power; thus it is said they are without distinction while both the defiled and the pure are fully present.
The statement that there are worlds as numerous as the atoms of an ocean of worlds refers to the teaching of inexhaustible integration. That is to say:
If one were to grind the entirety of the ocean of worlds into dust, with each particle of dust becoming a single ocean of lands (*kṣetrasāgara*),
and within each such ocean of lands there were likewise as many conditions and so forth as there are particles of dust in an ocean of lands— meaning that for every one of these oceans of lands,
the multitude of conditions and so forth contained therein is itself manifold upon manifold— it is therefore called "inexhaustible."
O Sons of the Buddha, in brief, it is due to ten causes and conditions that all world-oceans have been formed, are being formed, or will be formed.
What are these ten? They are: the spiritual power of the Tathāgatas; the natural course of phenomena;
the karma and actions of all sentient beings; that which is attained by all Bodhisattvas through the realization of omniscience; and [the aspirations of] all sentient beings...
Furthermore, it is because all bodhisattvas have gathered together roots of goodness; because of the power of the vows of all bodhisattvas to adorn and purify buddha-fields;
because all bodhisattvas have accomplished non-retrogressive conduct and vows; because of the sovereign power of the pure resolute understandings of all bodhisattvas;
and because of the flow from the roots of goodness of all Tathāgatas, as well as the sovereignty of all Buddhas at the time of their attainment of enlightenment.
By the power of their majesty; by the sovereign power of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s vows. O Sons of the Buddha, these are the ten kinds of causes and conditions briefly explained.
Were they to be explained in detail, they would be as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds. At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva—
Desiring to restate this meaning, and receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, he surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"The boundless oceans of lands thus described, Vairocana has entirely purified;
The realm of the World-Honored One is inconceivable— Such is his wisdom and power of spiritual penetration."
The Bodhisattva practices an ocean of vows, universally following the desires of the minds of sentient beings;
the mental activities of sentient beings are vast and boundless, and the Bodhisattva’s lands pervade the ten directions.
The Bodhisattva advances toward all-knowledge, diligently cultivating various powers of mastery.
Universally giving birth from an ocean of immeasurable vows, They accomplish vast buddha-fields in their entirety;
Cultivating oceans of practices without end, They enter the realm of the Buddhas, which is likewise immeasurable.
To purify all lands throughout the ten directions, They spend immeasurable eons in each and every land.

Sentient beings are agitated and turbid by afflictions; their discriminations regarding desires are not of a single form, and they create inconceivable karma according to their minds. All these oceans of lands are thus established;
O Son of the Buddha, this ocean of lands is a treasury of adornments, composed of stainless, radiant jewels.
This arises from a mind of vast faith and understanding; in all the worlds throughout the ten directions, it is thus.
Bodhisattvas are able to cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra;
traversing the paths within the atoms of the dharma-realm, they manifest in infinite lands, pure and vast as space.
Manifesting spiritual powers throughout the realm of empty space, they all proceed to the sites of enlightenment where the Buddhas sit upon lotus thrones and display various forms.
Each individual body encompasses all lands, universally manifesting throughout the three periods of time; thus, the entire ocean of lands is established.
The Buddha entered therein through skillful means; this is that which has been adorned and purified by Vairocana.

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O sons of the Buddha, within each ocean of worlds, there are as many bases of support as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds.
That is to say, some rest upon all manner of adornments, or they rest upon..."
It abides in space; or it abides supported by the radiance of all jewels; or it abides supported by the radiance of all Buddhas;
or it abides supported by the radiance of the colors of all jewels; or it abides supported by the voices of all Buddhas;
or it abides supported by Vajrapāṇi, who possesses the form of a powerful asura born from illusory karma; or it abides supported by the bodies of all world-protectors.
Some abide supported by the bodies of all Bodhisattvas; some abide supported by the oceans of various adornments produced by the vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
O Sons of the Buddha, the oceans of worlds have such supports as these, numbering as many as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power and contemplated.
Observing the ten directions, he spoke in verse:
"Pervading the entire realm of empty space throughout the ten directions, All the various lands that exist there—
Empowered by the spiritual power of the Tathāgata, They appear before one everywhere and can all be seen."
There are various kinds of lands, all of which are composed of stainless jewels;
they are pure, made of the most exquisite *maṇi* gems, and blaze forth as an ocean of pervasive light.
There are also pure lands of radiant light that abide supported by the realm of empty space.
Or in oceans of mani-jewel seas, there are Tathāgatas dwelling in treasuries of light;
in these oceans of assemblies, they expound the wheel of Dharma with exquisite skill.
The realm of all Buddhas is vast and boundless; those sentient beings who behold it rejoice in their hearts.
Some are adorned with mani-jewels, Shaped like flower-lamps, widely distributed, With clouds of fragrant flame-light blazing in color;
Covered by nets of light from exquisite jewels.
There are buddha-lands without limit, Abiding in deep oceans of lotuses.
Vast, pure, and transcending the world, for it is adorned by the wondrous and virtuous flowers of all Buddhas;
some oceans of lands revolve along with the wheel, yet through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power they abide in peace.
Within them dwell multitudes of Bodhisattvas, who constantly behold infinite and vast jewels.
Some abide as Vajrapāṇi, and others abide in the body of the Lord of Devas;
the Supreme Honored One Vairocana constantly turns the wheel of Dharma in this place,
or dwells evenly beneath jeweled trees, and likewise amidst clouds of fragrant flames.
Some rely upon the great waters, while others dwell in the firm diamond-ocean;
some take refuge in the diamond-banner, and others abide within oceans of flowers.
Vairocana can manifest these vast and divine transformations everywhere without exception.
Some are long, some are short, in immeasurable varieties; their circular forms are likewise not one.
This wondrous treasury of adornment is distinct from the world; only through pure cultivation can it be seen.
Such various differences all abide within the ocean of vows.
There are lands that eternally abide in space, entirely filled with Buddhas like gathering clouds;
some hang suspended in the void, sometimes present and sometimes absent;
there are lands of supreme purity, dwelling within the jeweled crowns of Bodhisattvas.
The great supernormal powers of all Buddhas of the ten directions are all seen within this;
the voices of all Buddhas completely pervade everywhere, brought forth by the power of karma.
There are lands that encompass the entire dharma-realm, pure and free from defilement, arising from the mind.
Like shadows and like illusions, vast and boundless; Like Indra’s net, each distinct and diverse;
Or manifesting various treasuries of adornment, Established by relying upon empty space.
The realms of all karmic activities are inconceivable; Through the power of the Buddha, they are revealed so that all may see them.
Within every single atom of every land, In every thought-moment,
he manifests Buddha-fields as numerous as all sentient beings; Such is the constant work of Samantabhadra,
For the sake of bringing sentient beings to maturity, Practicing therein through oceans of kalpas.
Vast and great spiritual transformations arise without exception, pervading everywhere throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
Within every single atom of the lands of the Dharma-realm, oceans of great buddha-fields abide;
clouds of Buddhas spread equally over them all, filling every single place.
Just as there is sovereign mastery within a single atom, so it is likewise within all atoms.
The great supernormal powers of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, Vairocana can manifest them all;
all vast and extensive buddha-fields are like shadows, like illusions, and like flames.
In the ten directions, its source of birth is not seen; Furthermore, it has no place of coming or going.
Dissolution and formation revolve in mutual succession;
Within the empty sky, there is never a moment’s rest— All of this is due to pure vows, Sustained by the power of vast karma.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O Sons of the Buddha, the oceans of worlds possess various distinct forms and characteristics.
That is to say, they may be circular, or square, or neither circular nor square; there are immeasurable distinctions.
Some are shaped like whirlpools of water, some like mountain flames, some like trees, some like flowers, and some like palaces."
Their forms were either like the forms of sentient beings or like the form of a Buddha; such forms existed in numbers as many as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to reiterate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:

The oceans of all lands are variously distinct; their various adornments and various dwellings possess unique forms that are collectively beautiful throughout the ten directions. You all should together observe them:
their shapes may be circular, or square, or even triangular and octagonal.
The jewel-wheels, lotuses, and so forth—all these are made diverse by karma;
some are adorned with pure flames, interspersed with refined gold, and many are most exquisite.
The gates and portals open in competition without obstruction; this arises from the vastness of karma and the absence of mental confusion.
The boundless treasury of distinctions within the ocean of lands, Like clouds spread across the void,
with jewel wheels adorning the ground in wondrous array, Amidst the radiance of all Buddhas’ light,
all realms of existence are mentally discerned, Manifesting through various kinds of luminous illumination.
Within such oceans of lands, the Buddha manifests supernatural powers individually;
some are defiled, others are pure, and they experience suffering and joy with their respective differences.
This arises from the inconceivable ocean of karma; the nature of all phenomena in saṃsāra is ever thus.
Within a single pore are inconceivable lands, Abiding in various ways as numerous as atoms;
In each one dwells the All-Illuminating Honored One, Proclaiming the wondrous Dharma amidst the great assembly.
Within a single atom are lands, large and small, With various distinctions as numerous as atoms.
Whether level or uneven, each place is different; the Buddha goes to them all to turn the wheel of Dharma.
Within every single atom, he manifests lands, all through the power of his original vows and spiritual penetrations;
according to the various inclinations of beings' minds, he is able to create all manner of diverse forms within the void of space.
Within every single atom of all lands, The Buddha enters them all;
For the sake of all sentient beings, he manifests spiritual transformations— Such is the Dharma of Vairocana.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O Sons of the Buddha, you should know that within the ocean of worlds..."
Various essential natures: that is to say, some have as their essence the adornment of all jewels; some have as their essence the various adornments of a single jewel;
some have as their essence the radiance of all jewels; some have as their essence the radiance of various colors;
some have as their essence the radiance of all adornments; and some have as their essence indestructible vajra.
Its substance may consist of the sustaining power of the Buddha; or its substance may consist of the marks of exquisite jewels; or its substance may consist of the Buddha’s transformations;
or its substance may consist of the solar maṇi-wheel; or its substance may consist of extremely subtle jewels;
or its substance may consist of the flames of all kinds of jewels; or its substance may consist of various fragrances; or its substance may consist of crowns of all kinds of jewel-flowers.
It has as its essence the reflections of all jewels; or it has as its essence the manifestations of all adornments;
or it has as its essence the universal manifestation of realms within a single thought-moment; or it has as its essence the jewels in the form of bodhisattvas;
or it has as its essence jewel flower-stamens; or it has as its essence the vocal sounds of the Buddhas. At that time, Samantabhadra...
The Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
There are oceans of lands, Composed of exquisite jewels, Firm and indestructible, Resting upon precious lotus flowers; Or they are pure radiance, Whose origin is unknowable.
Adorned with all light, they abide resting upon space; Or having pure light as their essence, they further rest upon radiance.
Adorned with clouds of light, these are the places where Bodhisattvas wander together.
Furthermore, there are oceans of lands that arise from the power of vows, Abiding like reflections.
Some are said to be ungraspable, or composed of mani jewels; Adorned with spheres of pearls that radiate the light of the Sun-Treasury, they are filled entirely by bodhisattvas.
There are lands formed of jewel-flames, with clouds of flames covering them above;
The light of their various jewels is exquisite and wondrous, all obtained through the power of karma.
Some arise from wondrous signs, adorning the ground with manifold marks; like a crown worn together upon the head, these arise through the Buddha’s transformation.
Some arise from the ocean of the mind, abiding according to what the mind understands—like an illusion, they have no fixed location.
All are conceptual constructions, or else produced by the Buddha’s radiance.
With the light of mani-jewels as its essence, all Buddhas appear within it; each manifests supernatural powers,
such as those of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, who transforms and manifests oceans of lands, adorned by the power of his vows—
all of which are exquisite and wondrous.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O Sons of the Buddha, you should know that the oceans of worlds possess various kinds of adornments.
That is to say, some are adorned by clouds of supreme excellence emerging from all manner of ornaments."
Either by expounding upon the adornment of all bodhisattva merits; or by expounding upon the adornment of the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
or by manifesting the adornment of the ocean of all bodhisattva vows;
or by representing the adornment of the images of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; or by manifesting in a single thought-moment the spheres of supernatural power spanning boundless eons.
The adornment of realms: some are adorned by the manifestation of the bodies of all Buddhas;

some are adorned by the manifestation of clouds of all precious incenses; some are adorned by the radiant illumination of all marvelous and precious objects within all sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*);
and some are adorned by the manifestation of all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra. Such [adornments] exist in the world...
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning in detail, received the Buddha’s majestic power,
surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
The vast oceans of lands are without limit, all formed by pure karma;
with various adornments and various dwellings, they fill every direction in the ten quarters.
Boundless clouds of jewel-flames with diverse forms and appearances constitute a vast array of manifold kinds.
Constantly appearing throughout the oceans of lands in the ten directions, They universally manifest wondrous sounds to preach the Dharma.
The Bodhisattvas, oceans of boundless merit, Adorned with various great vows,
Simultaneously produce sublime sounds in this land, Universally shaking the net of all lands in the ten directions.
The ocean of sentient beings' karma is vast and immeasurable; according to their respective retributions, each is different.
Amidst the adornments of all places, it is through the Buddhas that these can be expounded.
All Tathāgatas of the three periods of time universally manifest their spiritual powers throughout the oceans of lands.
Within each and every phenomenon, all Buddhas— You should contemplate such pure adornments as these.
Throughout the kalpas of the past, future, and present, And within all lands of the ten directions,
All their great adornments Are seen, one by one, within every buddha-field.
In all matters, infinite Buddhas, equal in number to sentient beings, pervade the world;
To subdue them, they manifest spiritual powers, thereby adorning the oceans of lands.
From every adornment, they emit wondrous clouds: Clouds of various flowers, clouds of fragrant flames, and so forth.
Mani-jewel clouds constantly appear, adorning this ocean of lands;
In all places throughout the ten directions where enlightenment is attained, Every kind of adornment is fully present.
Radiant light spreads afar like colored clouds, Causing all within this ocean of lands to behold them.

O sons of the Buddha who practice the vows and conduct of Samantabhadra, Diligently cultivating for as many eons as there are sentient beings, You have adorned all boundless lands, And you manifest everywhere within them.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O sons of the Buddha, you should know that within the ocean of worlds..."
The ocean of oceans of worlds contains an ocean of pure skillful means as numerous as the atoms therein, namely:
because all bodhisattvas draw near to all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) and share the same roots of goodness; because they increase vast clouds of merit that pervade the entire dharma-realm;
because they purely cultivate vast and supreme resolute beliefs (adhimukti); because they observe all the spheres of bodhisattvas and dwell therein; and because they practice purification...
Because all the *pāramitās* are completely fulfilled; because they observe, enter, and abide in all the stages (*bhūmi*) of the bodhisattvas;
because they give birth to the ocean of all pure vows; because they cultivate all practices leading to liberation;
because they enter the ocean of all adornments; and because they achieve the power of pure skillful means—such are the worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to reiterate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power,
surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
All the adornments of the oceans of lands arise from the power of countless skillful means and vows;
The oceans of lands are eternally radiant, produced by the power of immeasurable pure karma.
Having long approached spiritual friends, they have cultivated virtuous deeds together, all of which are utterly pure.
With great compassion pervading all sentient beings, They adorn the oceans of all buddha-lands with dharma-gates,
samādhis, and the like; Having thoroughly purified the stages of meditative concentration,
liberation, and skillful means in the presence of all Buddhas, They thereby bring forth the oceans of all buddha-lands.
Having generated immeasurable, resolute understandings and having cultivated the skillful means of the ocean of patience that realizes the Tathāgatas as being non-different,
they are thus able to adorn and purify boundless lands;
for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, they cultivate supreme practices, and their vast merit constantly increases.
Like clouds spreading across the entirety of space, all oceans of lands are fully realized;
The infinite perfections, as numerous as the atoms of all lands, have all been practiced to fulfillment;
Thus the perfection of vows is inexhaustible, and from this, the pure oceans of lands arise.
Purifying all peerless dharmas, Arising infinite practices of transcendence through various skillful means to transform all beings,
Thus adorning oceans of buddha-lands, practicing the stages of skillful adornment,
They enter the ocean of the Buddha’s gates of merit and dharma.
May all sentient beings exhaust the source of suffering; May vast and pure lands be fully realized.
The ocean of power is vast and beyond compare;
May all sentient beings plant roots of goodness, Making offerings to all Tathāgatas, Until every boundless land is entirely purified.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:

"O Sons of the Buddha, you should know that within each and every world-ocean, there are as many distinct manifestations of Buddhas as there are atoms in a world-ocean. That is to say, some manifest small bodies, some manifest large bodies;
some manifest short lifespans, some manifest long lifespans; some manifest by solely purifying a single Buddha-land, or..."
There are infinitely many Buddha-lands, adorned and pure. Some manifest only the wheel of the Dharma of the Single Vehicle (Ekayāna);
others manifest the wheels of the Dharma of inconceivable vehicles. Some appear to subdue a limited number of sentient beings; others demonstrate the subduing of boundless sentient beings.
There are as many such [lands] as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds. At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to...
To further proclaim this meaning, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, he surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"The various skillful means of all Buddhas Arise throughout the oceans of all lands;
They accord with whatever sentient beings delight in— This is the Tathāgata’s power of skillful mastery."
The Dharma-body of all Buddhas is inconceivable— Without color, without form, and without image;
Yet it can manifest various signs for the sake of sentient beings, Causing them all to see according to their mental inclinations.
It may manifest a short lifespan for some beings, Or manifest a lifespan remaining for immeasurable eons.
The Dharma-body manifests universally throughout the ten directions, appearing in the world according to what is appropriate;
sometimes it is wondrously pure and inconceivable, encompassing all the oceans of lands in the ten directions,
or perhaps it is purely adorned within a single land, manifesting everything therein without exception.
In accordance with the inclinations of sentient beings' minds, they manifest various inconceivable vehicles;
some proclaim only the Dharma of the Single Vehicle, while within that One, through skillful means, they manifest the infinite.
Some spontaneously attain perfect enlightenment, causing a few sentient beings to abide upon the Path.
Some, within a single thought-instant, awaken countless deluded beings; Others, from every pore,
emit clouds of emanations, Manifesting infinite and boundless Buddhas so that all worlds may behold them,
Using various skillful means to deliver all living beings.
There may be voices that universally pervade everywhere,
preaching the Dharma according to the inclinations of beings' minds throughout inconceivable great eons, taming oceans of immeasurable sentient beings;
or there may be lands of infinite adornment, where the assemblies sit in pure and solemn stillness.
The Buddhas are spread like clouds within it, filling every ocean of lands in the ten directions.
The skillful means of the Buddhas are inconceivable; according to the minds of sentient beings, they appear before them all.
Universally dwelling in various adorned lands, they pervade every single realm.

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O sons of the Buddha, you should know that within the oceans of worlds there are kalpas of duration as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.
That is to say, some have a duration of incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) kalpas; some have a duration of immeasurable (*aprameya*) kalpas;
some have a duration of boundless (*ananta*) kalpas; some have a duration of incomparable (*asama*) kalpas; and some have a duration of uncountable (*agaṇeya*) kalpas."

They abide for an eon; some abide for an incalculable eon, some abide for an inconceivable eon, some abide for an immeasurable eon, some abide for an ineffable eon, and some abide for an ineffably ineffable eon.
There were as many such [assemblies] as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
Within the oceans of worlds, the various kalpas, adorned by vast and skillful means, are all beheld in the lands of the ten directions;
their numbers and distinctions are all clearly understood.
I behold the oceans of worlds in the ten directions, where the number of kalpas is as infinite as the number of sentient beings.
Whether long, short, or boundless, I now proclaim through the Buddha’s voice:
I behold the oceans of lands in the ten directions; Some endure for eons as numerous as atoms in a land, Some for a single eon, and some for countless eons;
Through their vows, they are each diverse and distinct.
Some are purely pure, some are purely defiled, And others are a mixture of both defilement and purity;
The ocean of vows establishes these various distinctions Within the mental perceptions of sentient beings.
Having practiced for kalpas as numerous as the atoms of Buddha-lands in the past, One attains a great, utterly pure ocean of worlds.
The realm of all Buddhas is fully adorned, Abiding forever throughout infinite and vast eons.
It is named "Various Jewel Radiance," Or "Equal Sound," "Flame-Eye Treasury," "Stainless Radiance," and "Auspicious Eon. This pure eon encompasses all.
There are pure eons in which a single Buddha appears;
or within a single eon, immeasurable Buddhas manifest through the power of inexhaustible skillful means and great vows.
They enter into all various kinds of eons, or immeasurable eons enter into one eon; or again, one eon enters into many eons.
The various gateways of all oceans of kalpas are clearly manifested throughout the lands of the ten directions;
or the adorned events of all kalpas are all seen within a single kalpa;
or the adornments contained within a single kalpa universally enter into all infinite kalpas.
Beginning from a single thought and ending with the completion of an eon, all arise in dependence upon the mental conceptions of sentient beings.
All oceans of lands and boundless eons are purified through a single skillful means.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O Children of the Buddha, you should know that within the ocean of worlds..."
The transformations and distinctions of eons as numerous as the atoms within oceans of worlds are as follows:

because such is the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), oceans of worlds undergo transformations through immeasurable eons of formation and dissolution; because they are inhabited by defiled sentient beings, oceans of worlds undergo transformations through defiled eons;
because they are inhabited by sentient beings who cultivate vast merit, oceans of worlds undergo transformations through eons that are both defiled and pure; [and] through faith...
Because Bodhisattvas dwell therein, world-oceans undergo transformation through kalpas of defilement and purity;
because immeasurable sentient beings resolve upon bodhicitta, world-oceans undergo transformation through kalpas of absolute purity;
because all Bodhisattvas travel individually through various worlds, world-oceans undergo transformation through kalpas of boundless adornment. [All] world-oceans in the ten directions...
Because Bodhisattvas gather like clouds, the world-oceans undergo transformation during immeasurable great adornment eons.
Because the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, enter parinirvāṇa, the world-oceans undergo transformation during eons of the cessation of adornments.

Because the Buddhas appear in the world, all world-oceans undergo transformation during eons of vast, pure, and magnificent adornment. Because of the Tathāgatas’ supernormal powers and transformations, the world...
The oceans of realms are universally pure, and the eons undergo transformation. There are as many such [realms] as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
All lands and realms arise entirely through the power of karma; you should observe that the nature of their transformation is thus.
When sentient beings are defiled, bound by karma and delusion, they are terrifying;
their minds cause the entire ocean of worlds to become defiled. Yet, if there is a pure mind...
Cultivating various meritorious deeds, they cause that mind to [purify] the ocean of lands.
Bodhisattvas who possess faith and understanding in both defilement and purity are born within those eons;
according to the defiled or pure perceptions held by their minds, immeasurable sentient beings all resolve to attain bodhicitta.
That mind causes the oceans of lands to remain eternally pure throughout the kalpas;
immeasurable billions of bodhisattvas travel to the ten directions, their adornments being without distinction.
Within each and every atom, one perceives the differences of kalpas and Buddha-lands as numerous as atoms, where bodhisattvas gather together like clouds.
When the World-Honored One enters nirvana, all lands become pure;
yet when that land’s adornments vanish and sentient beings lack the capacity for the Dharma, the world becomes defiled.
If a Buddha arises in the world, everything becomes precious and excellent; according to the purity of their minds, all adornments are fully perfected.
The supernatural powers of all Buddhas manifest inconceivable displays; at that time, all oceans of lands become universally pure.
Then, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O Children of the Buddha, you should know that within the oceans of worlds..."
They are undifferentiated in number, equal to the atoms within oceans of worlds.
That is to say, within each ocean of worlds, there are oceans of worlds as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, and they are undifferentiated.
Within each ocean of worlds, the majestic power manifested by all Buddhas is undifferentiated. Within each ocean of worlds, all sites of enlightenment pervade the ten directions.
There is no distinction among realms. Within each and every ocean of worlds, there is no distinction among the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas.
Within each and every ocean of worlds, there is no distinction among the light of all Buddhas pervading the Dharma-realm.
Within each and every ocean of worlds, there is no distinction among the names and titles of the emanations of all Buddhas. Within each and every ocean of worlds...
The voices of all Buddhas pervade the oceans of worlds throughout boundless eons without distinction.
Within each ocean of worlds, the skillful means of turning the wheel of Dharma are without distinction.
Within each ocean of worlds, all oceans of worlds universally enter into a single atom without distinction. Within each ocean of worlds, within every single atom...
The vast realms of all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the three periods of time, all appear therein without distinction.

O Sons of the Buddha, such is the brief explanation of the non-distinction of the oceans of worlds. Were it to be explained in detail, there would be as many non-distinctions as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power and...
Observing the ten directions, he spoke in verse:
Within a single atom are many oceans of lands, Each location distinct and entirely pure;
Thus, the infinite enters into one, Each division distinct, without confusion or overlap.
Within each and every atom dwell inconceivable Buddhas, Appearing universally before the minds of sentient beings;
They pervade all oceans of lands without exception, Such skillful means being without distinction.
Within each and every atom are kings of trees, With various adornments all hanging down and spread abroad.
The lands of the ten directions all appear together; thus, all are without distinction.
Within every single atom, hosts of beings as numerous as atoms all surround the Lord of Men.
Transcending all, they pervade the world, yet there is no crowding or confusion.
Within each and every atom are immeasurable lights, Pervading all lands throughout the ten directions;
The bodhisattva practices of all Buddhas appear therein, Without distinction across the entire ocean of realms.
Within each and every atom are infinite bodies, Manifesting transformations like clouds that pervade everywhere.
Using the Buddha’s supernormal powers to guide all beings, The lands of the ten directions are likewise without distinction.
Within every single atom, he expounds myriad teachings; Those teachings are pure, revolving like a wheel.
Through various gates of skillful means and mastery, He proclaims them all without any differentiation.
Within a single atom, the voices of all Buddhas are universally proclaimed, Filling all sentient beings who are vessels of the Dharma.
Abiding throughout the ocean of lands for infinite eons, Such sounds are likewise without distinction.
The ocean of lands has immeasurable, wondrous adornments, And there is nothing that does not enter into a single atom.
Such supernatural powers of all Buddhas arise entirely from the nature of karma;
within every single atom, the Buddhas of the three periods of time appear according to the inclinations of beings.
Their essential nature neither comes nor goes, yet by the power of their vows, they pervade the world.
Below this, there is a detailed explanation of the ten distinct matters, which constitutes ten sections. Each section contains both prose and verse.
Now, first is the causal conditions for the arising [of the land], where ten types are briefly cited in the heading to collectively establish all Buddha-fields of the three periods of time.
As for what these are, the following interrogates and enumerates the ten conditions. Although the meaning of "Buddha-field" (buddhakṣetra) has many varieties, it is not...
There are three [types of] lands: first, the Land of Dharma-nature (*dharmatā-kṣetra*); second, the Land of Enjoyment (*saṃbhoga-kṣetra*); and third, the Land of Transformation (*nirmāṇa-kṣetra*).

If the Land of Enjoyment is divided into that which is self-enjoyed and that which is enjoyed by others, then there are four lands. However, when unified, there are only two kinds: namely, the Pure and the Impure, or the Essential Nature (*svabhāva*) and the Phenomenal Aspect (*lakṣaṇa*).
Now, these are fused into one, which differs from other schools. Furthermore, this Pure Land does not consist of a single substance; it is pure.

Defilement and purity, deficiency and fullness, differ in substance yet do not constitute separate principles; they are equal and level. That which possesses substance cannot be established without tracing its source, which is then profound darkness;
that which lacks substance cannot be established without the dependent origination of myriad forms. Thus, form and the sublation of form are perfectly interfused without any obstruction.

Since the lands are unequal, their causes and conditions are likewise distinct. Within the ten sections of the present text, the first three generally reveal this principle, while the subsequent four provide a detailed analysis.
The latter three refer to integration, inclusion, and transformation. Regarding the first three:

first, "the Tathāgata’s spiritual power" means that all lands, whether pure or impure, are accomplished through the power of the Tathāgata’s supernormal wisdom; he assumes them for the sake of sentient beings, intending to respond universally to their needs.
Second, "the nature of phenomena" (*dharmatā*): in Sanskrit it is *dharmatā*, which here is translated as "the natural state of things" (*fǎ'ěr*) or simply "phenomena" (*fǎ*).

Regarding nature: if it is the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), it takes the fundamental consciousness—the Tathāgata-garbha body—as its support, constantly and simultaneously transforming and giving rise to the external various receptacle worlds.
Regarding the third, the power of the karma of sentient beings: karma is either wholesome or unwholesome, and lands are either pure or defiled.
Next, the four [points] clarify the distinctions: there are causes and there are conditions. The first is the cause for the land of self-enjoyment (*svasaṃbhoga-kāya*); it is the Great Perfect...
Because it is accomplished by means of the mirror-like wisdom (*ādarśa-jñāna*), it is the cause for the second type, the land of transformation (*nirmāṇa-kṣetra*).

This refers to sentient beings and bodhisattvas collectively constructing a single objective condition, such that each is born into that land according to their respective karma and actions; thus, ordinary beings and sages dwell together there. The third and fourth types are the two kinds of lands of enjoyment for others (*parasaṃbhoga-kṣetra*).
As for the first of these, it pertains to those from the first stage (*prathamā bhūmi*) upward, as exemplified by the vow for the purification of the buddha-land among the Ten Great Vows.
It is so. This refers to the stages from the eighth bhūmi upward, as it is accomplished through the practice of non-retrogressive effort.

Within the eighth bhūmi, there is the section on the Pure Land. Regarding the subsequent three [sections] that involve integration and subsumption, they pertain generally to both causes and conditions.
The first specifically refers to the eighth bhūmi and above, where one churns the great ocean into cream and curd, transforms the great earth into gold, and turns the defiled into the pure.

Purity becomes defilement because it encompasses the birth of sentient beings through mastery. Among the ten masteries, there is the mastery over lands (*kṣetra-vaśitā*). To exhaustively investigate its cause:
it is pure resolute conviction (*adhimukti*). Through the sustaining power of this resolute conviction, things are transformed according to one's will.

The next [mastery] refers to the time of attaining perfect enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*), when one’s body fills the lands as numerous as the atoms within the worlds of the ten directions, and thoughts and eons are perfectly integrated (*yuganaddha*) in a single moment.

It is established by two kinds of causes: first, the cause of speech which flows from the roots of goodness; second, the power of the realization of the Path, which clarifies the function of the fruit.
This is the mutual integration of the enjoyment body (*saṃbhogakāya*) and the transformation body (*nirmāṇakāya*).

It is just as in the beginning of the sutra, regarding the solidity of the land of Magadha and so forth; subsequently, whether there is questioning or not, it is always able to be integrated and subsumed. Furthermore, the former...
This is the Sublime Enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*). This is the Equal Enlightenment (*samatā-bodhi*). Its *dharmatā*-land (*dharmatā-kṣetra*) serves as the substance for all lands.
Regarding the verses: the first verse praises the Tathāgata’s spiritual power; the second verse praises the shared accumulation of roots of goodness;
the third verse praises the attainment of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); the fourth verse praises the two lines [of the sixth and seventh stages]; and the fifth verse praises the assembly.
The practices of birth; six verses in one stanza praise the bodhisattva’s resolute conviction; seven verses in one stanza praise the vows of Samantabhadra’s conduct;
eight verses in two stanzas praise the sovereign mastery of the Tathāgata.

The first section provides a general explanation of the causes and conditions for the arising of the world. Next follow: second, the basis upon which it rests; third, its shape; fourth, its essential nature;

fifth, its adornments; sixth, its purity; seventh, the appearance of Buddhas; eighth, the differences between abiding kalpas; ninth, the transformations within abiding kalpas; and tenth, their lack of distinction.
These are presented in this sequence, with prose and verse explanations provided for each in the subsequent text. At this point—
The text is clear. The commentaries (*śāstra*) each contain numerous meanings; students should investigate them.
This concludes the "Chapter on the Accomplishment of the World" from the *Outline of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Volume Seven.
Essentials of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Scroll Eight Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda,
a śramaṇa from the Kingdom of Khotan Commentary on the Meaning by the Śramaṇa Chengguan of the Great Huayan Monastery at Mount Qingliang (Cool Mountain)
The Fifth Chapter of the *Huazang Shijie Jing* (The Scripture on the Flower Treasury World), Excerpted by the Śramaṇa Deqing of Hanshan at Fayun Monastery on Mount Kuang.
Regarding the intent behind the arrival of this chapter:
while the preceding chapter generally elucidated the oceans of lands of all Buddhas, this chapter specifically elucidates that of our own Teacher.
Regarding the "fruit of the adorned basis," it follows [the previous section] because it answers the question concerning the world-ocean. In the Sanskrit original, it is titled in full:
"The Chapter on the Radiance of the Ocean of Universally Pure Merits, Adorned with the Array of the Flower-Womb World-Ocean.
The translator, finding this too prolix, has now made it excessively brief; it should rather be called "The Chapter on the Lotus-Womb Adorned World-Ocean. This refers to the lotus...
That which contains a child is called a "repository" (*kośa*). Now, since these world-systems and lands are contained within a great lotus, it is called the "Flower Repository" (*Kusumakośa*).
Within each and every realm therein, there are pure merits as numerous as the atoms of an ocean of worlds;
therefore, they are called "adornments. Because the worlds are profound and vast, they are termed "oceans. Yet, this world...
The Ocean briefly cites two causes. First, with respect to sentient beings, the Tathāgata-garbha consciousness is the fragrant ocean;
thus, the *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra* speaks of the "ocean of the ālayavijñāna," which is also the ocean of dharmatā. Its basis in non-abiding is the wind-circle, which is also the wind of deluded thought.
Within this ocean, there is the aspect of cause and effect: the nature-virtues as numerous as the sands of the Ganges constitute the direct cause.
The flower. Because it fully encompasses all future dharmas of both the mundane and supramundane worlds, it is called a "store" (*garbha*).

If one takes the *dharmatā* (the nature of phenomena) as the ocean, the mind is the flower; the manner of its encompassing and storing is likewise so. However, within the objective aspect (*nimitta-bhāga*) of this storehouse consciousness (*ālaya-vijñāna*), half constitutes the external vessel-world because it is not grasped and appropriated (*anupātta*);
the other half constitutes the internal body, which is grasped and appropriated as one's own nature, giving rise to cognition.

Because of [the nature of] sensation (*vedanā*). Second, with respect to the Buddhas: it means that by means of the wind of great vows, they sustain the ocean of great compassion, giving rise to the flowers of boundless practices.
These contain the dharmas of the fruits of the two benefits—both defiled and pure—which are layered and unimpeded;
therefore, the characteristics of the lands they manifest resemble this. For this reason, within the *Avataṃsaka*, worlds are frequently used as metaphors for the virtues of the Buddhas.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O Sons of the Buddha!

This Flower Bank Adorned World-Ocean is the place where Vairocana Tathāgata, in the past, while practicing the bodhisattva path for as many eons as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, drew near to as many Buddhas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds during each and every eon."
It is purified by the adornment of great vows as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
O Sons of the Buddha, this Flower Bank Adorned Ocean of Worlds is supported by wind-circles as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru.
The lowest of these wind-circles is named "Abiding in Equality," which is able to support all the blazing, jewel-flame adornments above it. Above that...
The wind-circle named "Various Jewel Adornments Arising" can support the king of mani-jewel banners that emit pure light above it.
Above that is the wind-circle named "Jewel Splendor," which can support all the jewel bells above it.
Above that is the wind-circle named "Equal Flame," which can support the wheel of the sun-light-marked mani-king above it. Above that...
The wind-circle is named Various Universal Adornments; it can support the Flower of the Radiant Wheel above it.
Next, the wind-circle is named Universally Pure; it can support the Lion Throne of All Flower Flames above it.
Next, the wind-circle is named Sound Pervading the Ten Directions; it can support the Banner of All Jewel Kings above it. Next, the wind-circle is named All... [text ends]
The Jewel Radiance [Wind]. It can support all the mani-king tree flowers above it. Next above is the wind-circle named Swift Universal Support;
it can support all the fragrant mani-Sumeru clouds above it. Next above is the wind-circle named Wandering Through Various Palaces;
it can support all the clouds of jewel-colored fragrance terraces above it. O Children of the Buddha!
The wind-circle at the very summit of those wind-circles, as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, is named Repository of Supreme Majestic Radiance;
it supports the Fragrant Water Sea Adorned with Universal Light Maṇis.

Within this fragrant water sea is a great lotus flower named Banner of Fragrance with Various Radiant Filaments, and within it resides the Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean, which is perfectly symmetrical in the four directions.
It was level, pure, and firm, surrounded on all sides by the Cakravāḍa Mountains. The lands, oceans, and various trees each had their own distinct characteristics.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, relied upon the Buddha’s spiritual power and surveyed the ten directions.
And he spoke in verse:
"Because the World-Honored One cultivated pure deeds in the presence of as many Buddhas as atoms of dust throughout all realms of existence in the past,
he has attained this Flower Treasury Adorned Ocean of Worlds with its various jewel radiances."

A vast cloud of compassion pervades all; having sacrificed bodies as numerous as the atoms of infinite lands, through the power of practice over oceans of past eons, this world is now free from all defilements.
Emitting great light that dwells throughout space, it is sustained by the power of the wind and remains unshakable.
The Buddha-treasury mani jewels are universally adorned, purified by the Tathāgata’s power of vows;
mani-flower treasuries are scattered everywhere, abiding in the sky through the power of past vows.
An ocean of various firm adornments, with clouds of light streaming down, fills the ten directions.
From within all the mani-jewels, clouds of Bodhisattvas emerge, universally proceeding to the ten directions;
their blazing light forms wheels of exquisite floral adornments. They circulate throughout the entire Dharma-realm without exception, emitting pure radiance from within every jewel;
that light shines universally upon the ocean of sentient beings.
Pervading all the lands of the ten directions, they cause all beings to emerge from suffering and turn toward Bodhi;
as numerous as the atoms within the Buddhas, emanations such as Brahmā, Śakra,
and Cakravartin kings issue forth from every pore— emanations of all sentient beings and all Buddhas.
He manifests light that is equal to the Dharma-realm; within that light, he proclaims the names of all Buddhas, employing various skillful means to demonstrate their taming of beings.
He universally responds to the minds of all without exception.
Within every single atom of all the worlds in the Flower Treasury (Kusumatalagarbha), one perceives the entire Dharma-realm.
Buddhas of Jewel Light appear like gathering clouds;
this is the Tathāgata’s sovereign and vast vow-cloud pervading the Dharma-realm.
Throughout all kalpas, they transform sentient beings, and the practices of Samantabhadra’s ground of wisdom are fully accomplished; all adornments emerge from this.

The following section, which explains the text of this chapter, is divided into three parts: first, the elucidation of the essential nature of the Flower Treasury (*Flower-Garland*) world-system as both cause and fruit;

second, the elucidation of the abiding and adornments of the ocean of treasuries; and third, the elucidation of the distinctions within the network of lands it sustains. This section contains both prose and verse. Now, for the first part:
it points out that this Flower Garland (*Avataṃsaka*) ocean of worlds was purified by my own Teacher through his cultivation of causes, thereby manifesting the profundity of those causes.

"Vast": practicing for eons as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of lands implies a long duration; encountering Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of lands implies it is not merely one Buddha;
fulfilling vows as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of lands purified implies it is not merely the practice of non-arising. Thus, it is called "profound and vast.

This reveals the profundity of the cause, which pertains to those who have attained the fruit. Next, the following section clarifies the essence and characteristics of the fruit to demonstrate its expansive capacity.

Next, we shall distinguish the wind-circles (*vāyu-maṇḍala*) that support the world. The text states: "In this Flower Treasury World (*Puṣpasaṃbhava-lokadhātu*), there are wind-circles as numerous as the atoms of dust that support it.
This clarifies that the wind-circles act as the supporting agents (*dhāraka*), while the Flower Treasury realm is that which is supported (*dheya*).
These wind-circles have many names; the most supreme among them is called the "Treasury of Supreme Majestic Radiance" (*Vaijayanta-tejo-garbha*). This is formed by the accumulation of many winds.
Taking the wheel as that which is capable of supporting, that which is accumulated becomes thick; thus, there is the power to support.
That which is supported is the lowest of all, the great ocean named *Samantaprabhā-maṇi-vyūha-gandha-jala-samudra*.
This is the universal ocean of the Flower Treasury (*Kusumatalagarbha*), which is itself the world-ocean. Next, it says that within this fragrant water ocean there is a lotus flower named "Seed..."
"Various light-kalpa-lotus-fragrance-banners. This collectively refers to a single lotus flower within the ocean of fragrant waters.
Within this [lotus] are contained oceans of fragrant water as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field (*buddhakṣetra*), each containing lotuses that support many buddha-fields;
these constitute an "ocean of fields" (*kṣetrasamudra*). Therefore, it is subsequently stated: "Within the great earth of this world-ocean, there are unspeakably many buddha-fields."
There are as many oceans of fragrant water as there are atoms. These oceans rest upon a ground of vajra-stones supported by filaments of fragrance;

this constitutes a world-system cluster (*kṣetra-vyuha*). Within these numerous world-system clusters contained within the Banner of Filament Fragrance, each filament is a single world-system cluster, and each likewise possesses twenty tiers.
For now, we shall generally distinguish the primary world-systems, collectively named:

Regarding the ocean of world-systems: the subsequent arrangement of the network of lands clarifies the accompanying lands; therefore, it was previously stated that he dwells within the Flower Treasury Adorned Ocean of World-Systems.

The above explains how the wind-circle supports the fragrant water-ocean, from which lotus flowers emerge within the ocean, and within these flowers are contained many land-germs that form the ocean of world-systems, thereby manifesting the vast capacity of the essence of fruition.
First is the prose; next are the verses, which expound the meaning of the prose. At the end, the final two verses clarify mastery over the buddha-field (*kṣetra-vaśitā*).
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O sons of the Buddha, this Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean rests upon a lotus flower of the Sun-Jewel King atop the Great Cakravāḍa Mountains, with sandalwood *maṇi* jewels forming its base."
Its body has a king of precious jewels as its peak and exquisite fragrant *maṇi* gems as its rim.
It is established by the *vajra* of the treasury of flames, with streams of all kinds of perfumed water flowing through it. Forests of various jewels abound, and wondrous flowers bloom;
fragrant herbs carpet the ground, interspersed with bright pearls. All manner of incense and flowers fill every place, and *maṇi*...
It formed a net that hung down all around, providing a canopy. There were such arrays of exquisite adornments, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
The great oceans of the world are boundless; Their various pure jewel wheels possess every kind of wondrous adornment.
These arise through the spiritual power of the Tathāgata:
Wheels of exquisite maṇi jewels, And wheels of sublime fragrant incense, As well as wheels of pearl lamp-flames.
Adorned with various kinds of exquisite jewels, it rests securely within a pure perimeter;
its core is composed of firm maṇi-gems,
and it is embellished with Jāmbūnada gold that radiates light and flames throughout the ten directions, transparent and pure both inside and out.
Accumulated from vajra-maṇis, it rains down further various exquisite maṇi jewels;
these treasures are wondrous and diverse, emitting pure light that is universally magnificent and beautiful.
Fragrant waters flow in infinite colors, scattering various flowers, jewels, and sandalwood.
Multitudes of lotuses bloom in competition like spread garments; Precious grasses grow in profusion, all fragrant and sweet.
Infinite jewel trees provide universal adornment, Blossoming with flowers and emerging stamens of blazing color.
Various kinds of famous garments are within them, As clouds of light shine everywhere, ever perfectly full.
Immeasurable and boundless great bodhisattvas hold canopies and burn incense that fills the entire dharma-realm;
they all produce every kind of wondrous sound and universally turn the Tathāgata’s true wheel of Dharma.
These are formed from the precious powder of mani-trees, and each grain of precious powder manifests radiant light.
The pure body of Vairocana enters into all of them,
causing all to see the Buddha-body manifest within every adornment; with infinite forms and countless colors,
it pervades the ten directions without exception, and the sentient beings thus transformed are likewise limitless.
From all adornments, wondrous sounds emerge, Proclaiming the wheel of the Tathāgata’s original vows;
Throughout the oceans of pure lands in the ten directions, The Buddha’s sovereign power causes them all to be pervaded.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O sons of the Buddha, this world-ocean Great Wheel..."
The entire ground within the encircling mountains is composed entirely of vajra; it is firm, magnificently adorned, and indestructible.
It is pure and level, without any elevations or depressions. It has wheels made of maṇi and treasuries made of various jewels.
It is interspersed with all kinds of maṇi gems in the shapes of various sentient beings, and is strewn with powdered jewels. It is spread over...
Lotuses and portions of *gandhagarbha* maṇi-jewels were placed at intervals between them.
All manner of ornaments filled the space like clouds, adorned with every kind of embellishment found in all the Buddha-lands of the three periods of time.
A net of exquisite *maṇi* jewels was spread throughout, universally manifesting all the realms of the Tathāgatas, arranged therein like the net of Indra. All...
"O Son of the Buddha, this world-ocean of lands possesses such adornments as these, numbering as many as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:"
The ground is level and utterly pure, Firmly established and indestructible.
It is adorned everywhere with mani-jewels, With various precious gems interspersed throughout;
The diamond ground is most delightful, Adorned with jewel wheels and jeweled nets.
Lotus blossoms spread upon them, all perfectly full; Exquisite robes cover them entirely and pervasively.
Bodhisattvas’ celestial crowns and precious necklaces Are all spread upon the ground as a magnificent adornment.
Sandalwood and mani-jewels are scattered throughout, All radiating pure and wondrous light.
Precious flowers burst forth with flames, emitting wondrous light; The light and flames, like clouds, illuminate all things.
These wondrous flowers and various jewels are scattered, Universally covering the ground as a magnificent adornment.
Dense clouds arise and spread, filling the ten directions; Their vast and great radiance is inexhaustible.
Reaching everywhere to all lands in the ten directions, He proclaims the Tathāgata’s nectar-like Dharma;
Within the wish-fulfilling jewel of all Buddhas’ vows, The boundless and vast kalpas are universally manifested.
Whatever the Supreme Knower practiced in the past, None of it fails to appear within this jewel.
All the maṇi jewels found upon that ground enter into every single buddha-field;
within each atom of those various buddha-fields, all lands likewise enter.
This Flower Treasury World-realm is adorned with exquisite jewels, and bodhisattvas travel throughout the ten directions.
Proclaiming the great vows of the Bodhisattvas—this is the ground adorned with the exquisite jewels of sovereign power within the site of enlightenment.
Emitting pure radiance and arrayed with every ornament, it fills the Dharma-realm as vast as space;
through the Buddha’s power, it manifests spontaneously in this way.
Those who have cultivated the vows of Samantabhadra— The wise ones who enter the realm of the Buddhas can know this ocean of lands; All such miraculous transformations as these.
Then, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O Sons of the Buddha, in this ocean of worlds, the great earth..."
Within it, there are ten times the number of incalculable Buddha-lands of fragrant water oceans.
Their bottoms are adorned with all manner of exquisite jewels; their shores are adorned with exquisite fragrance-maṇis; and nets made of Vairocana-maṇi jewel-kings cover them.
The fragrant waters are transparent and possess the colors of all kinds of jewels, filling the space within. Various precious flowers swirl and are spread throughout.
Above it, fine sandalwood powder settled as a clear sediment; below it, the melodic voice of the Buddha’s speech resounded and precious light was emitted.
Boundless bodhisattvas held various canopies and manifested supernatural powers, such that all the adornments existing in every world were reflected therein.
Ten precious stairways were arranged in rows, and ten precious railings surrounded it on all sides. The four heavenly kings...
There were lotuses as numerous as the atoms of the lower realms, adorned with all kinds of jewels, blooming and flourishing in the water.

There were banners of the ten precious *śīla* (virtues) numbering in the hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas, which are unspeakable; there were banners of nets of bells and robes made of all kinds of jewels, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
and there were pavilions of jewel-flowers with boundless colors and forms, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, numbering in the hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas.
He manifested tens of millions of precious lotus-flower cities. Within them were groves of jewel trees as numerous as the atoms in the four continents, with nets made of flaming mani-jewels.

They were completely surrounded on all sides by walls of various jewels, numbering in the hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas—as ineffable as the sands of the Ganges—and filled with the fragrant sandalwood incense and the vocal teachings of the Buddhas.
Adorned [with these marks], at that time the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, relying on the Buddha’s spiritual power,
surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
Upon the great earth within this world-system, there is a fragrant ocean of perfumed water,
adorned with maṇi jewels and purified by the distribution of wondrous gems at its bottom;
it is established upon indestructible vajra-ground and has shores formed by heaps of fragrant-treasury maṇi jewels, while wheels of sun-flame pearls are spread over it like clouds.
Adorned everywhere with exquisite lotus-jewel necklaces, pure and stainless,
the fragrant waters are serene and possess every hue; precious flowers swirl and spread, emitting radiant light,
while a universal resonance of sound is heard far and near as the Buddha’s majestic power proclaims the wondrous Dharma.
The stairways are adorned with a multitude of jewels, further embellished with mani-gems as interspersed decorations;
the surrounding railings are entirely made of precious gems.
Nets of lotus pearls are spread like clouds, and rows of mani-jewel trees stand in formation, their blossoms and stamens in full bloom, radiating brilliant light.
Various musical sounds are constantly played in competition;
by the Buddha’s power of supernatural transformations, such various wonderful jewel *puṇḍarīka* lotuses are spread out as adornments upon the fragrant water-ocean.
Fragrant flames and radiant light never cease for a moment, vast and perfect, pervading everywhere.
Luminous jewel banners are ever blazing, And exquisite robes hang down as adornments.
Nets of mani-bells proclaim the sound of Dharma, Causing all who hear them to advance toward Buddha-wisdom.
Exquisite jewel lotuses form the city walls, Resplendent with ornaments of multicolored mani-gems.
Pearl cloud-shadows spread across the four quarters; thus adorned, the walls of the fragrant water-ocean encircle it completely on all sides.
Multi-storied pavilions face one another arrayed upon them, with immeasurable radiance constantly blazing forth—a sea of various adornments, pure and serene.
In the past, Vairocana purified all manner of oceans of lands;
such vastness is boundless, for it is entirely the sovereign power of the Tathāgata.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O Sons of the Buddha, within each and every ocean of fragrant water..."
There are rivers of fragrant water, as numerous as the atoms in the four continents, which encircle [the land] turning to the right.

All of them have diamond for their banks and are adorned with mani-jewels of pure radiance. They constantly manifest clouds of jewel-colored light from all Buddhas, as well as the voices and sounds of all sentient beings.
In every place where these rivers form whirlpools, there are the practices cultivated by all Buddhas.
From within it emerge all manner of causal activities and diverse forms. Nets of *maṇi* jewels, clusters of various precious bells, and all the adornments of the oceans of worlds appear therein.

Clouds of *maṇi* jewels cover its summit, and from these clouds manifest everywhere the Flower Treasury World, Vairocana, the transformation Buddhas of the ten directions, and the spiritual powers of all Buddhas.
...these matters. Furthermore, they emit wondrous sounds, extolling the names of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time.
From within those fragrant waters, clouds of light-flames of all kinds of jewels constantly emerge in continuous succession without ceasing.

To speak of them in detail, each river possesses adornments as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds. At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s [empowerment].
By his supernormal power, he surveyed the ten directions and spoke these verses:
A pure stream of fragrance fills the great river;
Its banks are made of wondrous vajra jewels, And its ground is spread with wheels of precious powder— All manner of adornments are exquisitely beautiful.
Rows of jeweled stairways are exquisitely adorned, with railings all around that are most magnificent;
filled with pearls and decorated with various flowers, diverse necklaces and garlands hang down together.
With the pure colors of fragrant waters and jewel-lights, they constantly emit mani-gems that flow forth in rapid competition.
Multitudes of flowers sway with the waves, All playing music to proclaim the wondrous Dharma.
Fine sandalwood powder forms the mud and silt, While all manner of exquisite jewels swirl together;
Clouds of fragrant treasuries spread throughout the midst, Emitting flames and flowing scents everywhere.
Within the river, various wondrous jewels are produced, all emitting light of blazing colors;
their radiance spreads shadows to form pedestals and seats, complete with flower canopies and pearl necklaces.
Within the sovereign maṇi jewel, the body of a Buddha appears, its light universally illuminating the lands of the ten directions.
Using these as wheels to adorn the ground, The fragrant waters are transparent, clear, and ever-full.
A net of mani-jewels with golden bells Completely covers the fragrant rivers, proclaiming the Buddha’s voice.
It fully expounds all paths to enlightenment And the sublime practices of Samantabhadra.
The mani-jewels on the jeweled banks are utterly pure, Constantly emitting the sounds of the Tathāgatas’ original vows;
The past practices of all Buddhas Are universally proclaimed by those sounds, causing all to see them.
From every place where the river has whirlpools, Bodhisattvas constantly emerge like clouds.
They all go forth into vast buddha-fields, filling them entirely throughout the dharma-realm;
pure jewel-kings are spread like clouds, completely covering all fragrant rivers.
These jewels, equal to the mark between the Buddha’s eyebrows, vividly manifest the reflections of all Buddhas.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha, the ground between these rivers of fragrant water is entirely adorned with various kinds of wondrous jewels.

In each location, there are *puṇḍarīka* flowers adorned with various jewels, as numerous as the atoms in four continents, filling the area completely on every side, each numbering as many as the atoms in four continents."
Numerous groves of jewel trees were arranged in successive rows.
From each individual tree, clouds of every kind of adornment constantly issued forth, with sovereign *maṇi* jewels shining amidst them. Various flowers and fragrances filled every place.
Furthermore, those trees produced subtle and wondrous sounds, proclaiming the great vows cultivated by all Tathāgatas throughout all kalpas, while scattering various [flowers].
Various kingly mani-jewels filled the ground, namely: the lotus-wheel kingly mani-jewel, the fragrant-flame-light-cloud kingly mani-jewel,
the variously adorned kingly mani-jewel, the kingly mani-jewel manifesting inconceivable colors of adornment,
and the sun-light-radiant-garment-treasury kingly mani-jewel, pervading throughout the ten directions.
There were *maṇi-rāja* jewels like clouds of radiating light-nets; *maṇi-rāja* jewels manifesting the spiritual transformations of all Buddhas;
*maṇi-rāja* jewels manifesting the ocean of karmic retributions of all sentient beings. Such [jewels] were as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
Every single portion of land between those fragrant water rivers was fully endowed with such adornments. At that time...
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to reiterate this meaning, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"The ground is level and utterly pure, Adorned with both true gold and mani-jewels."
Rows of trees shade the midst of it, their towering trunks and drooping branches clustering like clouds;
their branches are adorned with exquisite jewels, and wheels of radiant blossoms shine in all directions.
Jeweled *maṇi* fruits are spread out like clouds, causing [the scene] to be constantly visible throughout the ten directions.
The ground is completely covered with mani-jewels, Adorned together with various flowers and precious powders;
Furthermore, palaces are fashioned from mani-jewels, In which the reflections of all sentient beings appear.
Mani-kings, the reflections of all Buddhas, Are scattered everywhere across that ground, reaching every place.
Thus blazing forth throughout the ten directions, within every single atom, all Buddhas are seen;
Exquisite jewels are beautifully distributed, with pearl lamp-nets interspersed and interwoven;
Everywhere there are mani-wheels, each manifesting the spiritual powers of the Buddha.
Adorned with myriad jewels, they radiate great light; within that light, emanated Buddhas appear everywhere, each traveling in circuitous course until no place is left unvisited.
With the ten powers, they extensively expound the Dharma;
exquisite mani-jewels and white lotuses fill every body of water.
Their flowers are of various kinds, each distinct, All manifesting boundless and inexhaustible radiance.
All the adornments existing throughout the three times Are clearly revealed within the mani fruit;
Their essential nature is unborn and ungraspable— This is the sovereign power of the Tathāgata.
Within all the adornments of this ground, The vast body of the Tathāgata appears in its entirety;
Yet he neither comes nor goes— Through the power of the Buddha’s past vows, all are made to see him.
Within every single atom of this ground, All the children of the Buddha practice the path.
Each beholds the lands they are prophesied to attain in the future; according to their aspirations, all are completely pure.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha, the adornments of the world-oceans of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, are inconceivable. Why is this? O Sons of the Buddha, this Flower Treasury Adorned World..."
The oceans of all realms are each adorned with pure merits as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s spiritual power,
surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
In every place within this ocean of worlds, all are adorned with various jewels;
flames burst forth, soaring into the sky like clouds, their light penetrating and constantly pervading everywhere.
From the *maṇi* gems, clouds of light are emitted without end, and within them appear the reflected images of the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Supernatural transformations never cease; all bodhisattvas have gathered here.
All the mani-jewels emit the Buddha’s voice, a sound exquisite and inconceivable.
The deeds performed by Vairocana in the past are constantly heard and seen within these jewels.
The Honored One of Pure Radiance, Pervasive Illumination, Appears as reflections within every ornament;
Surrounded by a host of transformed emanations, He pervades all oceans of worlds.
All these manifested Buddhas are like illusions; If one seeks their point of origin, it cannot be found.
By the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha’s realm, such manifestations appear within all lands;
the Tathāgata’s sovereign deeds of supernatural power pervade all the countries of the ten directions.
Through this ocean of lands purified and adorned, all are seen within the jewels.
All the various manifestations throughout the ten directions Are entirely like images within a mirror;
They arise solely through the power of the Tathāgata’s past conduct And his supernormal powers and vows.
If there are those who can cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra, They shall enter the ocean of the Bodhisattvas’ supreme wisdom.
Able to manifest their bodies universally within all atoms,
purifying inconceivable billions of great eons of buddha-fields; drawing near to all Tathāgatas and manifesting,
in a single kṣaṇa, all their various modes of conduct.
The lands of all Buddhas are like space—ineffable, unarisen, and without marks;
yet for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, they are universally adorned and purified, and by the power of their original vows, they abide therein.

The following section is the second part, which specifically clarifies the arrangement and adornment. This text is divided into six sections. The first concerns the circular mountain ranges surrounding [the world].
1. The Ground of Two Jewels; 2. The Fragrant Ocean; 3. The Fragrant River; 4. The Forests; 5. The Trees; 6. A General Summary of Each. Regarding the first:
it is called the "Ground of the Sun-Jewel King" because it is the ground upon which [Mount Meru] rests. The older translation states that it "rests upon a ground of lotus-sun-jewel kings.
There is also a view that above the great lotus there is a separate flower which serves as the support for the mountain; this interpretation seems plausible.
This is not the case. The reason the ground receives this name is that it was previously called "Various Radiant Filaments" (*vicitrābhāsa-kesara*).
The verse states that "flames form a wheel," and further says that "pure radiance is emitted from among all jewels.
Thus, we know that these flowers have jewels as their substance. This is like the jewel-kings of the solar disc; they are precisely the filaments of the fragrant lotus.
This is the general designation for the flowers. This serves as the general indication of the ground upon which they rest.

Next, the phrase "with sandalwood and mani-jewels as its body" specifically reveals the characteristics of its substance. Finally, the single phrase "and so forth" concludes by manifesting their inexhaustibility. Following this, there is a repeated exposition in verse.
The first part clarifies the adornment of the mountain’s substance, versifying what was previously explained specifically. The first verse versifies the surrounding [enclosure].
1. One verse praises the mountain range; 2. one verse praises the mountain rim; 3. one verse praises the body of the mountain; 4. one verse praises the conditions of the mountain; 5.
two verses praise the preceding elements such as water; 6. four verses clarify the sovereign and wondrous functions of the mountain.
Next, from the passage beginning "At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly," there are prose and verse sections clarifying the Jewel Grounds (*ratnabhūmi*).
Next, from the passage beginning "At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly," there are prose and verse sections clarifying the Fragrant Ocean (*gandhasāgara*).
Next, from the passage beginning "At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly," there are prose and verse sections.
The section beginning with "At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly" and continuing through the prose and verse explains the fragrant rivers.
Next, the section beginning with "At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly" and continuing through the prose and verse explains the forest trees.

Following this, the section beginning with "In summary, the aforementioned adornments are unfathomable" provides the explanation for the reasons behind these descriptions. All of the above collectively elucidates the ocean of treasuries.
The arrangement and adornment having been completed, the following clarifies the net of world-systems it sustains.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying: "O Sons of the Buddha, what kinds of worlds abide herein?
I shall now explain. O Sons of the Buddha, these ten [arrays] are as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields of incense..."
Within the ocean of waters, there abide world-systems as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
Within each individual world-system, there are further worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
