O Sons of the Buddha, those various world-systems within the ocean of worlds each have their own basis of support, each their own shape, and each their own essential nature.

In each respective location, each respective entrance, each respective adornment, each respective boundary, each respective arrangement, each respectively without distinction, and each respectively empowered by strength—O Sons of the Buddha!
This world-system may rest upon a great lotus-ocean; or it may rest upon an ocean of jewel-flowers of boundless colors; or it may rest upon all...
They dwell upon oceans of pearl-treasury jewel necklaces; some dwell supported by fragrant water oceans;
some dwell supported by oceans of all kinds of flowers; some dwell supported by oceans of mani-jewel nets; and some dwell supported by oceans of revolving radiant light.
Some abide supported by oceans of Bodhisattvas’ jewel-adorned crowns; some abide supported by oceans of the bodies of various sentient beings;
some abide supported by oceans of mani-jewel kings of the voices of all Buddhas.
If these were to be explained in detail, they would number as many as the atoms within an ocean of world-systems. O Sons of the Buddha, among all those world-lineages, some are formed...
In the shape of Mount Sumeru; or in the shape of rivers and streams; or in the shape of revolving wheels;

or in the shape of swirling currents; or in the shape of wheel-rims; or in the shape of sacrificial altars; or in the shape of groves of trees; or in the shape of multi-storied pavilions; or in the shape of mountain banners;
or in the shape of universal squares; or in the shape of a *garbhadhātu*; or in the shape of a lotus flower; or...
They take the form of *khaḷuṅka* (wild horses), or the forms of sentient beings, or the form of clouds,
or the forms of the marks and signs of the Buddhas, or the form of perfect radiance, or the form of various jeweled nets,
or the form of all manner of gates and portals, or the form of various ornaments. If these were explained in detail, they would constitute world-systems.
"O Sons of the Buddha, as numerous as the atoms in the ocean, those various world-systems have, some, the clouds of mani-jewels of the ten directions as their substance;
some, the flames of manifold colors as their substance; some, various radiances as their substance;
some, the flames of precious incense as their substance; and some, the *tāla*-flowers adorned with all kinds of jewels as their substance."
Some have as their essence the image of a bodhisattva; some have as their essence the radiance of all Buddhas;
some have as their essence the physical marks of a Buddha; some have as their essence the light of a single jewel; some have as their essence the light of many jewels;
some have as their essence the sounds of the ocean of merit of all sentient beings; some have as their essence a single...
It has as its essence the sounds of the ocean of karmas of all sentient beings; or it has as its essence the pure sounds of the realm of all Buddhas;
or it has as its essence the sounds of the ocean of great vows of all Bodhisattvas;
or it has as its essence the sounds of the skillful means of all Buddhas; or it has as its essence the completion of the ornaments of all lands.
It has the destruction of sound as its essence. Alternatively, it may have the boundless voices of the Buddhas as its essence;
or it may have the transformative voices of all Buddhas as its essence; or it may have the virtuous voices of all sentient beings as its essence;
or it may have the pure voices from the ocean of all Buddhas' merits as its essence. If these were explained in detail...

There were as many such [worlds] as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds. At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
The world-systems are firm, wondrously adorned, vast, pure, and treasuries of radiant light;
they rest upon oceans of jewel-lotuses, or take the forms of fragrant oceans, Mount Sumerus, cities, trees, or sacrificial altars. All these world-systems pervade the ten directions.
Various ornaments and distinct forms are each arrayed and established;
some have bodies of pure radiance, while others are made of Flower Treasury and jewel clouds.
Some world-systems are formed from flames, abiding within indestructible treasuries of mani-jewels.
The radiance of lamp-clouds, flames, and brilliant light, Various infinite and pure colors,
Or those whose essence consists of speech and sound— These are the inconceivable manifestations expounded by the Buddha,
Or sounds produced through the power of his vows, Whose fundamental nature is the voice of miraculous transformation.
The great meritorious karma of all sentient beings, And the sound of the Buddha’s virtues are likewise;
Each distinct gate of the world-systems, Inconceivable and without end,
Thus pervading all the ten directions, Manifests spiritual power through vast adornment.
All the vast lands throughout the ten directions Come entirely into this world-system;
Though they are seen to enter everywhere within it, In truth, there is no coming and no entering.
One land-system enters all, And all enter one, without exception.
The essence and characteristics are as they originally were, without distinction;
equalless and immeasurable, they pervade all lands within the atoms of every realm.
Everywhere one sees the Tathāgata within the ocean of his vows, his voice like the roll of thunder, taming all sentient beings.
The Buddha’s body pervades all lands, And countless bodhisattvas likewise fill them.
The Tathāgata’s sovereign power is peerless, Universally transforming all sentient beings.
This concludes the third section, explaining the supported net of lands. It explains the term "world" (*loka*) in the title of the chapter. Furthermore, as previously clarified:

This [section] concerns the primary lands; now, to clarify the secondary lands, both the defiled and the pure are treated together. First, he addresses the great assembly and grants permission to speak.
Second, from the words "O sons of the Buddha" onwards, the headings are established, listing two categories: world-systems (*lokadhātu-jāla*) and worlds (*lokadhātu*).

Now, world-systems depend upon oceans of lands, and worldly fruits depend upon world-systems; proceeding from the broad to the narrow, this is intended to clarify that worlds are boundless, and thus serves as a skillful means to manifest this truth.
Because they are many, this name is established. That is to say, many worlds are accumulated together in one place; because they encompass all various categories, they are called "species" (*gotra*).
Furthermore, such species are themselves numerous, being profound, vast, and boundless; therefore, they are called an "ocean" (*sāgara*).
In this way, these numerous worlds are like the net of Indra, suspended and spread throughout the Flower Treasury Ocean;
therefore, they are called the "supported net of lands. Since the shapes upon which each individual world rests and abides are all different, they are called "distinctive.
Thus, the subsequent sutra says: "O Sons of the Buddha, those various world-systems within the ocean of worlds..."
Regarding "each according to their abodes" and so forth, it clarifies that there are ten distinct categories of differentiation. In the sutra, the phrase "unspeakable buddha-fields" appears;
the commentary states that the word "ten" has been omitted, and it should read "ten unspeakables.
In the prose section, the phrase "all you sons of the Buddha" occurs, which merely explains in sequence the three matters of abode, shape, and nature. In the verse, this constitutes the first stanza.
The first verse summarizes the basis and abiding; next, one verse summarizes the shape; third, three verses summarize the essential nature;

fourth, three verses summarize the three matters—namely, the extent of the entry and the adornments; fifth, one verse summarizes the lack of differentiation; sixth, one verse summarizes the sustaining power.
Above this, the distinctions of the supported net of lands are clarified; that is to say, within the ocean of lands...
There are world-systems as numerous as the atoms within ten unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, each resting upon the ocean of worlds.
Like the Indra-net, they are infinitely layered and inexhaustible; for now, let us clarify that these world-systems differ from one another.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:

"O Sons of the Buddha, these ten times unspeakably many oceans of fragrant water, as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, abide within the Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean, distributed like the net of Indra.
O Sons of the Buddha, this most central ocean of fragrant water is named Boundless Light of Wondrous Flowers."
It has as its base a king of mani-jewels banner that manifests the forms of all bodhisattvas,
from which emerges a great lotus named Adorned with All Fragrant Mani Kings. Upon it rests a world-system named Blazing Jewel Radiance Universally Illuminating the Ten Directions,
which consists of all manner of ornaments and contains ten unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.

Dust-mote-like worlds are arrayed therein. At the very bottom is a world named Supreme Light Pervading Illumination, bounded by a radiant wheel adorned with all vajras, resting upon flowers of various precious maṇi-jewels.
Its shape is like that of a maṇi-gem, and it is completely covered above by clouds of ornaments made of all kinds of jewel-flowers.
It is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, abiding in various ways and adorned with various ornaments.
The Buddha there is named Pure Eye, Lamp Free from Defilement.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, there is a world named Various Fragrant Lotus Wondrous Adornments, bounded by all manner of ornamental implements and resting upon a jewel lotus.
It is established as a net, its form resembling a lion throne. Canopies of clouds made of pearls of every precious color completely cover it above.
It is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms within two buddha-fields. The Buddha there is named Lion Light Supreme Illumination.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, there is a world named Adorned with All Jewels.
The world-system named Universal Radiance has a wheel of fragrant wind as its boundary and rests upon various jewel-flower necklaces.
It is octagonal in shape and covered above by clouds of sun-discs of exquisite light and the sun of Mānuṣī. It is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in three buddha-fields.
The Buddha there is named Banner of Supreme Wisdom of Pure Light. Above this, passing through worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field...
There is a world-system named Various Radiant Flower Adornments.
It has all kinds of jewel-kings as its boundaries and rests upon an ocean of multicolored vajra-śīla-banners.
Its shape is like a mani-lotus, covered above by clouds of light from vajra-maṇi jewels, and it is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in four buddha-fields.
It is entirely pure. The Buddha’s name is Vajraprabhāpramāṇavīryasudarsana (Golden Light Infinite Diligence Well-Appeared).

Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Samantamuktapuṣpābhāsa (Universally Radiating Exquisite Flower Light), which has a network of all-jeweled bells as its boundary and rests upon an ocean of jewel-wheel networks adorned with all kinds of forests.
Its shape is universally square and possesses many corners. It is covered above by clouds of *maṇi* kings of Brahma-sounds.
It is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms within five buddha-fields. The Buddha there is named Fragrant Light Joyful Power Ocean.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, there is a world named Pure and Wondrous Radiance, adorned with jewel kings.
Its boundary is the Banner of Adornment, resting upon an ocean of vajra palaces. It is square in shape and covered above by clouds of canopies with topknots of maṇi wheels.
It is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in six buddha-fields. The Buddha there is named Universal Light Sovereign Banner.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Multitude of Flowers.
It is adorned with flames, with various flowers serving as its borders, and it rests upon an ocean of flames of every precious color.
Its form is like that of a multi-storied pavilion, covered above by clouds of railings made of pearls and garments of every precious color.
It is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in seven buddha-fields, being entirely pure. The Buddha’s name is *Ānanda* (Joy).

Joyful Ocean of Merits, Renowned Sovereign Light. Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Ground of Manifesting Majestic Power, which has the adornment of all-sound-manifesting mani-jewel kings as its boundary.
It rests upon a sea of space supported by lotus thrones of various jewel colors, its form resembling Indra’s net.
It is covered above by clouds of flower-nets of boundless colors and is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in eight buddha-fields.
The Buddha there is named Wisdom-Ocean Banner of Vast Renown. Beyond this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field...
World System. There is a world-system named Producing Exquisite Sounds.
It is bounded by wheels adorned with mind-king maṇi-jewels, and it rests upon an ocean of maṇi-jewel kings adorned with clouds that constantly emit all kinds of exquisite sounds.
Its form is like the body of Brahmā, and it is covered above by clouds of lion thrones adorned with immeasurable jewels. It encompasses nine buddha-fields.
It was surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as atoms. The Buddha there was named Pure Moonlight Radiance Mark Unconquerable.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as atoms of a buddha-field, there is a world named Vajra Banner, whose boundaries are adorned with necklaces of pearls from the treasury of infinite ornaments, resting upon a lion throne of every kind of ornamented jewel.
It rests upon an ocean of mani-jewels and is circular in shape.

It is completely covered by clouds of all-fragrant mani-flowers as numerous as the atoms in ten Mount Sumerus, and it is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields.
It is purely and uniformly pure. The Buddha’s name is Sovereign King of the Ocean of All Dharmas.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Constantly Manifesting Sapphire Radiance.
It is bounded by an extremely firm and indestructible diamond ornamentation and rests upon an ocean of various extraordinary flowers; its shape is like that of—
It is shaped like a half-moon. Canopies of various celestial jewels cover it like clouds.
It is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in eleven buddha-fields. The Buddha there is named Infinite Merit Dharma.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Radiant Illumination, which has universal light-adornment as its boundary and rests upon a lotus.
It abides within a swirling sea of fragrant water, shaped like a whorl of flowers.
It is covered above by clouds of various garments and is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in twelve buddha-fields. The Buddha there is named Surpassing Śakra and Brahmā.
Above this, passing through worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, one reaches this world named Sahā, which has a boundary adorned with vajras and rests upon—
It rests upon a lotus net supported by wind-circles of various colors, appearing like empty space.
It is covered above by clouds of celestial palaces that adorn the void with universal perfection, and it is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in thirteen buddha-fields.
That Buddha is the World-Honored One, Vairocana Tathāgata. Beyond this is the Buddha...
In worlds as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field, there is a world named Tranquil Light Free from Dust.
It is bounded by adornments of all kinds of jewels and rests upon an ocean of various precious garments.
Its shape is like that of Vajrapāṇi, and it is covered above by clouds of vajras of infinite colors. It is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms of fourteen buddha-fields.
Circling around, there is a Buddha named Supreme Sound Pervading the Dharma Realm.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Lamp of Myriad Sublime Radiances, bounded by canopies of all manner of adornments and resting upon a sea of pure flower-nets.
Its shape is like that of the svastika, and it is covered above by clouds from seas of fragrant water and mani-trees.
It is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in fifteen Buddha-fields, all of which are purely and uniformly pure.
The Buddha there is named Indestructible Power Universal Radiance Banner.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field, there is a world named Pure Light Pervasive Illumination, bounded by infinite jewel-cloud *maṇi* kings and resting upon various fragrances.
It rests upon a sea of flaming lotuses, its shape resembling the shell of a tortoise.
It is covered above by a circular radiance of maṇi-wheels and sandalwood clouds, and is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in sixteen buddha-fields.
The Buddha there is named Pure Sun Virtue Eye. Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named...
The Treasury of Jewel Adornments has as its boundary the king of *maṇi* jewels in the forms of all sentient beings. It rests upon the ocean of *maṇi* jewel kings of the treasury of light.
Its shape is octagonal, and it is completely covered above by nets of flower trees adorned with the jewels of all the Cakravāḍa mountains.
It is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in seventeen buddha-fields. The Buddha’s name is [Unobstructed... (the name is incomplete in the source).
The light of obstructing wisdom shines universally throughout the ten directions. Above this, past as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Free from Dust.

It is bounded by all manner of exquisite and wonderful marks, rests upon a sea of lion thrones of various marvelous flowers, is shaped like a pearl necklace, and is covered by clouds of circular halos from all kinds of precious fragrant mani-kings.
Above that, it was surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in eighteen buddha-fields, all of which were purely and entirely serene.
The Buddha there was named Supreme Banner of Infinite Expedient Means.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there was a world named Pure Light Shining Universally, bounded by mani-jewel kings from which inexhaustible clouds of jewels issued forth, resting upon...
It measures as vast as the colors, fragrances, flames, Mount Sumeru, oceans, and mountains, and its form is like a swirling array of precious flowers.
It is covered above by a canopy of infinite-colored radiant *maṇi* kings and sapphire clouds. It is surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in nineteen buddha-fields.
The Buddha’s name is Universal Illumination of the Dharmadhātu and Space-Light. Beyond this, past further buddha-fields...
In worlds as numerous as atoms, there is a world named Wondrous Jewel Flame.

It is bounded by jewels of universal radiance like the sun and moon, and it rests upon an ocean of *maṇi* jewel-kings in the forms of all the devas; its shape is like an ornament of precious adornment.
It was covered above by clouds of banners of all kinds of precious garments and nets of caskets of mani-lamps.
It was surrounded on all sides by worlds as numerous as the atoms in twenty buddha-fields, being entirely pure. The Buddha’s name is Radiance of the Marks of Merit.
O Children of the Buddha, within this world-system called Blazing Jewel Radiance Illumining the Ten Directions, there are such [worlds].
It encompasses as many vast worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,
each with its own basis of support, its own shape, its own essential nature, its own orientation, its own mode of entry, its own adornments, its own boundaries,
its own arrangements, its own lack of distinction, and its own surrounding encirclement by the sustaining power of spiritual strength.
That is to say: worlds in the shape of whirlpools as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields; worlds in the shape of rivers as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
worlds in the shape of swirling currents as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields; worlds in the shape of wheel-rims as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
worlds in the shape of sacrificial altars as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields; [worlds in the shape of] ten buddha-fields...
Worlds in the shape of forests as numerous as atoms; worlds in the shape of multi-storied pavilions as numerous as atoms in ten buddha-fields;
worlds in the shape of banners of ethical discipline (*śīla*) as numerous as atoms in ten buddha-fields; worlds in the shape of universal forms as numerous as atoms in ten buddha-fields;
worlds in the shape of embryonic matrices (*garbha*) as numerous as atoms in ten buddha-fields; worlds in the shape of lotuses as numerous as atoms in ten buddha-fields...
Worlds in the shape of flowers; worlds in the shape of *khāraka* fruits, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
worlds in the shapes of various sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields; and worlds in the shape of the marks of a Buddha, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields.
There are worlds shaped like the orbs of light of ten buddha-field atoms; worlds shaped like clouds of ten buddha-field atoms;
worlds shaped like nets of ten buddha-field atoms; and worlds shaped like gate-towers of ten buddha-field atoms.
Such as these are as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields. Each of these individual worlds...
There are vast worlds, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, surrounding it on all sides.
Each of these worlds, in turn, has as its retinue worlds as numerous as the aforementioned atoms.
All these described worlds are situated within this Fragrant Water Sea of Boundless Exquisite Flower Light, and they surround this sea.
Within the River of Fragrant Water.
This concludes the second section, which specifically clarifies the fragrant oceans of world-systems (*kṣetra*). To explain these two chapters together:

it means that the fragrant oceans depend upon the ocean of world-systems, the world-system clusters (*kṣetrabhedas*) depend upon the fragrant oceans, and all worlds depend upon the world-system clusters. There are both prose and verse sections; first [the prose]:

This section provides a general summary of the bases upon which the oceans rest; secondly, it specifically reveals the types of oceans and lands in their respective order; and thirdly, it offers a concise summary and explanation. This is the first part.

Although the preceding sections have only introduced the two chapters on "Lands" (*kṣetra*) and "World-Systems" (*kṣetravinyāsa*), within the explanation of the "Bases of Abiding," it was consistently stated that they rest upon oceans.
Therefore, the number of oceans is now enumerated. This "Ocean of Many Fragrances" (*Bahugandha-samudra*) is situated upon the ground of the Ocean of Lands (*Kṣetra-samudra*).
It is called the "basis" because it serves as the foundation for the face. Regarding the analogy of Indra’s net (*indrajāla*): in its general distribution, it resembles a chariot wheel.
As for its specific features, the net of Indra’s palace is formed by threading celestial pearls;
a single large pearl is placed at the center, which is then encircled by the next largest pearls, continuing in this manner, winding around one another for hundreds of thousands of turns.
If one looks at it from above, below, the four cardinal directions, or the four corners, the rows and ranks are all perfectly aligned.

Although this fragrant sea is situated upon the ground, its distribution is similar [to that of the celestial palace], and because it also possesses the meaning of "interpenetrating layers," it is said to be "like" [the celestial palace].
This merely enumerates the various oceans upon which they rest. Next, it enumerates the Fragrant Water Ocean at the very center; this specifically enumerates the types of oceans and lands (*kṣetra*).

First, it distinguishes the single ocean at the absolute center as the principal one—namely, the twenty-fold Flower Treasury World System (*padma-garbha-loka-dhātu*) at the very center—which takes one type of land (*kṣetra-vyuha*) as its principal unit. Within each of the ten directions, there is an unspeakable number [of such units].
It is surrounded by world-systems as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field.

Thus, there are ten unspeakable numbers of fragrant-ocean world-systems as accompanying worlds, all situated together within the ocean of world-systems. Now, we shall focus solely on the central world-system.
Next is "Boundless Wondrous Flower Radiance," which is the collective name for this central fragrant ocean. Next is "All..."
"Adorned with Fragrant Maṇi Kings" is the general name for this central flower;
it is merely a different name given according to its specific meaning within the previously mentioned "Flame-Fragrance Banner.

"The Blazing Jewel Light Universally Illuminating the Ten Directions" is the general name for the central world-system (*kṣetradhātu*). Therefore, the Sūtra says: "There is a world-system situated therein. Next, there is...
"Inexpressible Buddha-land atom-count worlds. This refers to the worlds contained within the central world-system.
Next, at the very bottom, there is a world named "Supreme Light Pervading Illumination" (*Parama-jyotir-vyūha*).
This is the lowest point of the central world-system. This is calculated solely based on a single twenty-fold Flower Treasury World System (*Kusumita-garbha-lokadhātu*).
This distinguishes their vastness. At the very bottom layer, there is only one world as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field surrounding it as its retinue.
Each successive layer above increases by one; reaching the twentieth layer, there are twenty worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field serving as its retinue.
This is calculated solely with respect to the single central [world].

The world-systems are illuminated by light; thus, the Flower Treasury World (Kusumatalagarbha-lokadhātu) is like an inverted stupa, small at the bottom and large at the top, which is why its form appears as such.

However, this refers only to a single world-system among the world-systems numbering as many as the atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields within the ocean of worlds. It does not include those [other] ten Buddha-field atoms.
This is a numerical enumeration. The concluding statement says that each [direction] individually possesses ten Buddha-fields (*buddhakṣetra*).

The subsequent fascicle clarifies the fields to which one circumambulates to the right, thereby illustrating the extent of the territory under his jurisdiction and distinguishing how it gradually expands. The prose section has fully explained the central Buddha-field.
The tenth ocean, turning to the right, concludes the final scroll.
*An Outline of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll Eight;
*An Outline of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll Nine.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Śikṣānanda of the Kingdom of Khotan;
the commentary on the meaning by the Śramaṇa Chengguan of Qingliangshan Dafuhua-yan Monastery;
and the abridgment by the Śramaṇa Hanshan Deqing of Fayun Monastery on Mount Kuang, Ming Dynasty.
The Fifth Chapter: The Flower Treasury World System, Part Two.
Above, the central world-system of the Flower Treasury was explained as the primary realm; next, below, the accompanying world-systems that circumambulate in the ten directions are explained.
These consist of ten oceans arranged in a clockwise rotation, which surround the central ocean; there are ten such oceans.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha, to the east of this Fragrant Ocean named Boundless Radiance of Wondrous Flowers, there is another fragrant ocean named Stainless Flame Treasury.
From it emerges a great lotus flower named Exquisite Adornment of All Fragrant Mani Kings, upon which rests a world-system called Illuminating Everywhere."
It revolves, having the roar of the Bodhisattva’s practice as its essence. At the very bottom of this [array] is a world-system named Palace-Adorned Banner.
It is square in shape and rests upon an ocean adorned with all kinds of jewels. A cloud-net of lotus radiance covers it from above.
It is surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, and is purely and entirely serene. The Buddha there is named... [Bhrū-]... (The Buddha’s name begins with "Bhrū-").
The intervening light shines everywhere. Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Virtue Flower Treasury (*Guṇapuṣpakośa*).
It is circular in shape and rests upon an ocean of all-jeweled flower calyxes. Clouds of pearl-banner lion thrones completely cover its summit.
It is surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms in two buddha-fields. The Buddha’s name is All-Unbounded (*Sarvānantya*).
Dharmasāgaraprajñā. Beyond this, past as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Exquisite Fragrance Wheel of Skillful Transformation.
Its shape is like a vajra, and it rests upon an ocean of nets of bells adorned with all kinds of jewels.
Clouds of variously adorned circular halos completely cover its summit. It is surrounded by as many worlds as there are atoms in three buddha-fields. The Buddha’s name is...
The radiance of the marks of merit shines everywhere. Above this, past as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Wondrous Color Radiance.
Its shape is like a maṇi-jewel wheel, resting upon a fragrant water-ocean of boundless colored jewels.
Clouds of pearl pavilions of universal radiance completely cover its summit. [It is surrounded by] as many worlds as there are atoms in four buddha-fields.
The world-system is surrounded by a single, pure expanse. The Buddha’s name is Well-Arisen Universal Radiance of Good Retinues.
Above this, past as many worlds as atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Well-Covered with Good Canopies.
It is shaped like a lotus and rests upon a sea of fragrant water of diamond. Clouds of fragrant water of dust-free radiance completely cover its summit. Five buddha-fields...
It is surrounded by worlds as numerous as atoms of dust. The Buddha there is named Infinite Wisdom of Dharma-Joy.

Above this, past worlds as numerous as atoms of a buddha-field, there is a world named Śrīkusumaprabhāmaṇḍala. It is triangular in shape and rests upon an ocean adorned with all kinds of solid jewels.
Clouds of light from the mani-jewel crowns of bodhisattvas completely cover its summit. Six Buddhas...
It is surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field. The Buddha there is named Pure Universal Radiance.

Above this, passing through worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Adorned with Jewel Lotuses. Its shape is like a half-moon, and it rests upon an ocean adorned with all kinds of lotuses.
Clouds of all manner of jewel flowers completely cover its surface. Seven buddha-fields... [atoms]...
It is surrounded by worlds as numerous as atoms of dust, all of which are purely and uniformly serene. The Buddha there is named Pure Eye of Merit-Flowers.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as atoms of a buddha-field, there is a world named Stupa of Stainless Radiance Adornments.
Its shape is like rows of precious lamps, resting upon an ocean of jewel-flame treasuries. It constantly rains fragrant waters, and various clouds of bodies pervade it.
It covers the summit and is surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms in eight buddha-fields. The Buddha there is named Invincible Power of Wisdom.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, is a world named Wondrous Brahma-Sound. Its shape is like the svastika (卍).
It rests upon an ocean of jewel-cloth banners and is completely covered by clouds of canopies adorned with every kind of flower. Nine buddhas...
It is surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field. The Buddha there is named Vast Eyes Like the Pure Moon in the Sky.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Sound of Atom-Numbered Voices.
Its form is like Indra’s net, resting upon an ocean of all kinds of jewel-water, and it is filled with clouds of jewel-canopies that produce all manner of musical sounds.
It covers its summit and is surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, all of which are purely and uniformly clear.
The Buddha there is named Golden Sumeru Lamp. Above this, passing through worlds as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there is a world named Jewel-Colored Adornment;

Chapter Five, Part Three: The Flower Treasury World System.
Below this, it is generally explained that in addition to the ten oceans listed in the preceding fascicle, each of these also has its own ten subordinate oceans.
Within each of those, there are further ten oceans, each numbering as many as the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields;

however, the current text mentions only ten for each, which together constitute one hundred oceans. Each of these likewise possesses its own world-system (kṣetra-vyuha) and the worlds it sustains, and their arrangement is as follows:

From the interior to the exterior; therefore, at the very end, it merely mentions the world-system located in the single ocean closest to the Cakravāḍa mountains, which likewise consists of twenty tiers.
This is a case of citing the outer to include the inner. Thus, one should know that the ten oceans listed within each [tier] also constitute individual world-systems.
That the present text cites only one to represent the rest is merely a stylistic abbreviation by the translator, as will be seen below.
The ten oceans are listed; all are arranged in successive order based on the preceding ten inner oceans, such as the Inner Stainless Flame Treasury Ocean, and so forth.
Only the names of the inner oceans are recorded, and the text is naturally easy to understand.

The ocean is named *Candana-vedikā-svara-garbha*. The world-system is named *Abhyudgata-dhvaja*.
Next is a fragrant water ocean named *Sugandharatnarāja-prabhā-vyūha*. The world-system is named *Samantamukha-raśmi-bala*. O Sons of the Buddha!
Beyond that Lotus Indra-net fragrant water ocean, there is another fragrant water ocean named *Rajata-padma*.
Adorned with exquisite flowers. The world-system is named Universal Conduct. Next, there is a sea of fragrant water named Dense Flame Clouds of Lapis Lazuli Bamboo;
the world-system is named Universally Producing Sounds from the Ten Directions. Next, there is a sea of fragrant water named Mass of Radiant Flames of the Ten Directions;
the world-system is named Constantly Producing Transformations Distributed Throughout the Ten Directions. Next, there is a sea of fragrant water...
The ocean is named Appearance of True Gold Maṇi Banner; the world-system is named Vajra Banner Mark.
Next is a fragrant water ocean named Equal Great Adornment; the world-system is named Dharma Realm Valiant Revolution.
Next is a fragrant water ocean named Inexhaustible Light of Jewel Flower Clusters; the world-system is named Boundless Pure Radiance. Next is...
The ocean of fragrant water is named Wondrous Golden Banner; the world-system is named Expounding the Subtle and Secret Places.
Next is an ocean of fragrant water named Light and Shadow Pervasive Illumination; the world-system is named Universal Adornment. Next is an ocean of fragrant water named Silent Sound;
the world-system is named Manifesting and Hanging Down. Such as these are as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
There is an ocean of fragrant water. The ocean of fragrant water nearest to the Cakravāḍa Mountains is named Dense Flame Cloud Banner.
The world-system is named Adorned with All Light, and it has as its essence the sounds of the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas.
At the very bottom of this [system] is a world named Pure Eye Adornment; the Buddha there is named Vajra Moon Illumining the Ten Directions.
Above this, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, there is a world level with the world Vajradhvaja, named Padmaguṇa;
the Buddha there is named Mahāvīra-sujñānamati. Above this, level with the Sahā world, there is a world named Vajraguhya-vyūha; the Buddha there is named Śālarājadhvaja. Above this...
Beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in seven buddha-fields, there is a world named Pure Ocean Adornment.
The Buddha there is named Peerless Majestic Virtue, Unconquerable by Any. O Children of the Buddha, beyond that Sea of Fragrant Incense Treasury Perfumed Water, there is...
Next there is a sea of fragrant water named All-Jeweled Radiance Pervading; the world-system therein is named Stūpa-Array of Stainless Glory.
Next there is a sea of fragrant water named Blooming of Myriad Jeweled Flowers; the world-system therein is named Space-like Appearance.
Next there is a sea of fragrant water named Auspicious Canopy Pervasive Illumination; its world-system is named Unobstructed Light Universal Adornment.
Next there is a sea of fragrant water named Sandalwood Tree Flower; its world-system is named Universally Manifesting in the Ten Directions.
Next there is a sea of fragrant water named Producing Exquisite-Colored Jewels; the world-system therein is named Pervasive Course of Supreme Banners.
Next there is a sea of fragrant water named Universally Producing Vajra Flowers; the world-system therein is named Manifesting Inconceivable Adornments.
Next there is a sea of fragrant water named Adorned with the Mind-King Maṇi Wheel; the world-system therein is named Manifestation.
The Buddha’s light is unimpeded. Next is a sea of fragrant water named Accumulated Jewel Garlands;
its world-system is named Purifying Doubt. Next is a sea of fragrant water named Universally Adorned with Pearl Wheels;
its world-system is named Flowing from the Vows of All Buddhas. There are such seas of fragrant water, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields. Among them, the most...
Near the Cakravāḍa mountains is a fragrant ocean named Jambūnada-ratna-garbha-cakra.

The world-system is named Samanta-ghoṣa-dhvaja, and its substance consists of the sounds that enter the gateway to all-knowledge. At the very bottom of this [system] is a world named Kusuma-kośa-jvālā;
the Buddha there is named Vīryadatta. Above this, past as many worlds as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, is...
Equal in extent to the Vajradhvaja world, there is a world named Padmaprabhaketu. The Buddha there is named Sarvaguṇasāgravicitramanarāja.

Above this, passing through as many worlds as there are atoms in three buddha-fields and equal in extent to the Sahā world, there is a world named Daśabalavyūha. The Buddha there is named Suvyaktānantaguṇa.
O Virtuous King, at the very summit of this world-system, there is a world named Maṇi-Gandha-kūṭa-dhvaja.
The Buddha there is named Viśāla-sunetra-vimala-vicikitsā-prahāṇa.
O Sons of the Buddha, beyond that Jewel-Adorned Sea of Fragrant Water, there is another sea of fragrant water named Sumeru-prabhā-garbha-dhara; its world-system is named Vistīrṇa-megha-sambhava.
Next there is a sea of fragrant water named Great Majestic Power of Various Adornments;
its world-system is named Unobstructed Pure Adornment. Next there is a sea of fragrant water named Dense Array of Jewel Lotuses;
its world-system is named Adornment of Supreme Lamps. Next there is a sea of fragrant water named Dependent on All Jewel Adornments; its world-system...
The ocean of fragrant water is named Sunlight Net Treasury; next is the ocean of fragrant water named Multitudinous Pure Adornments;
the world-system is named Abode of Jewel Flowers. Next is the ocean of fragrant water named Utmost Wise Conduct;
the world-system is named Adornment of Supreme Forms. Next is the ocean of fragrant water named Holding Exquisite Maṇi Peaks; the world-system is named Universally Pure.
Gaganagañja. Next is a sea of fragrant water named Great Light Pervading Illumination; its world-system is named Sapphire Torch Radiance.
Next is a sea of fragrant water named Filled with Delightful Maṇi Jewels Pervasive Illumination;
its world-system is named Universal Roaring Sound. There are seas of fragrant water such as these, numbering as many as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields. Among them, the most...
In the fragrant ocean near the Cakravāḍa mountains, there is one named *Indranīlaratnodgata*.
Its world-system is named *Samantavyūhābheda*, and it has the resounding roar of all bodhisattvas as its substance. Within this, at the very bottom, is a world named *Suvijayagarbha*;
the Buddha there is named *Vijayaguṇaprajñā*. Above this, passing through worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields...
The realm is equal in extent to the Vajradhvaja world. There is a world named Adorned Appearance; its Buddha is named Transcendent Great Radiance.
Above this, equal in extent to the Sahā world, is a world named Universal Adornment of Lapis Lazuli Wheels;
its Buddha is named Sumeru Lamp. At the very top of this world-system, there is a world named Flower.
The Ocean of Banners. The Buddha’s name is Cloud of Inexhaustible Transformation and Wondrous Wisdom. O Sons of the Buddha!
Beyond that Fragrant Water Ocean of the Mass of Vajra Jewels, there is another Fragrant Water Ocean named Adorned with Exalted Jewel Ramparts;
its world-system is named Outstanding Jewel Banner. Next is a Fragrant Water Ocean named Adorned with Jewel Banners; its world-system is named Manifesting All Light.
Next is a sea of fragrant water named Cloud of Exquisite Jewels; its world-system is named Radiance Pervading All with the Adornments of Every Jewel.
Next is a sea of fragrant water named Adorned with Flowers of Jewel Trees; its world-system is named Interspersed with Exquisite Flowers.
Next is a sea of fragrant water named Adorned with Exquisite Jewel Garments; its world-system is named Ocean of Radiance.
Next is a sea of fragrant water named Jewel Tree Peak; its world-system is named Jewel Flame Cloud.
Next is a sea of fragrant water named Manifesting Radiance; its world-system is named Entering the Unobstructed Diamond.
Next is a sea of fragrant water named Lotus Universal Adornment; its world-system is named Boundless Shore Ocean Abyss. Next is a sea of fragrant water...
The ocean is named Adorned with Exquisite Jewels; the world-system is named Treasury of Universally Manifesting Lands.
There are as many such fragrant water oceans as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields. The fragrant water ocean nearest to the Cakravāḍa mountains is named Indestructible Ocean;
its world-system is named Lotus Field Interspersed with Exquisite Wheels, [manifested] by the power of all Buddhas.
The essence consists of the sounds that are produced. At the very bottom of this [array] is a world named Most Sublime Fragrance;

the Buddha there is named Light of Infinite Transformation as Numerous as Atomic Dusts. Above this, passing through worlds as numerous as the atomic dusts of ten buddha-fields, at the same level as the world Vajra Banner, is a world named Inconceivable Gate of Variegated Adornments; the Buddha there is named [Un-...].
The Wisdom of Measurement. Above this, level with the Sahā world, there is a world named *Daśadig-prabhāsa-guṇa-kusuma-garbha*.
The Buddha there is named *Siṃhacakṣur-jvālā-megha*. At the very summit above this, there is a world named *Sāgara-ghoṣa*.
The Buddha there is named *Varuṇaprabhā-jvālāmukha*. O Children of the Buddha! That is the jeweled rampart of the celestial city within the fragrant water-ocean.
Outside, there is a sea of fragrant water named Blazing Orb of Resplendent Light; its world-system is named Inexpressible Various Adornments.
Next, there is a sea of fragrant water named Path of Jewel Dust; its world-system is named Universally Entering Infinite Spirals.
Next, there is a sea of fragrant water named Possessing All Adornments; its world-system is named Jewel Light Shining Everywhere.
Next there is a sea of fragrant water named Arrayed Net of Various Jewels; its world-system is named Deeply Arranged and Secret.
Next there is a sea of fragrant water named Banner Adorned with Exquisite Jewels; its world-system is named Clear Sound of the Ocean of Worlds.
Next there is a sea of fragrant water named Pure Reflection of the Lunar Palace; its world-system is named Pervasive Entry into Indra’s Net.
Next is a sea of fragrant water named *Sarvatūryasaṃgītimanojñanirghoṣa*. The world-system therein is named *Paripūrṇasamatala*.
Next is a sea of fragrant water named *Vicitrasukhavyūha*. The world-system therein is named *Viśuddhasaṃdhyārcimegha*.
Next is a sea of fragrant water named *Samantaratnārcidīpa*. The world-system therein is named *Buddhapraṇidhānānuvartin*.

Of various forms—such as these incalculable oceans of fragrant water, numbering as many as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields—the ocean of fragrant water nearest to the Cakravāḍa mountains is named Accumulated Garlands and Robes; the world-system therein is named Manifesting Wondrous Garments.
It has the vocal sounds of all Buddhas of the three periods of time as its essence. At the very bottom of this [array] is a sea of fragrant water named Indralakṣaṇagarbha (Indra-flower Treasury).
The world-system is named Producing Joy. It is surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, and is uniformly pure.
The Buddha there is named Firm Wisdom. Above this, passing through worlds as numerous as the atoms within ten Buddha-fields...

The realm is equal in extent to the Vajradhvaja world. There is a world named Ratnajālapratimaṇḍita, surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, which is purely and uniformly pure. The Buddha there is named Anantaprītiprabha.
Above this, passing through worlds as numerous as the atoms in three buddha-fields, there is a world equal in extent to the Sahā world, named...
There is a precious lotus lion throne surrounded by worlds as numerous as the atoms in thirteen buddha-fields.
The Buddha there is named Most Pure and Unfailing Hearing. Above this, passing through worlds as numerous as the atoms in seven buddha-fields, one reaches the highest point of this world-system.
There is a world named Jewel-Colored Dragon Radiance, [surrounded by] twenty buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in [twenty] buddha-fields.
The world is encircled by a single, pure expanse. The Buddha’s name is Universal Illumination Pervading the Dharma Realm.
Below this, arranged in successive tiers outside the first layer, there are ten oceans in each of the ten directions.
These are aligned one after another from the center to the periphery; thus, at the very edge of these ten oceans, the ocean closest to the Cakravāḍa Mountains is the tenth.

Regarding the statement that there are "world-system seeds," this indicates that within each of the nine seas there are all types of world-systems (*kṣetra*), though they have simply not been enumerated.

This passage cites the eastern direction as an example; the same applies to the other nine directions. The scriptural text is very clear on this point, which is why the concluding summary at the end states:

O Sons of the Buddha! Within these seas of fragrant water, numbering as many as the atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields, there are world-systems numbering as many as the atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields.

All of them rest upon lotus blossoms adorned with mani-jewel king banners that manifest the forms of all bodhisattvas; each is adorned with boundless arrays that are continuous and uninterrupted, and each emits—
The light of jewel-like colors; each with clouds of radiance covering them above; each with various ornaments; each with the distinctions of different eons;
each with the appearance of Buddhas; each with oceans of Dharma being expounded; each filled everywhere with sentient beings.
Each and every one universally enters the ten directions; each and every one is sustained by the spiritual power of all Buddhas.

Within each and every world-system, all worlds abide through various adornments, joined together in succession to form a world-net, established throughout the Lotus Treasury Adorned Ocean of Worlds in all their various distinctions.
The concluding summary of this section states: "Abiding upon a lotus adorned with the king of mani-jewel banners, which manifests the forms of all bodhisattvas.

This "lotus of the king of mani-jewel banners" is none other than the previously mentioned central fragrant ocean named *Anantavicitrapuṣpābha* (Light of Boundless Wondrous Flowers). Here, the term "king of mani-jewel banners" refers to the seabed.

However, the current concluding statement that "all [worlds] rely upon this ocean" precisely reveals that these various oceans of lands all reside within the diamond ground amidst the calyx-fragrance;
because the scriptural passage was far removed [from its context], it has been extracted here so that the observer may understand their source.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, received the Buddha’s majestic power and spoke in verse:
The Flower Treasury World-Ocean Is equal to and no different from the Dharma-realm;
Its adornments are utterly pure, Abiding peacefully within space. Within this world-ocean, The arrays of lands are inconceivable.
Each and every one is sovereign, Each distinct and without confusion.
The world-oceans of Flower Treasury, With their various forms and diverse adornments, Are well-arranged as clusters of lands;
Their various characteristics differ, And the transformation-sounds of all Buddhas Take these various things as their essence, Appearing according to the power of karma.
The arrays of world-systems are wondrously adorned, With Mount Sumeru, mountain ranges, and nets; Circular in shape like swirling waters,
vast as blooming lotuses, Each surrounding the other, In forms of mountain banners, towers, and pavilions, Or revolving vajra-shapes—
Thus are these inconceivable and vast arrays of world-systems.
The ocean-like pearls of flame, with inconceivable nets of light—
all such world-systems dwell within lotuses. Within each and every world-system, in unspeakable numbers of nets of light,
all worlds are proclaimed within the light, pervading the oceans of the ten directions, across all varieties of world-systems.

All ornaments and all lands enter therein; Universally seen without end are the inconceivable clusters of realms, Worlds without limit, Variously and wonderfully adorned—all through the power of the Great Sage.
Within every cluster of realms, The worlds are inconceivable.
Some are forming, some are being destroyed, and some have already perished;
just as among the leaves in a forest there are both those that grow and those that fall, so it is within these world-systems: worlds undergo formation and destruction.
Just as there are various distinctions among fruits depending on a forest, so it is depending on these world-systems.
The various abodes of sentient beings are like the differences among seeds;
because the power of karma differs, the fruits produced are each distinct. The lands of sentient beings are not the same:
just as with the *cintāmaṇi* jewel, which manifests all colors according to the mind, because the minds of sentient beings are pure, they perceive pure lands.
Just as a great dragon king raises clouds that pervade the void,
so too do the powers of the Buddha’s vows give birth to all lands. Like the spells and arts of a magician who can manifest all manner of things,
the inconceivable lands arise through the power of the karma of sentient beings, like images painted upon a wall.
Just as the works of a painter, so too are all these lands;
The bodies of sentient beings, formed by the mind-painter, each differ, Arising according to the mind’s conceptualization.
Such diverse lands are all without exception produced by karma, Just like seeing a guide With various distinctions of color.
According to the mental activities of sentient beings, they see all lands in the same way.
At the boundaries of all these lands, nets of lotuses are spread out; their various characteristics differ, yet their adornments are entirely pure.
Those nets of lotuses are where the networks of lands are established, with their manifold and diverse ornaments.
In various abodes of sentient beings, or within some buddha-fields, there are rugged, treacherous, and uneven terrains;

these are seen as such because of the afflictions of sentient beings. Thus, immeasurable varieties of fields—both defiled and pure—arise according to the minds of sentient beings, sustained by the power of the bodhisattvas.
In some buddha-fields there is both defilement and purity; these arise through the power of karma as the transformations of bodhisattvas.
Some fields emit radiance, composed of stainless jewels and adorned with various exquisite ornaments;
these the Buddhas cause to be purified within each and every category of fields.
Though inconceivable kalpas burn and what appears therein may be ruined and evil, that place is always firm and solid due to the karmic power of sentient beings.
Many buddha-fields are produced, abiding supported by the wind-circle and the water-circle;
such is the nature of the world, appearing in various ways to different perceptions.
Yet in reality there is no birth, nor is there any destruction; within each and every thought-moment, immeasurable lands arise.
By the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, one sees all those pure and stainless lands as being composed of earth and mud;
their substance is exceedingly hard and solid, dark and devoid of light.
The abode of those who have performed evil deeds is a realm formed of vajra;
it is defiled, filled with great anxiety, fear, and suffering, while joy is scarce. It is the dwelling place of those with meager merit, constructed either of iron or of red copper;
with its rocky mountains and precipices, it is terrifying and teeming with evildoers.
Within this realm there are hells, where sentient beings suffer without rescue; they dwell perpetually in darkness, scorched by the blazing ocean of flames.
Or again, there are animals with various hideous forms, who due to their own evil karma constantly undergo all manner of suffering and affliction; or one may see the realm of Yama.
Tormented by hunger and thirst, they ascend great mountains of fire, Suffering various forms of most grievous pain.
There are some lands composed of the seven treasures, With various kinds of palaces and halls;
these are obtained through pure karma. You should observe this world, Both its humans and its devas.
The fruits of pure karma are accomplished, And one experiences happiness at all times.
Within each and every pore are inconceivable billions of lands, Adorned with various marks and signs. Never have they been cramped;
according to the individual karmas of sentient beings, There are infinite kinds of worlds, In which they give rise to grasping and birth.
Some experience suffering and pleasure differently; some lands are composed of various jewels.
They constantly emit boundless light from wondrous vajra lotuses, adorned, pure, and stainless.
There are lands where light is the very substance, abiding within spheres of light; With the fragrance of golden sandalwood, clouds of flames illuminate everywhere.
There are lands formed from lunar discs, where fragrant robes are spread everywhere; within a single lotus, bodhisattvas fill it completely.
There are lands formed of various jewels, their colors and forms free from all defilement, like the net of Indra, with light constantly shining. There are lands whose very substance is fragrance.
Some are like vajra-flowers, or the radiant forms of mani-jewels; Upon close observation, they are exceedingly pure.
There are inconceivable lands accomplished through the swirling of flowers, Filled everywhere with emanation-buddhas and the universal radiance of bodhisattvas.
Or there are pure lands where everything consists of various flowering trees.
In some realms, wondrous branches form a place of practice, shaded by clouds of *maṇi* jewels;
Some lands are composed of pure light and diamond flowers, where the Buddha’s transformative voice resounds. Boundless [lands] are arranged in a network;
some are like Bodhisattvas, Adorned with crowns of exquisite *maṇi* jewels; others are shaped like thrones.
Emanated from the light of transformation, whether as sandalwood powder, or from the light between the brows, or from the sounds within the Buddha’s radiance, this wondrous realm is thus formed.
Some see this pure realm adorned with a single light; others see it with manifold adornments—all varieties being marvelous and sublime.
Or using the exquisite objects of ten lands as adornments, or taking all things within a thousand lands to form an array;
or using the objects of a billion realms to adorn a single land— though their various forms differ,
they all appear like reflections, such that the objects of unspeakable numbers of lands cannot be fully described.
Adorning a single land, each emits radiant light;
Arising from the power of the Tathāgata’s vows, there are various lands Purified by the power of those vows.
Within every adornment, one universally perceives oceans of all lands; For those who cultivate the vows of Samantabhadra, The pure lands they attain are thus.
The adornments of the lands of the three periods of time all appear within them.
O Son of the Buddha, you should observe the majestic spiritual power of these world-systems:
the future lands and the oceans of past lands throughout the worlds of the ten directions are all made visible within a single land, as if in a dream.
Manifestations are like transformations; all Buddhas of the three times, along with their buddha-fields, are entirely perceived within a single dharma-realm atom.
Through the spiritual power of all Buddhas, myriad lands appear within a single atom;
all these various forms are clearly seen, yet they are without reality, like shadows.
There are many lands whose shapes are like the great ocean; Some are like Mount Sumeru—worlds inconceivable.
There are lands well-established, Whose shapes are like Indra’s net or like forest groves;
Buddhas fill them all, Or they take the shape of precious wheels.
Some are shaped like lotuses, complete with eight corners and various ornaments, all entirely pure;
some have the form of a seat, or again, they are triangular;
some are like the city walls of Kālakavana, or like the body of Brahmā, or like the topknot of the Lord of Devas, or like a half-moon.
Some are like Mount Maṇi; some have the shape of the solar disc. Some worlds have shapes like the swirling of a fragrant ocean;
some form circles of light. There are those adorned and purified by Buddhas of the past;
some have the shape of wheel-rims, some have the shape of sacrificial altars, and some are like the ūrṇā-kośa between the Buddha’s eyebrows.
The uṣṇīṣa is broad and long, and the eyes are like those of a Buddha;
some are shaped like a vajra, others like a mountain of flames. These bodhisattvas are everywhere present, appearing in forms such as lions or sea shells;
their infinite varieties of color and form differ in their essential natures.
Within a single world-system, the forms of worlds are inexhaustible;
all abide securely through the protective mindfulness of the Buddha’s power of vows.
Some worlds endure for one eon, or for ten eons, or even beyond hundreds of thousands, as numerous as the atoms within a land; or they may abide within a single eon.
One sees that some lands undergo formation and destruction, while others are immeasurable and innumerable, even to the point of being inconceivable.
Some lands have a Buddha, while other lands have no Buddha;
some have but a single Buddha, while others have immeasurable Buddhas. If there is no Buddha in a particular land, [one looks] to other worlds.
There is a Buddha who comes through transformation to manifest the various deeds of Buddhas:
passing away from heaven, descending in spirit, dwelling in the womb, and being born; subduing Māra and attaining perfect enlightenment;
turning the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma according to the inclinations of sentient beings, manifesting various forms to turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma.

In accordance with their faculties and inclinations, within each and every buddha-field, a single Buddha appears in the world and remains for hundreds of millions of years, expounding the unsurpassed Dharma.
Sentient beings who are not vessels for the Dharma cannot see these Buddhas; however, those whose hearts find joy in it shall see them in all places.
In each and every buddha-field, a Buddha appears in the world; within all these fields, there are inconceivable billions of Buddhas.

In each of these, every single Buddha manifests immeasurable spiritual transformations that pervade the entire dharma-realm, taming oceans of sentient beings. Yet, there are fields where no light shines.
Darkness brings much fear, and painful contact is like swords and blades; those who see it are themselves tormented by its venom.
Some realms possess the light of devas, some the light of palaces, and others the radiance of the sun and moon.
The networks of world-systems are inconceivable: some realms possess their own natural light, while others have trees that emit pure radiance.

There has never been such suffering and affliction; yet, by the power of the merit of sentient beings, some have the radiance of mountains, some the radiance of *maṇi* jewels, and some the light of lamps. All these are the result of the karmic power of sentient beings.
There is also the radiance of the Buddhas, within which Bodhisattvas are fully present, and there is the radiance of this lotus flower.

The color of the flames is most magnificent; some lands are illumined by the light of flowers, while others are illumined by fragrant waters, ointments, and burning incense—all resulting from the power of pure vows.
Some are illumined by clouds of light, by the light of mani-jewels and pearl oysters, and by the light of the Buddha’s spiritual power, capable of proclaiming sounds that gladden the mind.
Some are illuminated by the light of jewels, others by the flames of vajras; pure sounds resonate afar, and wherever they reach, there is no suffering.
Some have the light of mani-gems, some the light of ornaments, or the radiance of the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), shining brightly within the assembly. The Buddha emits this great radiance.
Transformation Buddhas fill its interior, their light universally touching and pervading the entire dharma-realm.
There are lands that are most terrifying, with sounds of wailing and great suffering; those sounds are so acutely agonizing that all who hear them give rise to loathing and fear.
These include the realms of hell-beings and animals, as well as the abode of Yama.
In this turbid and evil world, there constantly arise sounds of sorrow and suffering;
yet in some lands, there always emerge delightful sounds that gladden the mind and accord with the teachings—this is obtained through pure karma.
In other lands, one constantly hears the voice of Śakra, or hears the voice of Brahmā.
The voices of all the Lords of the World; In some buddha-fields, there are clouds that emit wondrous sounds, And jewel-ocean mani-trees with the sound of music pervading everywhere.
Within the circular halos of all Buddhas, emanated sounds are inexhaustible, Along with the sublime voices of Bodhisattvas, Which are heard throughout the lands of the ten directions.
Inconceivable lands resound with the universal turning of the wheel of Dharma; From the ocean of vows emerge sounds of sublime practice.
All Buddhas of the three periods of time, throughout all worlds, Are fully endowed with their various names and epithets; Their voices are inexhaustible, And may some be heard within a single realm.
The sounds of all Buddha-powers, the stages, the perfections, and the immeasurables—all such dharmas are expounded through the power of Samantabhadra’s vows.
In billions of lands he proclaims wondrous sounds;
those sounds are like the roll of thunder, remaining inexhaustible throughout kalpas. In pure lands, the Buddhas manifest these sovereign sounds.
Throughout the dharma-realm in the ten directions, there is nothing that does not hear this.
Below, there are one hundred and one verses of reiteration. The first verse clarifies the essential nature of the Flower Treasury World (*Kusumatalagarbha*).

The subsequent one hundred verses eulogize the network of lands (*kṣetra-jāla*) contained therein. There is a commentary (*śāstra*) providing a topical outline and explanation, all of which follows the meaning of the prose; these are not recorded here in full.
Supplementary Commentary: However, the boundless oceans of lands enumerated in the preceding three sections are all formed through two kinds of causes and conditions:
first, they are accomplished through the power of the vows and practices of the Buddhas and Tathāgatas; second, they are evoked by the karmic forces of sentient beings.
Thus, there are differences between pure and defiled lands. In general, this reveals that the Dharma-realm takes dependent origination as its fundamental principle.
Furthermore, the boundless worlds listed above form a network of lands (*kṣetra-jāla*) that abides within empty space.

This reveals the realm of the inexhaustible and multilayered interpenetration of phenomena and phenomena (*shishi wujin chongchong*). That which is elucidated by the six characteristics (*liu xiang*) and the ten mysteries (*shi xuan*) is precisely this alone.
First, the thirty phrases of the Bodhisattva’s request for the fruit constitute the inquiry; these two chapters have already provided the answer.
[The text] is complete. Although the commentary states that the arrival of the sutras is not yet finished, the causes and effects encompassed therein are all contained within this.
What is called the "ocean" is the ocean of the Tathāgata’s nature (*dharmatā-samudra*), also termed the ocean of wisdom (*jñāna-samudra*).

However, the Flower Treasury Ocean (*Huazang hai*) is the ocean of nature and the ocean of wisdom as they manifest according to conditions (*pratyaya*), arising from the winds of the great vows of all Buddhas and the winds of the deluded thoughts of sentient beings.
By means of these two kinds of conditions, this Flower Treasury (Kusumatalagarbha) is established. This clearly reveals that the Dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) is the Tathāgata-garbha;
it is also called the consciousness-store (vijñānagarbha). In sum, the Flower Treasury Ocean is the Tathāgata-garbha Ocean.
Each and every world-system within it is the result of the seeds contained within the eight consciousnesses of each and every sentient being. All other individual worlds are likewise...

It is induced by the wholesome and unwholesome karmic actions of the mind; therefore, purity and defilement differ. This is what is meant by "the three realms are mind-only" and "all phenomena are consciousness-only.

One should contemplate that the nature of the dharma-realm is entirely created by the mind, for the dharma-realm is inconceivable, the wondrous functions of the Buddhas' spiritual powers are inconceivable, and the karmic power of sentient beings is inconceivable.
[The author] deliberates: However, what is clarified in other teachings merely states that "the three realms are mind-only.
This generally refers to the three realms within this single Sahā world-system.
Furthermore, this Sahā world is but one world within the thirteenth layer supported by a single *kṣetra-vyuha* (world-array) at the very center; it does not yet exhaust even a single layer.
The worlds listed—such as Akṣobhya’s and Sukhāvatī—are situated at the eastern and western edges of this same layer;
they do not exhaust the full extent of this layer, yet only Sukhāvatī is specifically mentioned.

It is said to be ten trillion Buddha-lands away from Sahā, yet sentient beings, due to their habituation to narrow-mindedness, perceive it as distant; how much more so for the twenty layers of lotuses?
It is hidden within. Yet, this Flower Treasury (Avataṃsaka) is, within the emptiness of the dharma-nature (dharmatā-śūnyatā), like a single mote of dust;

how much more so when compared to the full extent of the ocean of lands? Furthermore, within the vast and boundless ocean of lands, all the various subtle differences among the ten dharma realms—the environments and inhabitants, the holy and the mundane—are known and seen in their entirety only by the Buddha’s wisdom, whereas those of the two vehicles...
Yet, within this single triple world of the Sahā universe, their hearts of weary detachment are such as these;
how then could they fathom the Buddha’s wisdom or know the Buddha’s realm? Thus, it is no cause for wonder that those seated here are like the blind and the deaf.
Such vast fruits of retribution were attained by my original teacher, Vairocana, through causes cultivated over immeasurable kalpas.
I now present them first to encourage sentient beings of great resolve, so that they may give rise to a mind of faith and joy, practice accordingly, and realize this for themselves.

Therefore, the gates of practice traversed by the three stages of worthiness and the ten stages of sagehood, up to the stage of Equal Enlightenment, are all said to be of the nature of the Dharma-realm.
One cultivates [the path] with the desire to realize this. Subsequently, in the "Entering the Dharma Realm" chapter (*dharmadhātu-prakaraṇa*), one enters according to the person who has realized it;
that which is realized is likewise the realization of this inexhaustible dharma realm, which alone constitutes the ultimate realization.

Nevertheless, while Sudhana visited fifty-three spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), each merely realized a single gate of liberation (*vimokṣamukha*). It was only upon directly entering into a single pore of Samantabhadra’s body that he attained thorough realization.
This boundless realm of phenomena—wherein the perfection of causes does not exceed even a single pore—is a dharma-gate so vast, subtle, and inconceivable;
how could it ever be discussed with those of shallow intelligence?

Chapter Six: Vairocana.

Regarding the purpose of this chapter’s introduction: the preceding chapter elucidated the fruit of these causes; now, we distinguish those preceding causes to answer the question concerning them, and thus it follows next.
Since these causes are the causes for the person who attains the fruit, they are designated by the title of that fruit.

If one did not apprehend the dharma through the person, one would not know whose causes they are. Thus, at the beginning of the preceding chapter, it was stated: "Vairocana cultivated the causes throughout vast eons."
This has been the adornment and purification [of the land]. Now, the matter of cultivating the causes is being revealed. Regarding the explanation of the name:

it is briefly stated as "Universal Radiance" (*Samantaprabhā*), as explained extensively before. Third, regarding the essential tenets: to clarify that the vastness of cause and effect is the primary tenet (*mūla*), and to realize the aforementioned fruit is the ultimate goal (*prayojana*).
The following scriptural passage introduces the time and place when the Tathāgata Vairocana cultivated the causes [of his enlightenment] in the past, as well as the Buddhas he encountered;
it first clarifies the time.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha, in the distant past, beyond world-microdust kalpas, and even twice that number."
This chapter is divided into three sections. First, a general explanation of the time of the primary narrative (*vṛttānta*).

onwards, a specific revelation of the primary narrative within that time. Now, for the first section: regarding the phrase "the time is again doubled by this number," it refers to eons numbering twice the atoms of a buddha-field.
Furthermore,
there is a world-ocean named Universal Gate Pure Radiance. Within this world-ocean, there is a world named Supreme Sound,

within this Great Forest of the Mani Flower Branch-Wheels, all manner of adornments—

He proclaimed the vast roots of goodness practiced therein, recited the names of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, and expounded the ultimate path of the vows and practices cultivated by all Bodhisattvas.

It is the locus of the lotus. Next, regarding the statement that "in the first eon of that world of Supreme Sound (Ghoṣavatī), as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in ten Mount Sumerus appeared in the world," this specifically clarifies the period of the original narrative.

In the lands of the ten directions, if there are sentient beings who should be tamed, as soon as they are touched by that light, they spontaneously awaken;

they extinguish the heat of all delusions, tear apart the net of all hindrances, shatter the mountains of all obstructions, purify all defilements and turbidity, and give rise to great faith and understanding.
They give birth to supreme roots of goodness; they are forever freed from all hardships and terrors; they extinguish all physical and mental suffering and affliction;
they give rise to the mind that beholds the Buddha; and they advance toward omniscience.

The following section correctly reveals the emergence of the Buddha. To say that he "suddenly appears" means that he is not a body associated with the eight consciousnesses, but rather a Buddha who is instantaneously perfected—the Buddha in whom the Dharmakāya and Sambhogakāya are of one essence.
Therefore, it is said next that "his body pervades the true Dharma-realm," and from his body emerge infinite transformation Buddhas, while various colored lights fill the Dharma-realm.
The dharmadhātu and every pore are pervaded in successive layers. This reveals the Buddha who was originally the teacher of Vairocana;
he is the Sudden Buddha. Therefore, the Dharma heard subsequently is also the Universal Dharma. Because its original cause was vast, the resulting fruition is likewise vast.
[This concludes] the ninth section on "arousing the mind to see the Buddha and aspiring toward omniscience."
The Sūtra on Practice explains the matter of the Buddha’s appearance in the world and his manifestation of light for the benefit of living beings.

When Prince Tejaprabha beheld the Buddha’s radiance, by the power of the roots of goodness he had cultivated in the past, he immediately realized ten dharma-gates.
What are these ten? They are: the realization of the Samādhi of the Wheel of Merits of All Buddhas;
the realization of the Universal Gate Dhāraṇī of All Buddha-dharmas; and the realization of the Vast Treasury of Expedient Means.
The Prajñāpāramitā: it realizes the great adornment of great loving-kindness that tames all sentient beings;
it realizes the great compassion of the universal cloud-sound; it realizes the great joy of the most excellent mind that gives rise to boundless merit;
it realizes the great equanimity that awakens to all phenomena as they truly are; and it realizes the great supernormal power of the treasury of equality through vast skillful means.
He attained the great vow that increases the power of faith and understanding, and he attained the gate of eloquence that universally enters the light of all-knowledge.
At that time, having obtained such illumination of the Dharma, Prince Mahātejas, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic power, [proceeded].
Surveying the great assembly, he spoke these verses:
"The World-Honored One sits at the site of enlightenment, A pure and great radiance.
Like a thousand suns rising together, He shines universally throughout the realm of space. After immeasurable billions of kalpas, The Guide appears only now."
The Buddha has now appeared in the world, the one revered by all.
Behold the Buddha’s radiance and the inconceivable emanation-buddhas; within every palace, he dwells in tranquil meditative absorption.
Behold the Buddha’s supernormal powers: from his pores emerge clouds of flames that illuminate the world.
The radiance is inexhaustible; you should contemplate the Buddha’s body.
A net of light, utterly pure, manifests forms equal in number to all things, Pervading the ten directions. With wondrous voices that fill the world, all who hear them rejoice;
In accordance with the languages of all sentient beings, They praise the virtues of the Buddha.
Wherever the World-Honored One’s light shines, all sentient beings find peace and happiness;

their suffering is entirely extinguished and their hearts give rise to great joy. Beholding the assembly of Bodhisattvas gathered from the ten directions, they all release clouds of *maṇi* jewels and, standing before the Buddha, offer praise with sublime sounds emerging from the site of enlightenment.
That sound is exceedingly deep and far-reaching, capable of extinguishing the suffering of sentient beings. This is the Buddha’s spiritual power;
all pay him homage with reverence, their hearts filled with great joy, as they together gaze up at the Dharma King before the World-Honored One.

At that time, that Tathāgata, desiring to discipline all sentient beings, within the ocean-like assembly of the *bodhimaṇḍa*, preached the *Sūtra on the Universal Collection of the Sovereign Dharmas of All Buddhas of the Three Times*, with as many *sūtras* as there are atoms in a world-system serving as its retinue;
