That is to say: may all sentient beings obtain the seats of the devas and realize great wisdom;
may all sentient beings obtain the seats of the noble ones, abandon the mind of ordinary worldlings, and abide in the bodhicitta;
may all sentient beings obtain the seat of peace and happiness, forever leaving behind all the sufferings and afflictions of birth and death; may all sentient beings obtain the ultimate seat.
Seated, they behold the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas. May all sentient beings obtain seats of equanimity, constantly and universally cultivating all wholesome dharmas.
May all sentient beings obtain the most excellent seat, possessing pure karma peerless in the world.
May all sentient beings obtain the seat of peace and security, realizing the true Dharma and being fully endowed with it.
This is the perfection of the feet. May all sentient beings obtain pure seats and cultivate the realm of the Tathāgata’s pure wisdom.
May all sentient beings obtain seats of peaceful dwelling and be constantly followed, protected, and sheltered by virtuous friends.
May all sentient beings obtain lion seats and always lie on their right sides as the Tathāgata does. This is [the perfection of] bodhi—
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness when giving beds and seats so that sentient beings may cultivate right mindfulness and well-guard their sense faculties.

This is the tenth instance of giving beds and seats; later, in the eighteenth [chapter], there is a separate clarification regarding the giving of seats. Therefore, in the Jin translation, this is rendered as:
Regarding bedding and seating, this is seen as profoundly appropriate.
O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away dwellings, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, they vow that all sentient beings shall attain abiding in pure Buddha-fields and diligently practice all [virtues].
Merit. Abiding in the realm of profound samādhi, they abandon all attachment to dwelling places; they realize that all dwelling places are non-existent.
Free from all worldly realms, they abide in omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), embracing the abodes of all Buddhas.
They dwell in the ultimate path, the place of blissful abiding, and constantly abide in the foremost pure roots of goodness, never—
To relinquish the unsurpassed dwelling place of the Buddhas—this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives dwellings.
It is for the purpose of benefiting all sentient beings by contemplating their protection according to their respective needs.
Eleventh is the gift of dwellings. Regarding the statement "not abandoning the Buddha’s unsurpassed abiding," it means abiding in the chamber of great tranquility.
Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives a dwelling place, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, may all sentient beings constantly obtain wholesome benefits, their minds peaceful and happy; may all sentient beings rely upon...
The Tathāgata abides: he abides in great wisdom; he abides in spiritual friends; he abides in the sublime and victorious;
he abides in virtuous conduct; he abides in great loving-kindness; he abides in great compassion; he abides in the six pāramitās; and he abides in the mind of great bodhicitta.

He abides by means of all bodhisattva paths; this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives a dwelling place, for the sake of purifying all merit, for ultimate purity, and for the purification of wisdom.
Because the path is pure; because the Dharma is pure; because ethical discipline is pure; because aspiration and delight are pure;
because faith and understanding are pure; because vows are pure; and because all supernatural powers and merits are pure.
The twelfth is the gift of dwellings. By "dwelling" is meant monasteries and the like.
O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives various lamps, namely:
ghee lamps, oil lamps, jewel lamps, *maṇi* lamps, lacquer lamps, fire lamps, aloeswood lamps, sandalwood lamps, and all kinds of incense lamps, emitting immeasurable colors of light.

Lamps. When giving such immeasurable lamps as these, it is for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings and for the sake of gathering in all sentient beings. One dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, may all sentient beings attain immeasurable light that universally illumines the true Dharma of all Buddhas; may all sentient beings attain purity.

May the light illuminate and reveal the most subtle forms in the world. May all sentient beings attain freedom from cataracts and realize that the realm of sentient beings is empty and devoid of inherent existence.
May all sentient beings attain a body of boundless light that emits wondrous radiance universally illuminating all things.
May all sentient beings attain the light of universal illumination and never regress in their resolve toward the teachings of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings attain the pure light of the Buddhas, appearing clearly within all buddha-fields.
May all sentient beings attain unimpeded light, a single ray of which illuminates the entirety of the dharma-realm.
May all sentient beings attain uninterrupted light, such that the radiance shines upon all buddha-fields without ceasing. May all sentient beings attain the light of the banner of wisdom.
It universally illumines the world. May all sentient beings obtain immeasurable colored lights that illuminate all lands and manifest spiritual powers.
When a bodhisattva thus gives lamps, it is for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings;
by means of these roots of goodness, they follow after sentient beings and, by means of these roots of goodness, they gather them in.
Born [into this state], they distribute these roots of goodness among sentient beings; through these roots of goodness, they feel compassion for sentient beings;
through these roots of goodness, they nurture and protect sentient beings; through these roots of goodness, they rescue and guard sentient beings;

through these roots of goodness, they fulfill sentient beings; through these roots of goodness, they bring sentient beings to mind; through these roots of goodness, they benefit sentient beings equally. Through these roots of goodness...
Observing sentient beings with the faculties is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives lamps.
Such a dedication is without obstruction, universally causing all sentient beings to abide within roots of goodness.
Thirteenth is the offering of lamps. Regarding "precious lamps," these are like noctilucent gems and the like. One uses agallochum and sandalwood incense mixed with clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
As for the "immeasurable colors": when burning fat, the color is white; when burning lac, the color is red; when burning oil, the color is yellow;
and when burning oil, the color is green. Through such various aspirations, one attains purity by means of the yoga of offering lamps.
Regarding the retribution of the eyes: by burning lamps as an offering to the Buddha, one can greatly extinguish sins and generate merit. One should make this vow:
"May I take the great ocean as oil and Mount Sumeru as a wick, lighting a great bright lamp to illuminate the oceans of Buddha-fields, making offerings without ceasing.

Furthermore, one should vow that the lamp of the Dharma-gate shall have great vows as its wick, and so forth. In the present text, within the section on vows, both body and wisdom are fully contained.
The two lights may both be inferred accordingly.
O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva bestows medicinal decoctions, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
namely, "May all sentient beings ultimately emerge from all hindrances and entanglements; may all sentient beings forever..."
May they leave behind the body of illness and attain the body of a Tathāgata. May all sentient beings become great medicinal elixirs to eliminate the diseases of all unwholesome states.
May all sentient beings become Agada medicines and abide on the stage of non-retrogression of a bodhisattva.
May all sentient beings become the medicine of the Tathāgata, able to extract the poisonous arrows of all afflictions. May...
May all sentient beings draw near to the noble and holy ones to extinguish their afflictions and cultivate pure conduct.
May all sentient beings become great kings of medicine who forever eradicate all illnesses so that they do not recur.
May all sentient beings become indestructible medicinal trees, capable of healing and saving all living beings. May all sentient beings attain omniscience.

Light issues forth as arrows against all maladies. May all sentient beings skillfully understand the methods of worldly medicine and pharmacology, so that they may provide relief and healing for all diseases.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas bestow medicinal decoctions and drugs, it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to forever leave behind all illnesses, to attain ultimate peace and security, and to attain ultimate purity, just like the Buddha who is free from disease.
Therefore, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way: to uproot all arrows of illness; to attain an inexhaustible and firm body;
to attain a body indestructible by the encircling mountains of diamond; to attain firm and perfect power; to attain the complete and irremovable bliss of the Buddhas;
and to attain the sovereign and firm body of all Buddhas. They dedicate their roots of goodness in this manner.
Fourteenth is the giving of medicinal decoctions. By giving medicine, one obtains the proximate fruit of freedom from illness, as in the case of Bakula;
in the distant future, one obtains a body like that of the King of Medicine Tree, and so forth. Regarding the phrase "not arising again" in the vow, the Sūtra says:
"That which is treated by worldly physicians, though cured, arises again; that which is treated by the Tathāgata never arises again. This refers to mastery.
Regarding the "solid body," Master Daosheng said: "The diamond (*vajra*) constitutes the substance of internal illumination; it is not merely golden.
Therefore, it is called 'sovereign' (*vaśitā*).
O Son of the Buddha! Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are fully capable of bestowing all manner of vessels, namely, vessels of gold."
They were filled with various jewels: silver vessels were filled with many exquisite gems; lapis lazuli vessels were filled with all kinds of treasures;
crystal vessels were filled with immeasurable ornaments of precious adornment; mother-of-pearl vessels were filled with red pearls; agate vessels were filled with coral and mani-jewels;
white jade vessels were filled with various delicious foods; and sandalwood vessels were filled with celestial garments.

He offered garments. He filled adamantine vessels with various exquisite incenses; he filled immeasurable and innumerable vessels of various jewels with immeasurable and innumerable varieties of precious gems.
He gave these either to the Buddhas, out of faith in the inconceivable field of merit that is the Buddha;
or to the Bodhisattvas, knowing that spiritual friends are difficult to encounter; or to the noble Saṅgha, so that the Buddha-Dharma might long abide in the world.
Therefore, one may give to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas because of generating pure faith toward the noble ones; or give to one's parents because of the respect due them;
or give to teachers and elders because they constantly provide guidance and instruction, leading one to cultivate merit in accordance with the holy teachings;
or give to those who are lowly, poor, destitute, and orphaned, regarding all sentient beings with the eyes of great loving-kindness and great compassion.
Therefore, with single-minded intent, they fulfill the *dānapāramitā* of all bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present.
Bestowing all things universally upon all beings, they never grow weary of or abandon sentient beings.
When giving in this manner, they are entirely without attachment to either the objects given or the recipients. By means of such various kinds [of practice], the bodhisattva-mahāsattva...
When giving away various precious vessels filled with immeasurable jewels, one dedicates the roots of goodness in this way:

"May all sentient beings become infinite treasuries like space, equal to it; may their power of mindfulness be vast, such that they are able to receive and uphold all mundane and supramundane scriptures without any forgetfulness. May all sentient beings become..."
Pure vessels, able to realize the profound and correct Dharma of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings become unsurpassed precious vessels, fully able to receive and uphold the Buddha-dharma of the three periods of time.

May all sentient beings achieve the vast Dharma-vessels of the Tathāgatas, embracing the Bodhi-dharma of the Buddhas of the three periods of time with indestructible faith. May all sentient beings become...
Abiding in the vessel of supreme jewel-adornment, one dwells in the bodhicitta of great majestic power.

May all sentient beings become vessels that serve as the basis for the accomplishment of merit, and may they give rise to pure faith and understanding toward the immeasurable wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
May all sentient beings achieve the vessel for entering into all-knowledge, ultimately attaining the unimpeded liberation of the Tathāgata.
May all sentient beings obtain the pure vessel for bodhisattva conduct throughout future kalpas, enabling them to universally establish all beings in the power of all-knowledge.
May all sentient beings achieve the lineage of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
A supreme vessel of merit, capable of receiving and upholding all that is spoken by the wondrous voices of all Buddhas.

May all sentient beings achieve the capacity to contain all world-systems within the entirety of the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, becoming foremost among great men in praising and expounding the teachings.
May they exhort all Buddhas to turn the wheel of the sublime Dharma.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva bestows vessels,
desiring that all sentient beings may universally attain the vessel of the complete and perfect conduct and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Fifteenth, regarding the "vessel for giving," it is called such because both the giver and the receiver are without attachment, thereby fulfilling the pāramitā.
However, a single vessel may give rise to many vows; it is not necessarily the case that one vessel corresponds to only one vow.

Chapter Twenty-five, Part Four: The Ten Dedications.
O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva takes various chariots adorned with manifold jewels and offers them as gifts to the Buddhas,
the Bodhisattvas, teachers, virtuous friends, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and other such immeasurable fields of merit,
even down to those who are poor, destitute, and without shelter. These multitudes of people may come from afar, or they may come from nearby, or...
They have come because they have heard the Bodhisattva’s renown; or they have come due to their karmic connection with the Bodhisattva;
or they have come because they have heard of the vows of giving he made in the past; or they have been invited by the Bodhisattva’s own mental vow.
At that time, the Bodhisattva may give precious chariots or golden chariots, all exquisitely adorned with nets of bells draped over them and jeweled ribbons hanging down. Or...
He bestowed magnificent chariots of lapis lazuli, adorned with immeasurable rare treasures;
or he bestowed silver chariots covered with golden nets and drawn by spirited horses;
or he bestowed chariots decorated with immeasurable varieties of jewels, covered with jeweled nets and drawn by fragrant elephants; or he bestowed sandalwood chariots. Wondrous...
The wheels were made of jewels and the canopies of various precious gems. Jeweled lion thrones were arranged with exquisite adornment, upon which hundreds of thousands of beautiful women sat in rows.
A hundred thousand men drew and guided them as they traveled. Alternatively, he bestowed crystal chariots, magnificently decorated with a multitude of diverse and wonderful jewels;
within them were filled with upright and beautiful women, covered above by jeweled curtains and banners.

Banners attend to his side. Or again, he may be given a car of agate, adorned with various jewels, perfumed with diverse incenses, and decorated with the scattering of many kinds of exquisite flowers.
Hundreds of thousands of beautiful women hold precious necklaces; the carriage is well-balanced and harmonious in its movement, remaining steady even when traversing dangerous terrain.
Or again, he may be given a sturdy fragrant chariot, with wheels made of various jewels, magnificent and grand in its adornment. Jewels...
Canopies covered the top, and jeweled nets hung down. Various precious garments were spread within, and pure, exquisite incense wafted its fragrance outward until it reached afar;
that scent was so sublime and wonderful that it delighted the hearts of men.
Immeasurable devas followed as attendants, carrying various treasures to provide for them at all times, or bestowing upon them radiant jeweled chariots adorned with all manner of exquisite gems.
The colors are translucent, and a net of various exquisite jewels covers its top.
Necklaces of assorted gems hang down all around, and powdered incense is scattered so that both the interior and exterior are fragrant and pure. Beloved sons and daughters are all seated upon it.
O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva offers such magnificent jeweled chariots to the Buddha, by these roots of goodness, thus...
Dedication: That is to say, may all sentient beings fully understand how to make offerings to the supreme field of merit;

may they have deep faith that making offerings to the Buddha yields immeasurable retribution; may all sentient beings direct their single mind toward the Buddha and constantly encounter immeasurable, pure fields of merit;
and may all sentient beings, regarding the Tathāgatas, be free from any sense of stinginess and fully achieve greatness.

The mind of relinquishment: May all sentient beings, in the presence of all Buddhas, practice the giving of material things and abandon the aspirations of the two vehicles, thereby attaining the Tathāgata’s unimpeded liberation and the wisdom of omniscience.
May all sentient beings, in the presence of all Buddhas, perform inexhaustible giving and enter the immeasurable merit and wisdom of the Buddhas. May all sentient beings enter the Buddha...
Supreme Wisdom! May they attain the pure, unsurpassed King of Wisdom.
May all sentient beings obtain the Buddha’s all-pervading, unimpeded supernormal powers, such that wherever they wish to go, they are never without mastery.

May all sentient beings enter deeply into the Mahāyāna, acquire immeasurable wisdom, and abide therein immovably. May all sentient beings be able to give birth to all-encompassing knowledge (*sarvajñatā*).

The Dharma is the supreme field of merit for all devas. May all sentient beings harbor no feelings of resentment toward the Buddhas, diligently planting roots of goodness and joyfully seeking the wisdom of the Buddhas.
May all sentient beings be able to travel spontaneously to all Buddha-fields, pervading the entire Dharma-realm in a single kṣaṇa without weariness. May all sentient beings...

Attaining the sovereign supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) of a bodhisattva, they manifest bodies that pervade all buddha-fields throughout the entirety of space, approaching and making offerings to every Buddha.
May all sentient beings attain an incomparable body, traveling everywhere throughout the ten directions without weariness.
May all sentient beings attain a vast body that flies with great swiftness, reaching wherever they wish without ever failing.

May all sentient beings be free from indolence and regression, and may they attain the ultimate sovereign power of the Buddhas, manifesting within a single kṣaṇa throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space all the supernatural transformations and miraculous powers of the Buddhas. May all sentient beings cultivate the practice of peaceful and blissful conduct.
May they accord with all bodhisattva paths. May all sentient beings swiftly attain the ultimate ten powers, wisdom, and supernormal knowledges.
May all sentient beings universally enter the dharma-realm and the lands of the ten directions, reaching their very limits without distinction.
May all sentient beings practice the conduct of Samantabhadra without ever regressing, until they reach...

Having attained omniscience on the other shore, may all sentient beings ascend the vehicle of incomparable wisdom and, in accordance with the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), perceive reality as it truly is.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva when offering precious chariots to all present Buddhas and to all stūpas and shrines after the Buddhas have passed into extinction. For...
It is to cause sentient beings to attain the Tathāgata’s ultimate liberation through the unimpeded vehicle.
Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives various precious chariots to spiritual friends such as other Bodhisattvas, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, may all sentient beings always remember and uphold the teachings of spiritual friends, and may they diligently and exclusively maintain them.
May they be protected so as not to forget or lose [the teachings]. May all sentient beings share the same purpose and benefit as their spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
May they universally embrace all [beings] and share in their roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*).

May all sentient beings draw near to spiritual friends, honoring and making offerings to them, relinquishing everything they possess to accord with their hearts' wishes. May all sentient beings attain virtuous aspirations and follow after their good companions.
Never having abandoned them, may all sentient beings always encounter spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), single-mindedly serving them and never contravening their instructions.
May all sentient beings delight in spiritual friends and never be separated from them, remaining constant, pure, and free from error.
May all sentient beings be able to offer their very bodies to spiritual friends, following [their guidance].

May their teachings and commands never be disobeyed. May all sentient beings be embraced by spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), cultivate the six kinds of loving-kindness, and remain far removed from all evils.
May all sentient beings follow spiritual friends and hear the true Dharma (*saddharma*) preached by all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings share the same roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*) and purity as their spiritual friends.
The fruit of karma: may I attain the same practice and vows as all bodhisattvas and perfect the ten powers;
may all sentient beings be able to receive and uphold the teachings of spiritual friends, and attain the wisdom, supernormal powers, and the spheres of all samādhis;
may all sentient beings be able to receive and uphold all true dharmas, cultivate all practices, and reach the other shore.
May all sentient beings ride upon the Great Vehicle without any hindrance, ultimately accomplishing the path to omniscience.
May all sentient beings fully attain the vehicle of omniscience and reach the place of peace and security, never to regress.
May all sentient beings know the practice of suchness, and according to all the Buddha-dharmas they have heard, may they [all...]
May they attain ultimate and eternal non-forgetfulness. May all sentient beings be universally sustained by all Buddhas and attain unimpeded wisdom regarding all dharmas.

May all sentient beings attain sovereign supernormal powers that are never lost, reaching wherever they wish to go in a single thought-moment. May all sentient beings travel with sovereign ease and practice extensively.
May they be transformed and guided so that they abide in the Mahāyāna. May the practices of all sentient beings not be in vain;
may they be borne by the vehicle of wisdom to the ultimate stage. May all sentient beings obtain the unimpeded vehicle, reaching all places through unimpeded wisdom.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give various chariots to spiritual friends,
in order to cause sentient beings to become fully endowed with merit, equal and no different from Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Son of the Buddha,
when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give chariots made of various jewels to the Sangha, they give rise to the mind that learns all forms of giving and the mind of excellent understanding through wisdom.

With a mind of pure merit, a mind of compliance with equanimity, a mind that the Jewel of the Sangha is difficult to encounter, a mind of deep faith in the Jewel of the Sangha, and a mind that upholds the true teaching, they dwell in the joy of supreme wisdom and attain what was never before. They establish great assemblies of giving, generating immeasurable and vast merit.
With deep faith that the Buddha’s teachings are indestructible, they dedicate all roots of goodness in this manner. The...
That is to say: may all sentient beings universally enter the Buddha-dharma and remember it without forgetting;

may all sentient beings leave behind the ways of the ordinary and foolish and enter the station of the worthy and noble; may all sentient beings swiftly enter the ranks of the sages and be able to guide and inspire others through the successive stages of the Buddha-dharma;
may all sentient beings be honored and esteemed by the whole world, their words always trusted and relied upon; may all...
May all sentient beings skillfully enter into the equality of all phenomena, thoroughly understanding that the intrinsic nature of the *dharmadhātu* is non-dual.
May all sentient beings be born from the sphere of the Tathāgata’s wisdom and be surrounded by those who are well-disciplined.
May all sentient beings abide in the dharma free from defilement and eliminate all the dust and grime of afflictions. May all sentient beings...
May all beings attain the accomplishment of the unsurpassed Saṅgha-ratna; may they leave behind the stage of ordinary persons and enter the assembly of the noble ones.
May all sentient beings diligently cultivate wholesome dharmas, attain unimpeded wisdom, and be endowed with the meritorious virtues of the sages.
May all sentient beings attain the mind of wisdom and remain unattached to the three periods of time, becoming sovereign like a king among all multitudes. May all sentient beings...

Riding upon the vehicle of wisdom, they turn the wheel of the sublime Dharma. May all sentient beings be fully endowed with supernormal powers, such that in a single thought-moment they can travel to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds.
May all sentient beings ride upon the body of empty space, possessing unimpeded wisdom regarding all worlds. May all sentient beings universally enter into all the dharmadhātus of empty space.

In the assembly of the Buddha, having accomplished the practice of the foremost *pāramitā*, may all sentient beings attain the supreme wisdom of a light and buoyant body, and be able to enter universally into all buddha-fields.
May all sentient beings obtain boundless and skillful *ṛddhipāda* (supernormal powers), manifesting their bodies everywhere in all lands. May all sentient beings attain...
The body of all things has no basis whatsoever; by the power of spiritual penetrations, it manifests universally like a shadow.
May all sentient beings attain inconceivable and sovereign spiritual powers, appearing before those who can be transformed according to their needs to teach, transform, and subdue them.
May all sentient beings attain the unimpeded skillful means of entering the Dharma-realm, traveling throughout the lands of the ten directions in a single thought-moment.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives precious chariots to the Saṃgha.
It is for the purpose of causing all sentient beings to universally mount the pure, unsurpassed vehicle of wisdom and to turn the wheel of unimpeded dharma-wisdom throughout all worlds.
O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives precious chariots as a gift to Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, he gives rise to such thoughts:
namely, the thought of a field of merit; the thought of reverence; the thought of an ocean of merit; the thought capable of producing merit and wisdom;
and the thought born from the power of the Tathāgata’s merits, throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas.
A mind that cultivates practice; a mind capable of practicing the bodhisattva path for unspeakable eons; a mind liberated from all the fetters of Māra;
a mind that crushes and destroys all the hosts of Māra’s armies; and a mind that illuminates the unsurpassed Dharma with the light of wisdom.
With all the roots of goodness from this gift of a chariot, he dedicates them in this way: namely, may all sentient beings be honored by the world...
Faith is the foremost field of merit. May they be fully endowed with the unsurpassed *dāna-pāramitā*.
May all sentient beings be free from useless speech and always delight in dwelling alone with minds free of dualistic thoughts.
May all sentient beings become the most supreme and pure fields of merit, gathering in all beings and causing them to cultivate meritorious deeds. May all sentient beings become deep pools of wisdom.
May they be able to bestow upon sentient beings immeasurable and innumerable fruits of the roots of goodness.
May all sentient beings abide in unimpeded conduct and fulfill the supreme field of merit that is pure.

May all sentient beings abide in the dharma free from contention and realize that all phenomena are without activity, having non-existence as their very nature. May all sentient beings always be able to draw near to the most...
The supreme field of merit. May they fully cultivate and perfect immeasurable merit and virtue.
May all sentient beings be able to manifest immeasurable sovereign supernatural powers, gathering all conscious beings through the pure field of merit.

May all sentient beings be endowed with an inexhaustible field of merit of virtuous qualities, able to bestow upon sentient beings the fruit of the foremost vehicle—the ten powers of a Tathāgata. May all...
May sentient beings become true fields of merit capable of producing fruits, and may they accomplish the inexhaustible mass of merit of omniscience.
May all sentient beings attain the Dharma for the extinction of transgressions, and may they be able to receive and uphold the words and meanings of the Buddha’s teachings never heard before.
May all sentient beings always diligently listen to and receive all Buddha-dharmas, and having heard them, may they all understand and awaken to them without letting them pass in vain.
May all sentient beings hear the Buddha-dharma and attain ultimate penetration; may they expound it in accordance with what they have heard.
May all sentient beings believe, understand, and practice the teachings of the Tathāgata, abandoning all ninety-six kinds of heterodox views of external paths.
May all sentient beings constantly behold the worthy and noble ones, and increase all that is supreme.
Supreme wholesome roots. May all sentient beings’ minds always have faith and delight in those who practice wisdom; may they dwell together with the holy sages and share in their joy.
May all sentient beings never find it in vain to hear the names of the Buddhas, and may they all behold them directly according to what they have heard.
May all sentient beings skillfully discern and understand the true teachings of all Buddhas, and be able to...

May those who protect and uphold the Buddha-dharma be so; may all sentient beings always delight in hearing all the Buddha-dharmas, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, elucidating, and clearly realizing them.
May all sentient beings have faith and understanding in the true merits of the Buddha’s teachings.
Relinquishing all that they possess to offer with reverence and honor—this is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give various chariots to Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.
It is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to fully achieve pure, supreme wisdom and supernormal powers;
to practice with diligence and without indolence; and to obtain the power of all-knowledge and fearlessness.

O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives precious chariots as offerings to various fields of merit, even to those who are poor, destitute, or solitary, he relinquishes everything they may request at any time.
With a heart full of joy and free from weariness, he further addresses those people, saying:
"I should have gone to you myself to provide offerings and support; I ought not to trouble you by coming so far."
When [the visitor] arrived weary and exhausted, he spoke these words, prostrated himself, and inquired after his well-being. Whatever was required was granted in its entirety.
At times, he bestowed upon him a *maṇi* jewel chariot filled with the foremost woman-treasure (*strī-ratna*) of Jambudvīpa;
at other times, he bestowed a gold-adorned chariot filled with a human woman-treasure; or again, he bestowed a sublime...
Lapis lazuli chariots were filled with palace maidens; or he gave various wondrous precious chariots filled with young girls like celestial nymphs;
or he gave countless chariots adorned with jewels, filled with precious women who were gentle, clear-sighted, eloquent, and wise;
or he gave exquisite sandalwood chariots upon which they rode; or again, he gave crystal chariots—altogether.
Jeweled women filled its interior; their countenances were upright and their physical features were peerless. Adorned with exquisite garments, those who beheld them were filled with joy.
At times, he bestowed crystal chariots upon the consecrated crown princes, with the princes themselves seated within.
At other times, he bestowed chariots of solid fragrance, with all the men and women riding therein. Or he bestowed every kind of jewel.

Adorned with carriages and carrying their beloved kin and retinues whom they find difficult to part with—O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva respectfully bestows such immeasurable jeweled carriages as are requested, causing all to fulfill their wishes and be joyful and satisfied.
With these roots of goodness, he dedicates them in this way: namely, "May all sentient beings ride upon the non-retrogressive [vehicle]."
Turning the wheel of non-obstruction, the vehicle of vastness, they proceed beneath the inconceivable Bodhi tree.
May all sentient beings mount the Great Vehicle of the Dharma-wisdom of pure causes, cultivating the bodhisattva practices throughout all future kalpas without ever regressing.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the non-existence of all phenomena, forever departing from all [afflictions].
Though free from conceptual attachment, they constantly cultivate the path to omniscience.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of straightforwardness, free from flattery and deception, and travel to the buddha-fields with sovereign unimpededness.
May all sentient beings accord with and dwell securely in the vehicle of omniscience, finding mutual delight through the teachings of all Buddhas. May all sentient beings...

Riding upon the vehicle of the bodhisattva’s pure conduct, and fully possessing the ten paths of renunciation and the bliss of samādhi, may all sentient beings ride upon the vehicle of the four wheels—namely, dwelling in a favorable land, relying upon virtuous friends, accumulating supreme merit, and making great vows—thereby fulfilling all the pure brahmacarya of a bodhisattva. May they... [one]... wish.
May all sentient beings attain the vehicle of the light that universally illumines the ten directions. May they cultivate and learn the power of wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
May all sentient beings ride upon the vehicle of the Buddha-dharma and reach the ultimate further shore of all dharmas.

May all sentient beings be carried by the inconceivable vehicle of manifold blessings, virtues, and dharmas, universally demonstrating the secure and correct path throughout the ten directions. May one...
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of great giving and abandon the defilement of stinginess.

May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of pure precepts and maintain boundless pure precepts equal to the dharma-realm. May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of patience and always remain free from the turbid mind of anger toward sentient beings.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of great diligence and the vehicle of non-retrogression, and steadfastly cultivate...

May all sentient beings, following the path of supreme conduct toward enlightenment, mount the vehicle of meditative concentration and swiftly reach the site of awakening to realize the wisdom of bodhi.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of wisdom and skillful means, manifesting transformation bodies that fill the entire dharma-realm and the spheres of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the Dharma King and achieve the unconditioned.
Fearless, he constantly and universally bestows the Dharma of omniscience.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of non-attached wisdom, able to enter everywhere throughout the ten directions without wavering from the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*).
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the Buddhas of all times, manifesting births throughout the lands of the ten directions. And...

May they not lose or destroy the Mahāyāna path. May all sentient beings mount the supreme jewel-vehicle of omniscience and fulfill the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva without weariness.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness by a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva when giving various precious chariots to fields of merit, including those who are poor, destitute, and solitary. As for...
It causes sentient beings to possess immeasurable wisdom and to leap with joy, for they ultimately all attain the vehicle of omniscience (sarvajñatā-yāna).

This is the sixteenth [perfection], the gift of vehicles. As for those who come due to past causes and conditions: because there were past affinities such that they ought to receive gifts, the *Yogācārabhūmi* states:
"If there are sentient beings who come seeking various things that lead to worldly amusement or lead to what is meaningless..."
Regarding objects to be given as gifts: there are things that should not be bestowed. Now, to say one gives away a beautiful woman of upright appearance—does this not constitute a contradiction?
Furthermore, regarding the various fields of merit mentioned now, does one bestow gifts upon all of them? It should be understood that within these there are twenty vows:
the first ten establish vows based on the field of merit to which the gift is given, while the latter ten establish vows based on the vehicle to which the gift is given. This concludes the section.
In the text, it mentions all stūpas and temples that exist after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa. A stūpa houses śarīra (relics), while a temple houses images of the Buddha.
"Stūpa" is correctly called *stūpa*; this is translated as "lofty and manifest," and is also called "the place where one returns to the source.

This section on the first type of giving—giving vehicles—is analyzed according to the distinctions of the fields of merit, revealing five types. First is giving to the Buddhas; second is giving to the Bodhisattvas.
Third, making offerings to the Saṃgha; fourth, making offerings to those of the Two Vehicles; fifth, making offerings to all fields of merit. Within these five categories, there are twenty vows each.
Among the first three, the first concerns the field and has ten vows; the second concerns the vehicle and has ten vows;
the third, regarding those of the Two Vehicles, has ten vows for Pratyekabuddhas and ten vows for Śrāvakas. Finally, within the various fields of merit, there are likewise two [sets of ten].
Regarding the ten vows: because there are objects of compassion within various fields of merit, one speaks of prostrating, kneeling, and so forth;
yet, because these are inferior fields, there are also twenty vows, as the fields of giving are not uniform. However, these are merely vows made in a manner similar to those made for a vehicle.
O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away the treasure of an elephant, it is by nature well-trained and possesses its seven limbs in full.
It is in the prime of its youth, with six pure tusks; the color of its mouth is crimson red like a lotus flower, and its body is as brilliant white as a snow mountain.
It is adorned with golden banners and covered with jeweled nets; its trunk is embellished with various kinds of exquisite jewels. Upon seeing it...
They take delight in it without ever feeling weary or satiated. They stride ten thousand *li* without ever growing fatigued.

Or again, they bestow precious horses of excellent breed, endowed with all auspicious marks like celestial steeds, adorned with the light of exquisite jewel-moons, and covered above by nets of pure gold bells;
their gait is level and upright, providing security for the rider as they travel swiftly wherever the mind desires.
Swift as the wind, they traverse the four continents with sovereign ease and without obstruction.

With these precious elephants and precious horses, the Bodhisattva may support their parents and spiritual friends, or provide for impoverished and suffering sentient beings; their mind remains vast and open, giving rise to neither regret nor stinginess.
Instead, their joy and celebration redouble, and their compassion increases further as they cultivate the virtues of a Bodhisattva and purify their awakening.

With this mind, he dedicates these roots of goodness in this way: that is to say, may all sentient beings abide in the vehicle of discipline and submissiveness, and increase all the merits of bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings obtain the skillful vehicle, being able to give rise to all Buddha-dharmas accordingly;
may all sentient beings obtain the vehicle of faith and understanding, universally illuminating the Tathāgata’s...
The power of knowledge regarding hindrances: May all sentient beings attain the vehicle of departure and be able to universally give rise to all great vows.
May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the vehicle of the equal *pāramitās* and bring to fulfillment all roots of goodness that are impartial.
May all sentient beings achieve the jewel-vehicle and give birth to the unsurpassed jewel of wisdom of all Buddha-dharmas. May one...
May all sentient beings accomplish the adornment of the vehicle of bodhisattva conduct and cause the flowers of the various bodhisattva samādhis to bloom.
May all sentient beings attain the boundless and swift vehicle and, throughout incalculable eons, purify their bodhisattva minds, diligently reflecting until they thoroughly comprehend all phenomena.
May all sentient beings accomplish the most supreme and well-tamed Mahāyāna vehicle. By means of this...
Possessing the stage of a bodhisattva through skillful means, they vow that all sentient beings shall achieve the most supreme, vast, and firm Mahāyāna,
capable of universally transporting all beings so that they may all reach the state of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives elephants and horses, in order to cause all sentient beings to mount the vehicle of non-...
It obstructs the vehicle of knowledge, for it brings one to the fulfillment and ultimate attainment of the Buddha-vehicle.
Seventeenth is the gift of elephants and horses; these two matters combined comprise ten vows: first, being well-tamed and compliant by nature;
second, going wherever one intends; third, resembling them in vigorous youth; fourth, like taking strides across ten thousand *li*; fifth, as if traveling...
1. Its stride is level and upright. 2. It is like that precious elephant. 3. It resembles a lotus flower. 4. It is as swift as the wind. 5.

It possesses the stages of a bodhisattva. These are called the "most excellent training. Since both elephants and horses possess the meaning of being "trained," they are distinguished into these two categories.
O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives a seat, he may give a lion-throne upon which he dwells; a seat that is high, vast, extraordinary,
and exquisitely beautiful, with legs made of lapis lazuli, spread with soft garments woven of golden threads,
adorned with jeweled banners, perfumed with various wonderful incenses, and decorated with immeasurable varieties of precious ornaments.
It was magnificently adorned, covered above with a golden lattice, and jeweled bells swayed in the wind, emitting wondrous sounds.

Countless rare treasures were arrayed all around as decoration, and it was gazed upon by all the ministers and subjects. The consecrated Great King alone sat atop it, proclaiming the transformative teachings of the Dharma, which the myriad kingdoms followed and honored.
That king further adorned his body with exquisite jewels, namely the Universal Radiance (*Samantaprabhā*).
Jewels: sapphire, great sapphire, and the *maṇi* jewel of the supreme treasury.
Radiant as the sun and cool as the moon, they are spread all around like the multitude of stars; supremely wonderful and adorned, they are foremost and peerless.
There are the wondrous jewels of the ocean and the firm banners of the ocean, adorned with various marvelous patterns and extraordinary marks, most venerable among the great assembly.
Most excellent! With a crown of Jāmbūnada gold and stainless precious silk upon his head, he received the position of consecration and ruled over Jambudvīpa.
Possessing immeasurable and great majestic power, he subdued all enemies with compassion as his primary guide;
there were none who did not obey his commands and instructions. At that time, the Wheel-Turning King, by means of such hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of immeasurable...

He offers seats adorned with countless jewels to the Tathāgata—the foremost field of merit—as well as to all bodhisattvas, true spiritual friends, the noble Saṅgha, teachers of the Dharma, parents, kinsmen, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and those who have set out upon the bodhisattva vehicle;
or even to the stūpas of the Tathāgata, and so forth, down to all who are poor, destitute, and exposed. According to their [needs]...
Whatever was required, he gave it all away. With these roots of goodness, he dedicated them in this way:
"May all sentient beings sit upon the seat of enlightenment and be able to fully awaken to the true Dharma of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings occupy the seat of mastery, attain mastery over the Dharma, be indestructible by any diamond mountains, and be able to utterly subdue all [adversaries]."
May all sentient beings attain the sovereign lion-throne of the Buddhas, which is gazed upon by all sentient beings.

May all sentient beings attain various exquisite jewel-adorned seats, ineffable beyond expression, and may they exercise mastery over the Dharma to transform and guide sentient beings. May all sentient beings attain the three kinds of worldly... [text truncated]

May all sentient beings obtain seats that are most supreme among the intermediate, adorned by vast roots of goodness, and which pervade unspeakably unspeakable worlds, such that they could not be exhausted even after praising them for incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*).
May all sentient beings obtain seats of great, profound, and secret merit, their bodies filling the entirety of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*). May...
May all sentient beings obtain various inconceivable jewel thrones, and according to their original vows, extensively bestow the gift of Dharma upon those sentient beings they keep in mind.
May all sentient beings obtain excellent and wondrous seats, manifesting the ineffable supernatural powers of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings obtain thrones of every kind of jewel, thrones of every kind of incense, and thrones of every kind of flower.
There are seats of all kinds of garments, seats of all kinds of garlands, seats of all kinds of mani-jewels, and inconceivable seats of various jewels such as lapis lazuli;
seats of immeasurable and ineffable worlds; seats pure with the adornments of all worlds;
and all vajra-seats. These manifest the majestic power and sovereign mastery of the Tathāgata in attaining supreme perfect enlightenment. This is [the first].
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate the roots of goodness from giving precious thrones, it is to cause sentient beings to attain the great Bodhi-throne that transcends the world,
so that they may spontaneously awaken to all Buddha-dharmas.

The eighteenth is the gift of a seat. The meaning of the three types of worlds is explained as usual. Furthermore, Master Bian states that those prior to the stages (bhūmi) are called the world of aspiration and joy;

from the first stage to the seventh stage, they are called the world of effortful application; and from the eighth stage up to Equal Enlightenment (samyaksambodhi), they are called the world of effortless spontaneity.
Some say that according to the traditions of the Western Regions, there are three worlds within the realm of sentient beings.
First, the subterranean world, including the nāgas, asuras, and others; second, the human world; third, the celestial world.
According to the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, these three worlds consist of sentient beings, the five aggregates, and the physical environment.
O Son of the Buddha, when Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas bestow various precious canopies, these canopies are exceptionally rare and noble, adorned with all kinds of great jewels.
Among hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of exquisite canopies, they are the foremost.
Their poles are made of various jewels, covered above by wondrous nets, and draped all around with jeweled cords and golden bells, as well as necklaces of *maṇi* gems.
Adornments were suspended and draped in succession; when stirred by a gentle breeze, they produced exquisite and harmonious sounds.

Jewels, pearls, and precious treasuries filled it in every variety, and immeasurable rare treasures served as its complete embellishment. Sandalwood and aloeswood perfumes wafted everywhere, and Jāmbūnada gold radiated pure brilliance.
Such were the countless hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeyas of wondrous marvels.
Fully adorned with precious objects, they offer them with a pure mind to the Buddhas and to all stūpas and shrines after the Buddhas have passed into extinction;
or for the sake of the Dharma, they give to Bodhisattvas, spiritual friends, and renowned Dharma masters;
or they give to their parents; or they give to the Sangha Jewel; or they further offer all the teachings of the Buddha; or they give to various sentient beings.
As fields of merit: whether giving to teachers, monks, and various venerable elders; or giving to those who have first resolved to attain bodhicitta;
or even to all the poor, the destitute, and the orphaned—to whoever comes seeking, one gives everything. With these roots of goodness, one dedicates them in this way:
namely, may all sentient beings diligently cultivate roots of goodness to cover their bodies, and may they always be...
May the merit and wisdom of all sentient beings serve as a canopy for the protection and shelter provided by the Buddha, so that they may forever be free from all worldly afflictions.
May all sentient beings be covered by wholesome dharmas, thereby eliminating the dust, grime, and feverish distress of the world.
May all sentient beings attain the treasury of wisdom, such that all who behold them find their hearts never weary of gazing upon them.
May all sentient beings shelter themselves with the tranquility of pure dharmas, and may they all attain the ultimate, indestructible Buddha-dharma.
May all sentient beings well-shelter their bodies, ultimately attaining the Tathāgata’s pure Dharma-body.
May all sentient beings become universal canopies, with the wisdom of the Ten Powers pervading the world. May all sentient beings...
One gives birth to wondrous wisdom that transcends the three periods of time and is free from all attachment.
May all sentient beings obtain the parasol of being worthy of offerings, becoming supreme fields of merit that receive all offerings.

May all sentient beings obtain the most excellent parasol, attaining unsurpassed wisdom and spontaneous awakening. These are the roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practices the giving of parasols.
Dedication: In order to cause all sentient beings to attain the canopy of mastery, so that they may uphold all wholesome dharmas;

in order to cause all sentient beings to be able to universally cover all lands within the dharma-realm of empty space with a single canopy, manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas without regression; in order to cause all sentient beings...
Because they are able to adorn all worlds in the ten directions with a single canopy as an offering to the Buddhas;
because they cause all sentient beings to offer exquisite banners, streamers, and various precious canopies to all Tathāgatas;
and because they cause all sentient beings to obtain universally adorned canopies that cover all Buddha-lands without exception.
Therefore, it is to cause all sentient beings to obtain vast canopies that universally cover all beings, so that they may all give rise to faith and understanding toward the Buddha;

to cause all sentient beings to offer unspeakably many wonderful jewel canopies to a single Buddha, and to do likewise before each and every unspeakable number of Buddhas; and to cause all sentient beings to obtain...
The Buddha’s Bodhi-canopy of vast and lofty height universally covers all Tathāgatas.
It is intended to cause all sentient beings to obtain canopies adorned with all kinds of maṇi jewels, canopies adorned with all kinds of precious necklaces,
canopies adorned with all kinds of solid fragrances, canopies adorned with various pure jewels, and canopies of immeasurable pure jewels.
The Adorned Canopy, the Vast Jewel-Pure Adornment Canopy, is covered by a net of jewels with precious bells hanging down,
which, swaying in the wind, produce subtle and wondrous sounds. Because it universally covers the bodies of all Buddhas throughout all worlds in the Dharma-realm and the space-realm,
it serves as a canopy of unobstructed and unhindered wisdom-adornment for all sentient beings, universally covering them all.
Because of all Tathāgatas; furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain supreme wisdom;
furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain the adornment of the Buddha’s merits;

furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to give rise to a pure desire and aspiration for the Buddha’s merits; furthermore, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain the immeasurable and...
Because he possesses the jewel of a mind of sovereign mastery over the limits [of existence]; because he desires to cause all sentient beings to fulfill the sovereign wisdom regarding all dharmas;
because he desires to cause all sentient beings to universally cover all things with their roots of goodness;
because he desires to cause all sentient beings to achieve the canopy of supreme wisdom; and because he desires to cause all sentient beings to become...

Because they wish to universally cover all things with the Ten Powers; because they wish to enable all sentient beings to use a single canopy to completely cover the Dharma-realm and all Buddha-fields;
because they wish to enable all sentient beings to attain mastery over the Dharma and become Kings of Dharma;
because they wish to enable all sentient beings to attain a mind of great majestic power and sovereignty; and because they wish to enable one...
Because they desire that all sentient beings attain vast wisdom that is never interrupted;
because they desire that all sentient beings attain immeasurable merit that universally covers all and reaches ultimate fulfillment;
because they desire that all sentient beings cover their minds with various merits; and because they desire that all sentient beings cover other sentient beings with a mind of equanimity.
Therefore, it is because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain the great wisdom of the equal canopy;
because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to be endowed with the skillful means of great dedication (*pariṇāmanā*);

because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to obtain the pure mind of supreme desire and joy; and because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain the pure intention of virtuous desire and joy.
Therefore, it is also because one desires to cause all sentient beings to attain the Great Dedication (mahā-pariṇāma) that universally covers all sentient beings.

This is the nineteenth gift: the parasol made by weaving grass, followed by parasols of the seven jewels, let alone those adorned with various treasures; how could the karmic reward for this be limited?
O Son of the Buddha! A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva may give various kinds of sublime banners and flags, with poles made of various jewels and streamers made of precious silk.
These banners are composed of various multicolored fabrics, draped over with jeweled nets that fill the space with radiant colors.
Precious bells sway gently, their rhythms harmonizing with one another. Extraordinary and wondrous jewels are shaped like half-moons, and Jāmbūnada gold radiates light.
After a full day had passed, they were all placed atop the banners. Various wonderful objects manifested according to the karmic fruits of the various worlds served as their adornments.
Thus, countless thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of these exquisite banners and flags joined their shadows and linked their splendors, alternating and radiating light.
Their brilliant, pure radiance pervaded the great earth and filled the space of the ten directions and the Dharma-realm.
Throughout all Buddha-fields in the ten directions, Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, with pure minds and resolute faith,
offer such immeasurable banners and pennants to all Buddhas currently residing there, as well as to all stūpas and temples after the Buddhas have passed into parinirvāṇa;
or they offer them to the Jewel of the Dharma, or to the Jewel of the Saṃgha, or to Bodhisattvas and spiritual friends, or to Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.
To Pratyekabuddhas; or to the great assembly, or to individuals—bestowing gifts universally upon all who come seeking them.

With these roots of goodness, he dedicates them in this way: namely, may all sentient beings be able to establish all roots of goodness and banners of merit that cannot be destroyed; may all sentient beings establish mastery over all dharmas.
Banners and streamers: may they be revered, cherished, and diligently protected.
May all sentient beings always transcribe the True Dharma with precious silk and uphold the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. May all sentient beings erect lofty and prominent banners.
May the lamp of wisdom shine universally throughout the world. May all sentient beings establish the banner of firm resolve, so as to utterly destroy all demonic activities.
May all sentient beings erect the banner of the power of wisdom, which no demons can ever destroy.
May all sentient beings attain the Nārāyaṇa banner of great wisdom, thereby crushing and annihilating all worldly [afflictions].
The Banner of Arrogance. May all sentient beings attain the great radiant banner of the sun of wisdom, which universally illumines the dharma-realm with the light of wisdom.
May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the banner of immeasurable jewel adornments, filling all worlds throughout the ten directions to make offerings to all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings attain the banner of the Tathāgata, destroying and extinguishing [all afflictions].
All ninety-six kinds of heterodox views of non-Buddhists constitute the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva offers banners and flags.
This is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to attain the banner of the profound, lofty, and vast conduct of bodhisattvas,
as well as the banner of the supernormal powers of bodhisattvas, so that their path may be purified.
The twentieth is the gift of banners and pennants. These two matters are unified in a single vow.

O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva opens the treasuries of various jewels and bestows hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of exquisite and rare treasures upon countless all sentient beings, giving them according to their wishes with a heart free from stinginess or regret. By means of these...
They dedicate their roots of goodness in this way: that is to say, they vow that all sentient beings shall always behold the Buddha-jewel, abandon ignorance, and practice right mindfulness;
that all sentient beings shall fully attain the radiance of the Dharma-jewel and protect and uphold the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas;
and that all sentient beings shall be able to fully embrace the entire Sangha-jewel. Universally...
May they provide offerings with never-tiring devotion. May all sentient beings attain the supreme jewel-mind of omniscience, purifying their bodhicitta so that it never regresses.
May all sentient beings attain the jewel of wisdom, universally entering into all phenomena with minds free from doubt.
May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the jewels of all bodhisattva virtues, and may they reveal them.
I shall expound immeasurable wisdom. May all sentient beings attain the jewels of immeasurable, wondrous merit and cultivate the ten powers and wisdom of perfect enlightenment.
May all sentient beings attain the jewels of wondrous samādhi and the sixteen kinds of knowledge.
To bring to ultimate fulfillment vast wisdom; to cause all sentient beings to achieve the jewel of the foremost field of merit and to awaken to and enter the unsurpassed wisdom of the Tathāgata;
to cause all sentient beings to become the foremost, unsurpassed King of Jewels, expounding all dharmas with inexhaustible eloquence—this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s giving of various jewels.
At that time, one dedicates the roots of goodness so that all sentient beings may fully attain the precious,
unimpeded, pure eye of the Tathāgata, which is the foremost jewel of wisdom.
Regarding the twenty-first opening of the treasure-store, the sixteen jewels of wisdom, some say they refer to the four wisdoms of the Buddha-ground (*buddhabhūmi*).

Each wisdom has four aspects, thus totaling sixteen. Because they are perfectly integrated through mastery at the stage of fruition, according to Xianshou, these constitute the eight patiences and the eight wisdoms.
O Son of the Buddha, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva may practice giving by means of various exquisite ornaments.
That is to say, he provides all manner of bodily ornaments to make the body pure and sublime, such that nothing is unsuitable. Thus does the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva [give].

He regards all sentient beings in the world as his only child, desiring that they all attain the pure adornment of the body and achieve the supreme worldly peace and happiness, as well as the bliss of the Buddha’s wisdom; he abides securely in the Buddha-dharma to benefit sentient beings.
With such hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of various exquisite and wonderful jewel ornaments, they diligently practice giving.
When practicing giving, they dedicate these roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, may all sentient beings achieve unsurpassed and sublime ornaments, adorning themselves with all pure merits and wisdom.
O Celestial One! May all sentient beings attain the marks of pure adornment, adorning their bodies with pure merit.
May all sentient beings attain the marks of supreme and wondrous adornment, adorning their bodies with the marks of a hundred blessings.
May all sentient beings attain the marks of unconfused adornment, adorning their bodies with all marks. May...
May all sentient beings attain the mark of adornment through pure and excellent speech, being endowed with various kinds of inexhaustible eloquence.
May all sentient beings attain the mark of adornment through the sound of all merits, their voices being pure so that those who hear them rejoice.
May all sentient beings attain the mark of adornment through the delightful speech of all Buddhas, causing all...
May sentient beings, upon hearing the Dharma, joyfully cultivate pure conduct.
May all sentient beings attain the mark of mental adornment, entering profound meditative concentration and universally beholding all Buddhas.

May all sentient beings attain the mark of the adornment of dhāraṇī, illuminating the true Dharma of all Buddhas. May all sentient beings attain the mark of the adornment of wisdom, by means of the Buddha...
Wisdom adorns their minds. This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva bestows all ornaments,
in order to cause sentient beings to be fully endowed with all the immeasurable merits of the Buddha-dharma,
to achieve the perfection of wisdom and adornment, and to forever leave behind all pride and negligence.
The twenty-second is the adornment of giving ornaments. Among the ten vows, the first concerns benefiting others, while the remaining nine concern self-benefit.

O Son of the Buddha! The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva takes the maṇi-jewel crown of the sovereign position of consecration and the jewel from his topknot, bestowing them universally upon all sentient beings without a trace of stinginess. He constantly and diligently practices as a great donor. Thus he cultivates...
They study generosity and wisdom, increasing the faculty of relinquishment and becoming skillful in wisdom. Their minds are vast as they bestow gifts upon all;
they dedicate those roots of goodness in this way: namely, may all sentient beings receive the empowerment of the Buddhas' teachings and attain omniscience;
may all sentient beings be endowed with the uṣṇīṣa and attain the supreme knowledge that reaches [the ultimate].
On the other shore, may all sentient beings universally gather in sentient beings with the jewel of wondrous wisdom, causing them all to reach the ultimate pinnacle of merit.
May all sentient beings achieve the crown-jewel of wisdom, becoming worthy of the world’s veneration and respect.
May all sentient beings adorn their heads with the diadem of wisdom, becoming one...
Sovereign King of all dharmas, may the bright jewel of wisdom be bound upon the crowns of the heads of all sentient beings, such that none in any world can behold it;
may all sentient beings be worthy of receiving the prostrations of the world.
May they achieve the illumination of the Buddha-dharma through the summit of wisdom.
May all sentient beings wear upon their heads the crown adorned with the ten powers, and may they be fully endowed with the purity of the ocean of jewel-like wisdom.

May all sentient beings reach the summit of the great earth and attain the ultimate ten powers of omniscience, destroying the hosts of Māra at the summit of the desire realm. May all sentient beings attain fulfillment.
The first is the Unsurpassed Crown King. Having attained the crown of the light of omniscience, it cannot be eclipsed or surpassed by anything else.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva bestows a precious crown, for the sake of enabling all sentient beings to obtain the crown of the exquisite maṇi-jewel of wisdom—the foremost knowledge and the most pure state.
The twenty-third [chapter] concerns the bestowing of the jeweled crown and the topknot jewel; these two matters are treated as one. Regarding the phrase "the bright pearl of wisdom" and so forth:
its substance is perfect and its virtues complete; it reflects all clearly and eliminates delusion, thus it is the "bright pearl of wisdom.

As it is the object of veneration for the ultimate fruit, it is called the "summit. It is secret and wondrous, such that none can see it; furthermore, because the provisional conceals the real, it is said to reside in the topknot.

In the middle [section], the provisional is opened to reveal the real; thus it is called "Untying the Topknot. Although the text does not explicitly contain the meaning of "untie," it is included here for the sake of convenience.

"O Son of the Buddha! When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees sentient beings dwelling in a dark prison, their bodies bound by shackles, manacles, and neck-irons, unable to rest in sitting or rising as various sufferings converge upon them, and having no relatives or acquaintances..."
They have no refuge; they are naked, emaciated by hunger, and their agonizing suffering is unbearable.

Upon seeing them, the Bodhisattva relinquishes all his wealth, treasures, wife, children, kinsmen, and even his own body to rescue those sentient beings from prison—just as the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika and the Bodhisattva King Subhavyūha did.
Having delivered them, he provides for them everything they require according to their needs.
He bestows gifts to eliminate their suffering and distress and bring them peace and security;

thereafter, he bestows the unsurpassed treasure of the Dharma, causing them to abandon negligence and abide in wholesome roots, so that their minds never regress from the Buddha's teaching. O Son of the Buddha, such is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
When rescuing sentient beings from within prisons, one dedicates all roots of goodness in this way:
namely, may all sentient beings ultimately be liberated from the fetters of craving; may all sentient beings sever the flow of birth and death and ascend to the shore of wisdom;
may all sentient beings eliminate ignorance and folly and cultivate wisdom; [may they be] liberated from...
May all beings bound by the fetters of every affliction extinguish their bonds within the three realms and attain ultimate liberation through omniscience.
May all sentient beings forever sever all knots and fetters of affliction and reach the further shore of wisdom—the ground free from affliction and obstruction.
May all sentient beings be free from all stirring thoughts, deliberations, and conceptual discriminations.

May they enter the stage of the impartial and immovable wisdom. May all sentient beings be liberated from the bonds of desire, forever depart from all worldly greed and lust, and remain unstained by attachment within the three realms.
May all sentient beings attain superior aspiration and joy, constantly receiving the Dharma gates taught by all Buddhas. May all sentient beings attain non-attachment and non-bondage.
The mind of liberation is as vast as the Dharma-realm and as ultimate as space.
May all sentient beings attain the supernatural powers of Bodhisattvas, taming sentient beings in all worlds, causing them to leave the mundane world behind and abide in the Mahāyāna.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva rescues sentient beings suffering in prison. In order to...
Because sentient beings universally enter the ground of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.
Twenty-fourth: giving one's wife and children to rescue those imprisoned. All that precedes clarifies external giving;
the following two sections clarify the gift of fearlessness (*abhaya-dāna*). The first of these involves both internal and external wealth, as the internal wealth is more difficult to give.

O Son of the Buddha, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva sees a prisoner bound at five points, undergoing all manner of agonizing suffering, being guarded and driven toward the place of execution where his life is about to be severed;
when he has abandoned all the pleasures of Jambudvīpa and must bid eternal farewell to his kinsmen and friends;
and when he is placed upon a high block to be butchered with knives, or impaled upon a wooden stake—
Their bodies were pierced; they were wrapped in cloth, drenched in oil, and consumed by fire.

When the Bodhisattva saw such various forms of suffering and oppression, he sacrificed his own body to undergo them in their stead—just as the Bodhisattva Ajita, the Bodhisattva Viśeṣacāritra-rāja, and countless other great Bodhisattvas did for the sake of sentient beings, sacrificing their own lives to receive [the suffering] on their behalf.
Regarding all such bitter poisons, the Bodhisattva then said to the master: "I vow to give up my own body to take his life in its place.
You may inflict such sufferings upon me as you wish;
even if they exceed that person's suffering by incalculable times, I shall endure them so as to bring about his liberation. If I were to see him being led to execution..."
To sacrifice one’s own body and life to redeem the suffering [of others] is not what is called abiding in the bodhisattva mind.
Why is this? It is because I have generated the bodhicitta of omniscience for the sake of protecting and rescuing all sentient beings.
Son of the Buddha, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva sacrifices his own body and life to save sentient beings, he dedicates his roots of goodness in this way: namely, the vow—
May all sentient beings attain an ultimate body and life that is never severed or exhausted, and may they forever be free from all calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions.
May all sentient beings dwell in reliance upon the Buddhas and receive the prophecy of enlightenment endowed with the ten powers of omniscience.
May all sentient beings universally rescue all conscious beings, causing them to be without fear and to forever emerge from the evil realms. May all...
May all sentient beings attain all life and enter the realm of deathless wisdom.
May all sentient beings forever be free from enemies and adversaries, be devoid of all calamities and hardships, and always be sustained by the Buddhas as their virtuous friends.
May all sentient beings abandon all swords, blades, weapons, and instruments of evil suffering, and practice various kinds of pure goodness.
Karma. May all sentient beings be free from all fears. Having subdued the armies of Māra beneath the Bodhi tree, may all sentient beings be free from the fear of great assemblies;
with pure minds regarding the unsurpassed Dharma, may they be fearless and able to let out the supreme lion’s roar.
May all sentient beings attain the unobstructed wisdom of a lion and, within all worlds...
One practices right action with the vow that all sentient beings may reach the state of fearlessness, constantly mindful of rescuing and protecting those suffering from all miseries.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva sacrifices their own body and life to save prisoners facing execution,
in order to cause sentient beings to leave behind the suffering of birth and death and attain the supreme, wondrous bliss of the Tathāgata.
Twenty-fifth: Sacrificing One’s Body to Die in Another’s Place—This Is Exclusively an Inner Resource.
*The Compendium of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Fascicle Twenty-six;
*The Compendium of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Fascicle Twenty-seven.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Śikṣānanda of Khotan;
commentary on the meaning by the Śramaṇa Chengguan of Qingliangshan Dàhuá yán Temple;
and edited and summarized by the Śramaṇa Hanshan Deqing of Fǎyún Temple on Kuāng Mountain in the Ming Dynasty.
Chapter Twenty-Five, Part Five: The Ten Dedications. O Sons of the Buddha!

There are Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who give even their skin and topknots to beggars, such as the Bodhisattva Ratnaśikhin, the Bodhisattva Varabhadra, and countless other Bodhisattvas. At that time, these Bodhisattvas see the beggar...
When he arrived, [the Bodhisattva] felt joy arise in his heart and spoke to him, saying: "If you now require my topknot together with its skin, you may take it from me.
This topknot of mine is the foremost in all of Jambudvīpa. While speaking these words, his mind was unmoved and undisturbed;
he did not think of other activities, but renounced the world, aspiring for tranquility, seeking ultimate purity, and applied himself with diligence.
With a straightforward mind directed toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), he took a sharp blade and cut off his topknot together with the skin from his head.
Placing his right knee on the ground and joining his palms, he offered it with single-minded devotion.

Maintaining right mindfulness of the practices of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time, he gave rise to great joy and an exalted aspiration. Within all phenomena, his mind was well-liberated and free from grasping.
Regarding suffering, one thoroughly understands that painful sensations are signless and unarisen, and that all sensations arise in mutual succession without any permanence.

Therefore, I should practice great equanimity (mahopekṣā) just as all bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present do; I shall give rise to deep faith and joy, seeking omniscience (sarvajñatā) without ever regressing.
By the power of spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), rather than through the instruction of others, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva acts...
At the time of giving, one should dedicate all roots of goodness in this way:
namely, may all sentient beings attain the invisible crown of the head and achieve the *uṣṇīṣa* of a bodhisattva, which is like a stūpa;
may all sentient beings attain hair that is deep blue-black, adamantine, and fine and soft, capable of extinguishing all the afflictions of sentient beings; may all sentient beings attain moist...
May their hair be glossy and dense, never encroaching upon the temples or the forehead. May all sentient beings obtain hair that is soft and supple, growing fully across the temples and forehead.
May all sentient beings obtain hair marked with the *svastika* and hair with right-turning curls like a conch shell.
May all sentient beings obtain the hair of a Buddha’s marks, forever free from all afflictions, fetters, and habitual tendencies. May they...
May all sentient beings obtain hair that emits light, the radiance of which universally illumines the worlds of the ten directions.
May all sentient beings obtain hair free from disorder, pure, wondrous, and untainted, just like the hair of the Tathāgata.

May all sentient beings obtain hair worthy of being enshrined as a stūpa upon the crown of the head, such that all who see it shall feel as if they were beholding the hair of a Buddha. May all sentient beings attain...
The Tathāgata has hair free from defilement, forever detached from all darkness, obscurations, dust, and impurities.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives away his topknot together with the skin,
in order to cause sentient beings to attain tranquility of mind and to fully realize all dhāraṇīs and the ultimate ten powers of the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes.
